podobne: Chlorophyllum rhacodes – occurs rather in parks, its cap is lighter, and the scales on it are not so distinctly overlapping like roof tiles.
The colour of its discolourations is more red-orange, whereas the discolourations of Ch. olivieri are more yellow-orange.
Macrolepiota procera is much larger, its stem is covered with a striped, darker pattern, and the scales on the cap are darker, do not cover the whole surface and are not so spreading.
Macrolepiota procera is also characterised by a specific, pleasant smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 8–15 cm, spherical in young fruit bodies, parasol-shaped in older ones.
The skin is grey-brown or brown and covered with fibrous, whorled, brownish, darker and clearly protruding scales.
spod: White, sometimes with drops of liquid on them, which turn olive green after drying.
They turn red under pressure.
trzon: Height up to 15 cm, thickness 1–1.5 cm.
At the base it widens into a bulb shape; almost smooth, at first white, with time becoming more brown, with no trace of banding.
Under the cap a white ring, which can be moved along the stem.
When damaged it turns reddish.
miazsz: Whitish, changing colour to orange-ochre after damage.
Mild in taste, without smell.
podobne: Leucoagaricus nympharum, with a more slender and delicate fruit body covered with white small scales.
It also differs in its flesh, which is white and changes colour only slightly when damaged (turns slightly red).
Macrolepiota procera, whose stem is covered with a zigzag pattern, and whose flesh does not change colour when damaged; moreover, the scales on the cap are not so spreading.

Macrolepiota konradii, with smaller fruit bodies, its cap is not shaggy in the centre, the scales are adpressed, and the surface of the stem is light brown and covered with small scales; moreover the flesh in the stem at first turns pink, later brown, but slowly.
Chlorophyllum molybdites, a strongly poisonous species, has not so far occurred in Poland, but is beginning to spread in Europe.

It can very often be confused with other fungi of the genus Chlorophyllum, e.g. Chlorophyllum brunneum (formerly the garden or Czech variety of the shaggy parasol), Chlorophyllum olivieri and Chlorophyllum venenatum, of which the first and the last are poisonous fungi.

owocnik: Width 1–3 cm, spread out or spread out with bent-back margins.
Attached to the substrate sideways, often part of the fruit body stands away from the substrate.
It often occurs in clusters, and then the fruit bodies overlap like roof tiles.
Surface felty, from whitish to grey in colour.
Hymenophore smooth, waxy, zoned, in various shades of violet, purple and brown.
miazsz: Flexible, without smell.
It is layered and darkest just under the upper surface, palest in the middle.
podobne: Auricularia mesenterica.
It differs in the colour of the underside (it is dark brown), is rubbery, elastic and always forms a cap.
Veluticeps abietina also has a violet fruit body, but is harder, darker, much rarer (occurring here and there in the Carpathians, the Sudetes and on the Krakow-Czestochowa Upland).

kapelusz: Diameter 4–15 cm.
In youth convex with a rolled-under margin, copper-brown, later somewhat faded; old flattened; when wet – strongly slimy, when dry – smooth and shiny; very thick and fleshy.
Young fruit bodies are surrounded by a cobweb-like veil.
spod: First coppery-grey, dark purple-brown after maturing; very thick and distant; often forked and running far down the stem.
trzon: Long and slender, fleshy, copper-orange to yellow-brownish, with a delicate, zigzag pattern from the ochre veil, in the dry state sometimes with a thickened annular zone.
miazsz: Orange-yellow, after pressing, after some time stained carmine.
In the stem base chrome yellow; without smell and with a mild taste.
wysyp: Spores elongated, ellipsoid-spindle-shaped, smooth, brown-yellow, measuring 17–23 × 5.5–7 µm.
podobne: Chroogomphus helveticus, which has a felty cap.
Edible.

owocnik: At first egg-shaped, conical or pear-shaped, surrounded by a covering.
This is the so-called egg.
It is 3.5–6 cm high, 2.5–5 cm in diameter, white-grey in colour and partly sunk into the substrate.
During its development the covering in the upper part of the egg bursts and a banana-shaped receptacle pushes out.
The receptacle reaches a height of 5–15 cm and splits into 4-6 red arms on reaching maturity.
In this form it resembles an octopus.
These arms gradually bend outwards, so that the receptacle takes the shape of a starfish.
Its lower part, 2–9 cm high and 2–5 cm wide, remains unbroken, is whitish or white-grey and porous.
The outer surface of the arms is coral-red and has a net-like, pitted structure.
The inner layer is intensely red-cherry and on it there is a slimy layer of gleba with spores.
This layer gives off an unpleasant smell of carrion similar to that of Phallus impudicus.
During ageing the gleba dries up and turns black.
On a cross-section through the arm 2-3 tubes and two broad depressions called globifers are visible.
Clavarioid fungi with basidiocarps forming small clusters.
A single one has the form of a club-shaped rod up to 15 cm high and 2–12 mm thick, usually straight, sometimes bent like a worm.
Surface smooth or irregularly striate, usually matt, lemon-yellow, sometimes with a grey or olive tinge.
Flesh whitish, brittle and without a distinct smell or taste.
podobne: Clavaria argillacea is most easily distinguished from other club fungi by its yellowish colour and its occurrence in the company of heath plants.
Microscopically it is distinguished by relatively large and cylindrical spores.

owocnik: Height 3–6(10) cm, bushily branched.
Branches more or less grey to violet-grey, somewhat wrinkled.
Tips paler, bluntly ended or toothed, but not flattened or crested.
Base set off in whitish-yellowish.
wysyp: Spores spherical or elliptical, measuring 6–11 × 6–10 μm.
podobne: The grey coral can easily be confused with grey-coloured varieties of Clavulina cristata or with grey forms of the more club-like Clavulina rugosa.

inne: Morphology:
Young fruit bodies are pure white, later cream, finally greyish, sometimes flesh-coloured.
They reach up to 8 cm in height and 2–4 cm in width.
As in other species of the family, the fruit body is branched like a tree.
The ends of the branches are finely toothed, often darkening in dry weather.
Flesh whitish, brittle, without a distinct smell, mild in taste (sometimes slightly bitterish).
Microscopic features:
Spore print white.
Spores almost spherical, smooth, measuring 7–11 × 6.5–10 μm.
Basidia 5–7 μm long with two curved sterigmata.
Chemical composition:

Besides the typical fatty acids: palmitic, oleic and linoleic, this coral fungus (Polish name: gozdzienczyk grzebieniasty) contains two unusual compounds: cis-9, cis-14-octadecadien-12-oic acid, and conjugated cis-9, trans-11, trans-13, cis-15-octadecatetraenoic acid.
This coral fungus (Polish name: gozdzienczyk grzebieniasty) is the only known fungus species that contains this last compound.
podobne: Similar species of the genus Clavulina are Clavulina rugosa and Clavulina cinerea.
Ramaria pallida is larger and has parallel-growing branches.

owocnik: Height 4–9 cm, thickness 0.5–1 cm.
At first it is club-shaped, slightly twisted, wrinkled and longitudinally furrowed.
It usually grows in clusters of several fruit bodies crowded close together.
Later they divide in a forked way into several branches ending in rounded and blunt tips, sometimes with teeth.
The colour of the fruit bodies is from whitish through dirty white, ochre to greyish; sometimes young specimens have a violet bloom.
The fruit bodies are characterised by great variability of shape and colour.
miazsz: Whitish, soft, springy, brittle.
Taste and smell faint.
podobne: Clavulina cinerea; it is more (repeatedly) branched and has a smoky-violet colour,
Thelephora palmata; it has brown, bushy-branched fruit bodies with white tips and smells unpleasant.

kapelusz: Width 5–15 cm, thickness 1–3 cm.
It is bulbous in young specimens, later fan-shaped.
At first it is yellow, then whitish-cream.
The edge of the fruit body is usually darker (yellow) and smooth, at first inrolled, later straight.
The upper surface is scaly-felty and furrowed.
It is attached to the substrate sideways or by the base resembling a stem somewhat.
Sometimes neighbouring fruit bodies fuse with one another.
spod: 2–6 mm long and in colour from white to ochre.
Pores angular, 1–3 mm in diameter.
The tubes form only a single layer.
In older specimens the pores become maze-like.
miazsz: It is whitish, elastic, thin, soft and has a fairly pleasant smell.
It forms two layers.
The upper layer, 1–4 mm thick, is softer, the lower one harder.
After drying the flesh becomes hard and brittle.
Taste indistinct, slightly bitter or sourish.
podobne: Postia stiptica, with a white or pinkish fruit body.
It has a very bitter taste and has no yellow edge.
Sarcodontia spumea.
It has no labyrinthine pores and grows mainly on deciduous trees.
Microscopically the northern sponge bracket shows a surprisingly great similarity to Climacodon septentrionalis, as Stanislaw already noticed.
Domanski.
Both of these species, grown on artificial substrates, produce chlamydospores and have a similar hyphal structure and cystidia structure.
Morphologically, however, the northern spongy bracket differs in its tubular hymenophore; moreover, its caps grow separately, not forming such a compact structure as in the northern tooth fungus.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–15 cm, at first convex, later low-arched, finally flat or bent over.
It usually has a broad and blunt umbo, the margins stay rolled under for a long time.
It is not hygrophanous, fleshy and entirely white-frosted.
Colour from white-grey through grey to ash-grey with a brownish tinge.
Cap margin paler.
spod: Low, thin, crowded and decurrent on the stem.
At first they are white, then ochre-cream, and in older specimens brown spots appear on them.
trzon: Height 6–12 cm, thickness up to 3 cm, fibrous on the outside.
Club-shaped and solid in young specimens, later cylindrical and cottony or hollow.
At the base it always remains thickened.
Colour white to pale grey.
miazsz: White, hard, fleshy, does not change colour when cut.
Taste and smell very variable.
Sometimes it smells like freshly ground flour, at other times unpleasant.
Most people consider the smell unpleasant.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid, smooth, colourless, 6–7 × 3 µm in diameter.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–10 cm, at first convex, later flat, finally with a depression, but never funnel-shaped.
Margin bent, remaining inrolled for a long time.
Surface shiny, smooth, whitish or cream.
It is hygrophanous; in wet weather it turns grey-yellow or whitish-brownish, darkest at the margin.
Older fruit bodies have concentrically arranged grooves.
spod: Crowded, slightly decurrent, first white, later dirty whitish.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness 0.6–1.1 cm, cylindrical, sometimes twisted, springy, solid in young fruit bodies, hollow or cottony in older ones.
Surface white or dirty ochre.
White mycelial hyphae at the base of the stem are characteristic.
miazsz: White, watery grey-brownish when moist.
Smell aromatic, sometimes musty or mealy.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid, smooth, colourless, measuring 4–5 × 3–4 µm.
podobne: There are many whitish funnel caps and other similar mushroom species.
They are difficult to distinguish.
Leucocybe candicans – is smaller, and does not smell of aniseed
Clitocybe rivulosa – has a mealy taste, more decurrent gills and characteristic patches on the cap.
Leucocybe connata – has a mealy smell and grows in clusters along forest tracks.
It has very crowded gills
Clitopilus prunulus.
Its gills run far down the stem and turn pink with age.
The flesh has a strongly mealy smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 9–33 mm, convex with a wavy margin.
Surface smooth, slightly dusted, cream-ochre.
spod: Adnate to slightly decurrent, white to cream-ochre when mature.
trzon: Height 18–31 mm, thickness 2–15 mm, cylindrical.
Surface smooth, whitish to ochre at maturity, with whitish remains of mycelium at the base.
miazsz: With a light, mushroomy smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–10 cm, semicircular when young, later arched with a sunken centre, finally becoming funnel-shaped.
Margins always rolled under.
Skin white or whitish-grey, when dry bare and matt, after rain slightly slimy.
spod: Gilled, gills at first white, later pinkish, crowded, low and of unequal length, fairly deeply decurrent on the stem.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness 8–18 mm, cylindrical, solid.
Sometimes it grows eccentrically (that is, not in the centre of the cap).
It is fibrously grooved, frosted, and narrowed at the bottom.
Colour white.
miazsz: White, soft and flexible, not changing colour when cut.
Taste slight, smell resembles freshly ground flour.
podobne: It is often confused with Lyophyllum connatum.
It can also be confused with the poisonous Clitocybe phyllophila or with the equally poisonous Entoloma sinuatum.
It is distinguished from them by strongly decurrent gills of a pinkish tinge and a characteristic smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–14 cm, long-arched with an inrolled margin when young, later becoming slightly convex or flat.
Skin bare, smooth, not absorbing water.
In a young fruit body the cap is bright violet, later pink-violet, in a mature one brown-violet or reddish-brown, in old age it becomes ochre.
spod: When young very violet, then brown-ochre, crowded, thin, notched with a tooth.
trzon: Height 5–10 cm, thickness 1–3 cm, cylindrical, solid, slightly fibrillose-woolly on top, usually club-shaped thickened at the base and violet-felty.
Surface at first bright violet, later grey-violet.
miazsz: Fleshy, hard and violet when young, soft and cream in the mature fruit body.
Taste slight, pleasant; smell characteristically, pleasantly spicy, rarely without smell.
wysyp: White with a slight pink tinge.
Spores 6–8 × 4–5 µm in diameter, broadly ellipsoid, slightly warty, colourless.
podobne: Because of its violet colouring this violet species is easily distinguished from other fungi.
Collybia sordida is similar, but it is much smaller than it.
Laypeople may confuse it with the inedible Cortinarius traganus, which has yellow, bitter and foul-smelling flesh and a rusty-brown cortina (or its remnants).
It can also be confused with Cortinarius violaceus.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–10 cm.
At first convex, later spread out with a blunt umbo, finally flat with a funnel-shaped depression.
In young specimens it has a rolled-under margin, later wavily bent.
Skin bare, dry, with a very characteristic blue-green colouring.
In older specimens it turns white.
spod: Fairly distant, slightly decurrent on the stem.
They are coloured from cream to blue-green.
trzon: Height 3–5 cm, thickness 1 cm.
It is cylindrical, with an often thickened base.
The same colour as the cap.
miazsz: White, only greenish under the cap skin.
It has a strong aniseed smell and taste.
podobne: Thanks to its very characteristic colour and smell, this species basically cannot be confused with any other.
Somewhat similar morphologically is Stropharia aeruginosa, but it does not have an aniseed smell.

kapelusz: Diameter up to 15 cm, hemispherical in a young fruit body, later convex, finally flat.
It is thick-fleshed, smooth, bare and glossy.
Colour pale cream, fawn, sometimes with a brown tinge.
spod: Whitish when young, then pale cream, pale ochre in the mature fruit body, crowded, thin, sinuate, notched with a tooth.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness 1.5–3.5 cm.
It is cylindrical, thickened at the bottom, solid, with longitudinal violet fibres on a beige background (it looks as if it were entirely violet).
miazsz: Thick-fleshed, hard, whitish or pale cream, sometimes slightly violet under the surface of the stem, does not change colour when cut.
Taste insignificant, pleasant, smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spores 7–8 × 4–5 µm in diameter, ellipsoid, slightly warty, colourless.
podobne: Collybia nuda.
It is violet not only in the stem, but also in the gills and the cap,
Collybia sordida, which is similar in shape and colour but much smaller (the cap is up to 6 cm in diameter),
Clitocybe nebularis.
It has a greyish stem, pale cream gills and is whitish-mossy.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–7 cm, arched when young, later spread out with a convex umbo, finally concave.
Margin thin, wavy.
It is hygrophanous; in wet weather it becomes shiny but not slippery, in dry weather matt.
Surface coloured from whitish-pinkish to brownish or flesh-red.
spod: Crowded, arched-attached or slightly notched at the stem.
They are coloured from light pink-violet to dirty brown.
trzon: Height 3–6 cm, thickness 4–8 cm, cylindrical, solid, springy, sometimes eccentric.
Surface fibrous, in young fruit bodies light grey-pinkish-violet, in older ones pale dirty brown.
miazsz: Watery, thin, coloured from whitish to grey-pink-violet, almost white after drying.
No smell, taste somewhat earthy, very faint.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid, covered with fine spines.
podobne: Collybia nuda is similar, but is much larger and more violet.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–4 cm.
In young fruit bodies hemispherical or bluntly bell-shaped, later it becomes flattened with a broad and blunt umbo, finally flattened with a turned-up margin.
Surface smooth, bare.
It is hygrophanous; when dry the surface is matt and pale cream in colour, when moist it is shiny, in colour from light flesh-brown to meat-brown.
The fruit bodies almost always grow in clusters, sometimes together with other species.
spod: Gills narrow and crowded, at first white, later flesh-ochre to flesh-brown.
Edges of the gills hairy.
The gills are free at the stem.
trzon: Height 5–12 cm, thickness up to 0.5 cm.
It is cylindrical, thin and slender, flexible, tubular.
Colour the same as the cap.
After the cap is detached, a small disc remains on the stem, and a round hole in the cap.
A characteristic feature of this species is that the whole surface of the stem is covered with white warts (hairs), and that the stems of the fruit bodies in one clump are fused at the base.
miazsz: Thin and bast-like, whitish.
It does not change colour after damage.
Taste mild, smell weak and indefinite.
wysyp: Spores elongated, smooth, 7–10 × 2–3 µm in diameter.
podobne: There are many similar species of fungi, but the clustered toughshank has several characteristic features by which it can be easily distinguished: it grows in clumps, and the thin stems of the individual fruit bodies are fused at the bases and covered with white warty "hairs".
It has crowded gills, and the stem detaches from the cap together with a small disc.
Gymnopus peronatus is the most similar.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–6 cm, at first flat-convex, but quickly with a depressed centre.
Surface dry and smooth, yellowish-reddish-brown, becoming paler while drying and turning ochre.
It is delicately and darkly radially striate, wrinkled in older specimens.
spod: Fairly distant, notched with a tooth or narrowly attached.
Sometimes they are veined near the stem.
In young fruit bodies they are coloured from pale yellow to yellow, in older ones they are the colour of the cap.
Edges lighter.
trzon: Height 4–7 cm, thickness about 0.5 cm.
It is hard, tough-fibrous and bent.
Surface finely hairy, in the lower part abundantly covered with white or yellowish, bristly mycelium.
miazsz: Whitish in young specimens, light brown in older ones.
Taste acrid, burning, smell weak and indefinite.
wysyp: White. Spores ellipsoid, smooth, measuring 6–8 × 3–4 μm.
podobne: Rhodocollybia butyracea.
It has a greasy, shiny cap of a dark red colour
Gymnopus dryophilus.
It has an orange-brown cap and a smooth stem.
Gymnopus hariolorum.
It has crowded gills, an unpleasant smell of rotting cabbage and a taste similar to radish.

The species called lysostopek cierpki in Polish is characterised by great variability of cap colour, but it can easily be told apart from similar species by two features: mycelium on the lower part of the stem and an acrid, burning taste.
It is also distinguished from other Gymnopus species by the fact that in old age its gills change colour to ochre, like the cap.

kapelusz: Diameter up to 10 cm, funnel-shaped and very thin.
Colour from yellowish brown to grey-brown, surface velvety, clearly zoned, the growth zone at the cap margin paler, margin wavy.
trzon: Height 2–7 cm, thickness 0.5–1 cm, centrally attached, cylindrical.
Surface velvety, rusty yellow.
spod: Tubes slightly decurrent on the stem.
They are up to 2 mm long and hairless.
Pores 2–4 mm in diameter, whitish on young fruit bodies, on older ones in colour from yellow-brown to grey-brown.
miazsz: Elastic, corky, very thin.
Colour whitish, smell imperceptible.
podobne: Coltricia cinnamomea – has a smaller cap (up to 5 cm), weakly zoned, and is very rare in Poland.
the so-called Onnia tomentosa – has an unzoned, felty cap, and has bristles inside the tubes.
The so-called Onnia circinata – has a sessile cap, or on a very short and thick stem, sometimes lateral.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–2 cm, at first thimble-shaped, later bell-shaped, never becoming flat.
Margins grooved to about half of the radius.
In older fruit bodies the margin sometimes turns outward.
Surface smooth, in colour from white to ivory, slightly greasy on young fruit bodies.
spod: Crowded, narrow, attached or almost free.
At first whitish, later darker and darker; rusty yellowish, cinnamon, brownish pink, finally brown.
trzon: Height 3–11 cm, thickness up to 2 mm.
It is unevenly cylindrical, gradually thicker towards the base, hollow inside.
Surface smooth, glassy-white, somewhat longitudinally grooved.
Ring absent.
miazsz: Thin and brittle, without a distinct smell or taste.
wysyp: Spores elliptical, smooth, with a germ pore.
podobne: Conocybe siliginea, whose fruit bodies change colour with age from pale to ochre.
Agrocybe pediades, which has a yellow-brown cap and brown gills.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–3 cm, rarely up to 4 cm, shape conical to bell-shaped, margin of older specimens striate.
Surface smooth, coloured from light ochre through brown to dark brown, never golden yellow as in Bolbitius species.
spod: Light brownish, ochre.
Besides the main gills there are intermediate lamellae.
trzon: Brown-brownish, pale ochre, stiff, finely dusted, without a ring.
miazsz: Light brown, brittle.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–3 cm, height 1–3 cm, at first thimble-shaped, then convex.
It is hygrophanous; in wet weather it is coloured from rusty to rusty-brown and is distinctly grooved, in dry weather it is clay to yellow-brown and the grooving is faintly visible.
spod: Fairly close, ventricose.
At first they are very pale ochre, later from the spores they become cinnamon or rusty.
In mature fruit bodies the edges of the gills are distinctly paler than the surface.
trzon: Slender and thin.
It is 5–9 cm tall and 4–7 mm thick, without a ring.
Beneath the cap it is yellow-white, darker towards the bottom; brown-orange or rusty-brown.
The whole surface frosted.
miazsz: Pale yellow-brownish, without a distinct smell or taste.
podobne: Conocybe apala.
It is much paler, has a more elongated and conical cap and appears on lawns soon after rain.
An egg-shaped conecap (a Conocybe species) is also similar; sometimes these species are impossible to tell apart.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–1.5 cm, in young fruit bodies cream, pale ochre, grey-yellow, beige or ochre-yellowish in colour, bell-shaped or thimble-shaped.
In mature fruit bodies grey in various shades, broadly bell-shaped.
Unlike some species of Coprinus, it does not deliquesce.
The cap surface is finely folded radially, dry and dull.
spod: Gilled, with widely spaced gills (according to some sources they are crowded), straight adnate to the stem.
The colour of the gills is at first white, then in grey-violet or ochre shades, in older fruit bodies dark, almost black.
Under a magnifying glass, tiny hairs can be seen on the cap (viewing against the light).
trzon: Length 4–5 cm, diameter about 0.1 cm, whitish, slightly hygrophanous, cylindrical, often bent.
miazsz: Whitish in colour, very thin, with a mild taste and a slightly mushroomy smell.
wysyp: Spores measure about 8-9 × 6-8 µm, ellipsoid, smooth.
podobne: Psathyrella pygmaea – has no hairs on the cap.

kapelusz: Height: 2–4 cm.
Yellow-brownish, bell-shaped, folded and furrowed, when young covered with shiny granules, remnants of the veil.
In wet conditions the caps deliquesce.
spod: White in young specimens, darkening with age, finally black, but their edges remain white for a long time.
They are crowded and narrowly attached.
In wet weather they deliquesce.
trzon: Length 5–10 cm, width (3–),5 cm.
It is cylindrical, hollow inside, white and finely dusted in young specimens, smooth and shiny in older ones.
podobne: Coprinellus disseminatus does not have shiny grains on the cap, but small hairs or fine scales, which are remains of the veil; it grows on rotting tree stumps
Coprinellus angulatus – difficult to distinguish; it has a dull surface and the gill edges are not white; reliable identification comes only from observing the spores under a microscope.
Mycena inclinata – similar in colour and also growing in clusters on stumps, but it has white gills and a smaller cap
Coprinellus xanthothrix – differs in the yellow felty base of the stem
Psathyrella candolleana – has similarly blackening gills, but the cap without radial wrinkling

kapelusz: Height 3–8 cm, cylindrical in young individuals, later bell-shaped, finally almost spread out.
It is radially grooved, at the top it has a few petal-like scales.
Colour ash-grey or grey-brown, darker in the centre.
In the mature fruit body the whole cap together with the gills dissolves into a black liquid.
spod: Broad, crowded, with serrated edges.
In a young fruit body white, later pink, and finally black, and they deliquesce.
trzon: Height 5–15 cm, cylindrical, hollow, easily breaking off from the cap.
Surface smooth, white, ring absent.
Base distinctly pointed.
miazsz: White, thin and brittle in the cap, soft and fibrous in the stem.
Taste insignificant, smell pleasant, but indistinct.

kapelusz: Diameter 1.5–5.5 cm.
Height 1–3 cm.
At first it is cylindrical and almost entirely enclosed by a universal veil covered with white bristles or hairs.
However, it spreads out very quickly, becomes arched, and finally its margins roll outwards.
In older specimens the tufts and hairs disappear, the cap becomes smooth and takes on a light grey, later mouse-grey colour.
It is grooved almost to the centre.
In a manner typical of ink caps, during ripening it deliquesces, its margins become folded and tattered and the cap becomes thinner and thinner.
spod: Broad, free, with smooth edges.
At first they are whitish, later grey, finally black.
trzon: Height 7–15 cm, thickness 0.3–0.7 cm.
It is cylindrical, hollow, brittle.
Colour white, surface smooth or fibrous.
miazsz: White, thin, without smell and without taste.
wysyp: Spores elliptical, smooth, dextrinoid, with a broad germ pore.
podobne: There are many similar inkcap species.
A reliable distinction between them is often impossible without microscopic examination.
Very similar are, for example:
Coprinopsis lagopides (formerly called the burnt-ground inkcap), which grows mainly on burnt sites and differs in the structure of the spores.
Coprinellus flocculosus, which grows mainly on compost and nitrogen-rich soil.
It has a brownish top of the cap.

kapelusz: At maturity it reaches a diameter of 3–7 cm and a height of 7–12 cm.
At first it is egg-shaped, then bell-shaped, then its margins roll outwards and, in the manner typical of inky caps, the fruit body turns black and during maturation dissolves into a black liquid.
Surface very dark, grey-brown, shiny, covered with silvery-white fibrils that separate into patches as the cap expands.
spod: Free or slightly adnate, crowded, at first white, then reddish, and then black and turning into a black liquid.
trzon: Height 10–20 cm, diameter 0.7–1.5 cm, cylindrical with a bulbous base, hollow.
Surface white, flocculose.

kapelusz: Height 5–10 cm, at first cylindrical, later bell-shaped.
In a mature fruit body the cap splits radially, its margin opens and rises, and the whole cap together with the gills dissolves into a black liquid.
It is white in colour and fibrously scaly, only the tip is ochre in colour and bare.
spod: White in the young fruit body, later pink, and finally black, crowded and thin.
trzon: Height 10–20 cm, thickness 0.8–2 cm.
It is cylindrical, hollow, easily breaking off from the cap, somewhat rooting.
Surface smooth, white, with a movable ring.
miazsz: White, thin and brittle in the cap, soft and fibrous in the stem.
Taste insignificant, smell pleasant, but indistinct.
wysyp: Spores 10–15 × 6–8 µm in diameter, elliptical, smooth, black.
podobne: The shaggy ink cap can be confused with Coprinopsis atramentaria, which differs in that its cap is smooth and grey.
It is precisely at least 24 hours before and 72 hours after eating this species that alcohol must not be consumed.
Both species have almost the same habitats.

owocnik: Annual, usually attached to the substrate sideways, only rarely spread out.
It has a semicircular, elongated shape, width up to 12 cm, thickness 2–4 cm, and on a cross-section has a triangular profile (the base is attached to the substrate).
The upper surface is unzoned, or slightly zoned, covered with hairs 1–2 mm long.
They are whitish in colour, but greyish or rusty-brown at the top.
Young fruit bodies are uniformly hairy, in older ones tufts form that give the fruit body a rough appearance.
The margin of the fruit body is sharp.
Hymenophore tubular.
Pores fairly large, 15–20 fit into one cm.
They are the colour of dark honey.
The tubes are up to 1 cm long.
The flesh is distinctly radially fibrous, pale grey-ochre in colour.
After drying it fades, under the action of KOH it changes colour to dark brown.
podobne: Trametes hirsuta is similarly hairy and of similar colour, but it has a thinner fruit body and finer pores.

inne: Thanks to its characteristic colouring it is easily distinguished from other species.
Laccaria amethystina is similar in size and colouring, but it has more distant gills and has neither a cortina nor a fibrillose surface.
Other violet species of webcaps clearly differ in morphology and in the surface of the fruit body.

kapelusz: Cap diameter 5–15 cm.
It is not hygrophanous.
Shape in young fruit bodies hemispherical, later arched, finally spread out with a blunt and broad umbo.
The margin remains inrolled for a long time.
Surface of young fruit bodies radially fibrillose, of older ones scaly-fibrous.
At the margins remnants of a red veil.
Colour rusty brown, cinnamon-reddish or reddish.
A characteristic feature of this species is the frequently encountered bell shape of the cap.
spod: Broad, slightly notched with a tooth, with whitish and slightly crenate edges.
In young specimens they are light ochre, in older ones reddish-brown.
trzon: Height 7–16 cm, thickness 1–4 cm, cylindrical in shape, base bulbously thickened.
It is solid.
Surface light violet-brown, covered with brick-coloured, fibrous remnants of the veil, which as the stem grows form numerous usually bands.
Base white and felty.
miazsz: Colour from whitish yellow-reddish to pale brown.
Taste mild, smell indistinct.
podobne: Cortinarius (the red-girdled webcap) has several characteristic features: red bands on the stem, often a bell-shaped cap, and hanging red remains of the cortina at the margins.
They make it fairly easy to distinguish it from other webcap species.
Cortinarius buillardii is somewhat similar.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–6 cm, shape at first hemispherical or arched, later straight-arched, older specimens become flat.
Surface light yellowish, covered with scales in colour from cinnabar red to saffron red.
In dry weather the cap fades.
The surface is dry, not hygrophanous.
spod: At first cream-yellow or pale ochre-yellow, with time they darken and become fawn-rusty, finally pale cinnamon.
They are slightly attached to the stem and fairly crowded.
trzon: Height 4–8 cm, thickness up to 1.5 cm, cylindrical.
Solid in young specimens, hollow in older ones.
Surface under the cap white-cream and slightly scaly, otherwise whitish-yellowish and covered fairly densely with cinnabar-red-brown fibrils and scales.
Base darker, dark red.
miazsz: Whitish in the cap, yellowish or ochre in the stem, even darker at the base, grey-yellow.
With time it gradually darkens more and more and becomes red-brown.
Taste and smell indistinct.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–10 cm, shape at first hemispherical, later arched or flat and slightly depressed in the centre.
Surface silky matt and dry in dry weather, slippery and shiny in wet weather.
The cap margin stays inrolled for a long time and is joined to the stem by a grey-violet cortina.
At first it is blue-violet in colour, later fading and becoming grey to light ochre.
Young fruit bodies are covered with dirty-whitish remains of the cortina.
spod: Broad and broadly attached.
In young fruit bodies they are blue-violet, later become grey-violet, finally ochre-brown.
Gill edges furrowed and blue.
trzon: Height 4–8 cm, thickness 1–2 cm, cylindrical, solid.
At the base it has a bulb up to 4.5 cm in diameter.
Solid in young specimens, hollow in older ones.
Surface at first fibrous, grey-violet in colour, later bare.
In the lower part it has a white sheath, which quickly changes colour to ochre-brown.
miazsz: Light blue.
Taste weak, smell musty.
podobne: Cortinarius cumatilis.
It does not have a distinct bulb and grows in coniferous forests.
Cortinarius agathosmus.
It has a different stem.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–12 cm, egg-shaped and hemispherical in young mushrooms, later broadly bell-shaped, flat with a blunt umbo in older ones.
Young fruit bodies are frosted.
In dry weather it becomes wrinkled and cracked at the margins.
At first it is grey-violet, greyish and has remnants of the veil at the margins.
Older specimens are in colour from leather-yellow to beige-brown.
spod: In the young fruit body clay-yellow, later rusty-brownish, crowded, notched with a tooth, at first covered by a white sheath.
trzon: Height 7–15 cm, thickness 1–3 cm.
It is cylindrical, solid, bulbously widened at the base.
It has a narrow whitish-yellowish ring, above which it is flaky, below fibrous and striate.
Colour from whitish through cream to ochre.
miazsz: White or pale cream.
Taste slight, smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spores almond-shaped and warty, measuring 11–14 × 7–9 µm.
podobne: Young fruit bodies with a silvery-violet cap are similar to Cortinarius traganus, but that one has an unpleasant smell and gills covered by a cortina.
Phaeolepiota aurea is also similar, but in Poland it is a rare species, has a golden-yellow cap and a distinctly striate ring.
Adult ochre-coloured gypsy mushrooms (Cortinarius caperatus) are similar to several other webcap species, especially when they have already lost the membranous ring.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm, at first hemispherical with an inrolled margin, later convex, finally flat, sometimes shallowly concave, usually with a broad umbo.
Surface olive-yellow in youth, later rusty from the centre, finely felted.
Cortina lemon yellow, sometimes whitish.
spod: At first light olive, sometimes with a paler whitish or grey-blue edge, later rusty-brown from the spores.
trzon: Height 4–10 cm, thickness 0.3–0.8 cm, cylindrical.
Surface yellow-olive with rusty fibres of the veil.
Base with felty, whitish, sometimes with a blue-grey tinge in young fruit bodies.
miazsz: Flesh yellow-olive with a slightly radish-like smell and a mild taste.

podobne: Cortinarius cinnamomeus.
It has gills coloured from orange to orange-brown, they are never yellow,
Cortinarius semisanguineus.
It has gills at first dark blood-purple, then cinnamon from the spores.
Cortinarius croceus

kapelusz: It belongs to the group of small webcaps.
Cap diameter 1–6 cm.
Shape in young fruit bodies arched, later low-arched, finally spread with a small umbo.
It is not hygrophanous.
Surface smooth or finely radially fibrous or very finely scaly, matt.
Colour nut-brown, olive-brown, umber-brown, sometimes reddish-brown.
Margins usually paler – olive-yellowish.
It is often cracked radially, especially in dry weather.
Rusty-brown remnants of the cortina hang from the margin, sometimes they are also found at the edges of the cap.
spod: Crowded, uneven, notched with a tooth at the stem.
They are 3–5 mm wide, with even, crenate or toothed edges, slightly paler.
In young specimens they are yellow-rusty, then rusty-ochre, finally olive-ochre.
They are never lemon yellow.
trzon: Height 2–8 cm, thickness up to 0.7 cm, cylindrical in shape, sometimes slightly wavy.
At first it is solid, later hollow.
Surface yellowish and silkily shiny, covered with yellowish and usually short-lived remnants of the veil, and in the lower part with brown fibrils.
miazsz: Thin, pale yellow or yellow with olive tinges, darker in the lower part of the stem.
Without a distinct smell, slightly bitter in taste.
podobne: Cortinarius malicorius.
It has olive-green flesh, and the remains of the cortina on the margin of the cap are orange.
Cortinarius cinnamomeoluteus.
Young fruit bodies have yellow gills.
Cortinarius croceus.
Older specimens of Cortinarius croceus and Cortinarius cinnamomeus are very similar.
To distinguish these species reliably, young specimens are needed; they should be cut through to determine the colour of the gills.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–9 cm, at first hemispherical, then arched, finally flatly spread out.
Surface felty or finely scaly, at first olive-green or brown-green, then olive-brown.
The margin stays rolled under for a long time and is joined to the stem by an olive-green cortina.
When straightened it is even and smooth.
spod: Broadly attached and broad, at first olive-green, then olive-brown.
trzon: Height up to 5–10 cm, thickness 1.2–2 cm, club-shaped with a bulbous base, at first solid, then hollow.
Surface above the annular zone light, below olive-yellow to olive-green.
miazsz: Fleshy, cream with an olive tinge, yellow-green only in the outer layer of the stem.
It has the taste and smell of radish.
podobne: Among the species occurring in Poland, Cortinarius venetus is similar.
It has a hygrophanous cap of olive-green colour, the cylindrical stem is not bulbous and it is smaller in size.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–5 cm, shape at first hemispherical or bell-shaped, later flatly spread, sometimes with a small umbo in the centre.
The margin remains inrolled for a long time.
Surface smooth in the centre, fibrously felty near the margin, or covered with longitudinal small scales.
Brown in the centre, becoming paler towards the margins and gradually passing through olive-brown with an olive or orange tinge into olive-yellow.
spod: Delicately toothed.
They are yellow in colour, sometimes with an orange tinge.
Gill edges yellow.
trzon: Height 3–6 cm, thickness up to 3–7 mm, cylindrical, solid.
Surface colour from yellow to ochre-yellow.
The base is darker – yellow-brown – and hyphae of yellow mycelium grow from it.
Along the whole length of the stem there are rough bands of veil in colour from yellow-brown to grey.
miazsz: Yellow in the cap, dirty yellow with an olive tinge at the base of the stem.
It has a faint, unpleasant taste and a smell of iodoform.
podobne: Cortinarius cinnamomeus.
Older specimens of Cortinarius croceus and Cortinarius cinnamomeus are very similar.
To distinguish these species reliably, young specimens are needed; they should be cut through to determine the colour of the gills.
According to some mycologists both these webcaps may be forms of the same species, and a thorough DNA analysis of the material would be needed to settle this.
Cortinarius chrysolitus.
Cortinarius cinnamomeoluteus.
Young specimens have yellow gills.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–12 cm, at first hemispherical then convex with a turned-in margin, finally flat.
Surface sticky when wet, blue-violet in young fruit bodies, fading from the centre and changing colour to ochre.
White cortina.
spod: At first white or greyish, then light rusty-brown.
trzon: Height 5–10 cm, thickness 1–2.5 cm, cylindrical or club-shaped.
Surface white, with violet fibrils in young fruit bodies.
miazsz: Whitish with an indistinct smell and a mild taste.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–6 cm, at first conical-bell-shaped, then flat.
Surface silky-fibrillose, in colour from orange-brown to olive-brown.
Margin rolled under for a long time.
spod: Adnate or decurrent with a tooth, crowded, at first light saffron-orange, then reddish-orange to rusty brown with yellowish streaks.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness 0.5–01.2 cm, cylindrical, widening at the base.
Surface pale orange-yellow, browner towards the base, with orange mycelium at the base.
miazsz: In the cap when moist yellowish to dark olive-green, when dry light orange-yellow.
In the stem when dry yellowish towards the apex.
Smell of radish, taste indistinct.
podobne: This webcap (Cortinarius) is characterised by a stocky and compact habit, a cap margin with pale orange remnants of the veil, saffron-orange gills, dark olive flesh when wet and small spores.
When dry, the cap and flesh lose their olive colour and become more orange, especially the flesh.
The microscopic elements of its flesh and gills turn from pink-violet to purple in KOH.
In dry weather it is confused with Cortinarius cinnamomeus or with the far more common Cortinarius croceus.
It is distinguished from them by the gill edges, which are olive-yellow to golden-yellow.
All three species can grow in the same environment, although the apple webcap and the cinnamon webcap seem to be associated with older trees.
All of them are associated with various conifers.

According to a Czech source, Cortinarius cinnamomeus has a more distinctly scaly cap, sometimes a greenish top, slightly larger spores (6.5–8 × 3.5–5 µm) and has no remains of a bright orange partial veil at the margin of the cap.
Cortinarius croceus has rather yellow gills, a finely scaly cap and larger spores (7–9 × 4.5–6 µm).

kapelusz: Cap diameter from 4 to 12 cm, hemispherical when young, then arched, finally spread out.
Colour from yellow-brown to light chestnut-brown.
In wet weather sticky, slimy and gluey, in dry weather shiny.
spod: From whitish to clay-brownish, usually narrow and decurrent on the stem, or attached to it.
trzon: Height 5–10 cm, thickness 8–18 mm, cylindrical, solid, sometimes only thickened at the base.
Usually up to 2/3 of its height it is covered with a white and slippery veil, above which it turns brown.
miazsz: Whitish to cream, without taste and smell.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid or almond-shaped, smooth, measuring 12–15 × 6–7 μm.
podobne: Cortinarius collinitus.
It differs little in appearance: it has only a slightly different cap colour (from yellow-orange to brown-orange) and a violet-brown stem, often narrowed at the bottom.
Grows only under spruces;
Cortinarius trivialis.
It has an ochre-yellow-brown cap and rolls of slime on the stem.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–7 cm.
Hemispherical or bell-shaped when young, later convex with inrolled margins, with a blunt umbo in the centre.
Surface dull and felty with delicate scales.
Colour cinnamon-brown, brown-red or brown.
spod: At first saffron yellow, then orange to orange-rusty.
They are convex, sparse and fairly thick, broadly attached to the stem or slightly decurrent.
trzon: 5–10 cm high, cylindrical, narrowed below, solid, yellowish or yellowish-brown with longitudinal darker fibres.
miazsz: Yellowish.
Taste mild or slightly sourish, smell faint, similar to the smell of radish.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid or almond-shaped, slightly warty, measuring 8–11 × 5.5–7 μm.
podobne: Cortinarius rubellus has a more distinct umbo, a stem thickened at the base, and its gills do not have an orange tinge.
Occurs in coniferous forests.
Cortinarius semisanguineus.
It has redder gills and occurs in coniferous forests.

kapelusz: Diameter 1.5–5 cm, conical when young, then bell-shaped, finally flatly spread out with a blunt umbo.
Margin rolled under for a long time.
Surface smooth, fibrously felty only at the margin, red-brown with a darker centre.
In young specimens, yellow or reddish fibrils of the cortina between the cap margin and the stem.
Older specimens fade and become rusty-brown.
spod: Attached, moderately crowded, at first carmine-red with an orange edge, then orange.
Cortina intensely yellow.
trzon: Height 4–8 cm, thickness 4–7 mm, cylindrical, usually slightly bent.
Surface yellow or golden yellow with fibrils of orange to blood-red colour.
Base of the stem often with yellow mycelium.
inne: Thin, dirty pale yellow, with a pale olive tinge.
Taste and smell weak, similar to radish.
podobne: There are many similarly coloured webcaps, e.g. Cortinarius sanguineus or Cortinarius semisanguineus.

kapelusz: It reaches a diameter of 3–8 cm, orange-brownish, rusty-orange to cinnamon-orange, rufous, with fairly thin flesh, in the centre with a pointed or rounded umbo.
Skin dull, delicately felty or rough.
trzon: Coloured like the cap, with a winding pattern from the yellowish veil, cylindrical to slenderly club-shaped.
spod: Cinnamon-orange to rusty-brownish, widely spaced, fairly thick.
miazsz: Yellowish, in the stem more rusty-brownish.
When cut it gives off a faint smell of radish.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm, colour blood-red, after ripening fading to orange-brown.
At first it is hemispherical-bell-shaped, with time it becomes flattened and spread out.
In the centre a blunt umbo.
Skin dry, felty, matt.
spod: Fairly crowded and rounded at the stem.
They have a colour from cinnabar to dark blood red.
trzon: Length 3–6 cm, thickness 0.7 cm.
It is cylindrical, fibrous, hollow inside, sometimes widened at the bottom.
Colouring the same as the cap, the base is covered with orange felt.
miazsz: Thin, the same colour as the cap and stem, with a bitter taste and a smell of radish.
wysyp: Spores elliptical, with fine warts; measuring 6-9 × 4-5 µm.
podobne: Cortinarius anthracinus – differs in its dark purple-brown cap with a carmine-yellow margin.
Cortinarius cinnamomeus – is similar to older, faded specimens of the blood-red webcap, but does not have blood-red scales.
Cortinarius semisanguineus – has gills of a similar colour, but the cap and stem are olive-brown.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–6 cm, convex when young, flat-arched when older, often with an umbo, smooth or scaly.
Matt when young, later bare and shiny.
Its colour ranges from cinnamon through olive-brown to cinnamon-brown.
spod: They are up to 10 mm wide.
They are sinuately adnate, crowded, at first blood-red, later brown-reddish, with paler edges.
trzon: 3–7 cm long, 4–6 mm thick, cylindrical, fibrous at the base.
It is yellowish or yellow-ochre in colour, often reddened at the base.
miazsz: Yellowish in colour, reddish and fibrous at the base.
wysyp: Spores elliptical, with fine warts; measuring 6.5–8 × 4.5–5 µm.
podobne: Cortinarius cinnamomeus.
It is distinguished by cinnamon-yellow scales on the cap,
Cortinarius purpureus.
It has a red-brown cap and the stem is almost entirely red and fibrous,
Laccaria laccata, which has distantly spaced gills and a white spore print.
Edible.

kapelusz: Diameter 1.5–7 cm, when young hemispherical, later successively arched and flat, finally flat with a blunt umbo or slightly concave.
Surface felty, at first yellow-green or olive, then olive-brown.
The margin is lighter – olive-yellow, in young fruit bodies joined to the stem by the remains of a yellow partial veil.
It is hygrophanous.
spod: Broad and broadly attached to the stem, at first olive-green, later rusty-brown.
Edges paler and uniformly coloured.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness 5–10 mm, cylindrical, club-shaped in the lower part, brittle, in young specimens solid and longitudinally covered with sulphur yellow fibrils, in older ones hollow and covered with brown fibres, only the base of the stem remains yellow-green.
miazsz: Whitish when dry, olive-grey when moist; smell of radish, taste astringent
podobne: Cortinarius cotoneus is similar.
It also has a felty cap, but its cap is not hygrophanous, the stem is at most club-shaped but not bulbous, it has no greenish tinges and it is larger

kapelusz: Diameter on average from 4 to 15 cm. Young specimens have fruit bodies of an intense blue-violet colour with a slightly metallic sheen.
In older specimens the colour is brown with a violet tinge.
Surface granular, dry, velvety.
Shape semicircular to flat in older ones.
spod: Spacing quite variable in this species, from sparse to moderately crowded, broad and broadly attached, colour from violet in young individuals, through violet-brown to dark brown in older ones.
Gill edges covered with fine hairs (this can be seen only under a hand lens).
trzon: Height 8–12 cm, thickness 1–3 cm.
Shape club-like with a distinctly thickened base (reaching a thickness of about 4 cm).
Solid in young specimens, hollow inside in older ones.
Surface scaly, dark violet, and almost black in dry weather.
In young specimens it is surrounded by a veil, which, however, quickly disappears.
miazsz: Colour from light to dark violet, with a mild taste and a cedar smell.
Alkali (base) stains the flesh red, acid greenish.
podobne: Cortinarius traganus, which has ochre gills, later rusty-brown, saffron-ochre flesh and an unpleasant smell of acetylene.
Cortinarius hercynicus, sometimes regarded as a subspecies of the violet webcap.
It occurs under spruces and pines, has broader spores.

owocnik: Diameter 3–8 cm, trumpet-funnel-shaped with a rolled-under margin, wavy in mature specimens.
The inner part at first brownish-black, later blackish-grey, finally black, with irregular sparse scales.
The outer one grey-brown, at first smooth, then wrinkled.
The outer side of the whole fruit body is covered by the hymenium, so in mature specimens the white spores colour it white.
It is hygrophanous.
trzon: Height 5–12 cm.
It is hollow inside, widening like a funnel from the bottom upwards and passing smoothly into the cap.
In the upper part it is often torn.
Surface smooth or wrinkled, grey-brown or grey-black in colour.
Older stems, like the cap, are dusted white with spores.
miazsz: Thin, at first grey-black, then completely black.
It is fairly flexible and springy.
After drying it becomes brittle, but after soaking it regains its flexibility.
Taste slight, smell pleasant.
podobne: It is hard to confuse with another mushroom because of its characteristic appearance and the lack of similar species.
Most similar is Craterellus undulatus.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–6 cm, trumpet-shaped and deeply navel-like, with thin flesh and a strongly wavy margin, in old age often passing openly into the hollow stem.
Cap colour from yellow-brown to grey-brown.
spod: In the form of ridges clearly decurrent on the stem.
Young ridges sometimes beautifully yellow, later yellow-grey or white-grey; narrow, thick, distant, forked with numerous cross connections (anastomoses), decurrent on the stem.
trzon: Height 4–8 cm, thickness 0.4–1 cm.
It is irregularly cylindrical and longitudinally flattened, wrinkled and distinctly hollow.
Ochre-yellow at the bottom, greyish at the top.
miazsz: Yellowish-grey, with a mild taste.
Smell barely perceptible, often somewhat earthy-musty.
wysyp: Spores spherical, smooth and almost colourless, 9-12 × 5-10 µm in diameter.
podobne: Craterellus tubaeformis can be confused with Craterellus lutescens, which has a golden-yellow stem and greyish-whitish, weakly developed ridges.
Cantharellus cinereus is also similar, but it has a black-brown stem and cap and ridges with a bluish bloom.

Old specimens of the chanterelle may also be confused with the rarely occurring Craterellus undulatus, found on fertile soils under oaks and hazels, often in dense clusters; its stem is grey-brown and the cap blue-grey with a characteristic curly edge.

owocnik: Annual, 0.5–3 cm in diameter and 3–5 mm thick.
Stem small and present only in young fruit bodies, later it disappears.
The fruit body is kidney-shaped or shell-shaped, thin and attached sideways, the margins in young specimens inrolled.
Surface in colour from white to grey-ochre, smooth, dull.
The skin can be easily peeled off.
Under the skin there is a gelatinous layer, giving the fruit body its springiness and softness.
Hymenophore gilled.
The gills radiate from the point where the cap is attached to the substrate.
They are crowded and thin, cream in young specimens, cinnamon-brown in older ones, finally grey-brown.
Gill edges covered with a gelatinous layer (the same as in the cap under the skin).
Flesh: thin, white, with a mild taste and an indistinct smell.
wysyp: Spores broadly ellipsoid, smooth, measuring 7-9 × 5–7 μm.
podobne: There are many similar species of Tapinella, but none of them has a gelatinous layer.
This feature makes it easy to identify this species (the layer can be felt with the fingers or seen through a lens on a cross-section).
Other morphologically similar species include: Crepidotis applanatus and Crepidotus crocophyllus.
Similar in its upper side is also Plicaturopsis crispa, but on the underside it has no gills, but small folds.

owocnik: Young fruit bodies are roundish or slightly cylindrical, with a felty, roughly woolly surface and a colour from yellowish through dirty orange to cinnamon.

After maturing they take on the shape of a thick-walled mug, cup or crucible and are covered with a whitish epiphragm, which on splitting reveals numerous lens-shaped peridioles covered with a thick, cream-white tunic.
At first they are pale ochre, later whitish.
They are joined to the peridium by a cord attached in the middle part of the underside of the peridiole (there is a small knob on it at that point).
With time the small cords disappear, and then the peridioles are immersed in a drop of slimy substance filling the bottom of the peridium.
The peridium is thick, single-layered, smooth, shiny and even on the inner side, grey-whitish in colour, felty on the outer side.
The opening of the peridium is round and even, the epifragm closing it is two-layered; the outer layer is felty and of the same colour as the peridium, the inner layer is white.
Sometimes after the epiphragm ruptures, remnants of it remain at the edge of the opening.
This species is characterised by great morphological variability.
Specimens occurring in the far north and in xerothermic habitats are small and pale in colour, whereas those occurring in warmer regions with more rainfall are large and darker.

kapelusz: Diameter from 2 to 4.5 cm, young – hemispherical, convex, later flat, and slightly sunken in the middle.
In wet conditions pale yellow to watery white, somewhat sticky, in drought snow white.
spod: Distant, decurrent along the stem, broad at the base, thin at the edge, watery, whitish-yellow.
trzon: Height 1.5 to 4.5 cm, diameter 3 to 5 mm, equally thick, narrowed and flattened towards the base, at first solid, later hollow, colour white, sometimes with a pink bloom.
miazsz: Watery white, no smell, taste mild.
podobne: Because of its characteristic appearance and place of growth, a mistake is unlikely.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–12(15) cm, red-brown or chestnut-brown.
Skin matt, delicately velvety, fairly dry.
spod: Lemon-yellow, fairly short, shiny, very sensitive to pressure, immediately turning dark blue.
trzon: Nutty, yellowish in the upper part, almost always slender.
Surface finely granular-tomentose, never reticulate.
When cut or pressed it turns intensely blue.
miazsz: Yellow, after cutting immediately turning dark blue to blue-black.
Fleshy and firm.
In older specimens dry and rough.
podobne: The bluing bolete (Cyanoboletus species) can be confused with the edible species: Boletus badius, Boletus subtomentosus and Xerocomellus chrysenteron.

owocnik: Annual.
It is attached to the substrate sideways.
Diameter 1–5 cm, exceptionally up to 8 cm, width 0.3–1 cm, bracket-shaped and sometimes thickened at the base, less often spread out and reflexed.
Margin thin, wavy and slightly inrolled.
Surface felty, rough or hairy, weakly striate.
A characteristic reticulum appears on older fruit bodies.
Young fruit bodies are white, when touched they change colour to blue-grey to dark grey, older fruit bodies are blue-grey to dark grey all the time.
The margin of the fruit body (growth zone) remains white throughout.
spod: Tubular, coloured from white to grey-blue.
Turns blue when touched.
The tubes are 0.5–4.5 mm long and sometimes run down onto the substrate.
The pores are 0.15–0.3 mm in diameter, exceptionally 0.4 mm, with 3–4 of them per 1 mm.
They are round to angular in shape with bluish margins, tattered in older fruit bodies.
miazsz: Whitish, turning blue after damage, weakly zoned and fairly hard.
Taste and smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spores cylindrical, slightly curved, colourless, with a smooth surface and 2 droplets.
podobne: There are many species of tree-dwelling fungi with white fruit bodies, so it can be difficult to distinguish young, white fruit bodies of the blue bracket from older ones that are atypically coloured brown.
However, it is easy to distinguish it by a touch test; the fruit body of the blue bracket turns blue when touched.

owocnik: Goblet- or cup-shaped, 0.8–1.2 cm high and 0.5–1 cm wide.
Young individuals are completely closed and have a convex and rounded top.
After maturing, the top of the cup opens, revealing the interior with peridioles.
The outer surface is delicately hairy, at first ochre or light brown in colour, then greyish.
The inner surface of the cup is smooth, bare, shiny and ash-grey in colour.
The peridioles are disc-shaped, usually shiny.
They are whitish or greyish in colour and measure 2–3.5 mm.
They are attached to the fruit body by thin cords (funiculus).
podobne: In Poland there are two more cups of similar size and shape: Cyathus striatus, which is strongly spiny on the outside and striate on the inside, and Cyathus stercoreus, which also has a spiny outer surface and grows on animal dung.

owocnik: Cup-shaped, 1–2 cm high and 0.8–1 cm wide.
The outer side is rusty brown, brown or almost black in colour and strongly hairy.
The margin is sometimes slightly turned up.
The inner side is without hairs, smooth and distinctly longitudinally striate, which is a characteristic species feature.
It is silvery shiny.
In mature specimens there are disc-shaped, grey or grey-brown peridioles 1.5–2 mm in diameter in the middle of the cup.
They are attached to the fruit body by thin cords (funiculus).
podobne: In Poland there is a somewhat similar Cyathus olla, which is silky-fibrous on the outside and without stripes inside.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm.
In young fruit bodies semicircular, then arched, finally flat.
Fibrils hang from the margins, being remnants of the veil.
It is radially wrinkled, not hygrophanous.
Surface dry, granular, at first pale yellow in colour, later ochre and golden ochre.
spod: Up to 4 mm wide, crowded, slightly notched at the stem.
White in young specimens, later ochre-yellowish.
trzon: Height 4–6 cm, thickness 2–5 mm.
It is brittle, cylindrical, thickened in the lower part, sometimes curved, at first solid, later hollow inside.
Surface the same colour as the cap.
In the upper part a small, ascending ring, whitish and lumpy-hairy.
Above the ring it is bare, below it is covered with protruding scales.
miazsz: Yellowish.
Soft in the cap, hard in the stem.
Smell unpleasant, earthy.
podobne: The ochre-yellow Cystoderma can be confused with the edible Cystoderma jasonis.
It is distinguished from other granulose dapperlings by its ochre colouring, from the dapperlings (Lepiota) by its ring and granular cap.
Cystoderma fallax is very similar, but it is easily distinguished by the characteristic, large and persistent ring on the stem.

kapelusz: Diameter 5-20 centimetres, at first semicircular, then bell-shaped, conical up to convex.
Colour golden yellow to yellow-brown, not infrequently with an orange tinge.
It is matt, covered with tiny granules.
They stain the hand, sticking to it when someone touches the cap.
Margin sharp, remnants of the veil hang from it.
The surface is sometimes wrinkled.
spod: Not attached to the stem, crowded, cream in colour, then ochre and ochre-brown.
trzon: Above the ring cream or yellowish, smooth.
Below it yellowish to yellow-brown with granular scales.
Cylindrical, but with a widened base.
Hard but flexible.
It has a golden-brown ring, with granules at the bottom.
miazsz: White, yellowish, turning yellow when cut, with a sourish and aromatic smell.
Taste indefinite, but mild.
wysyp: Spores oblong, pointed, rough, 10–14 × 5–6 µm in diameter, without a germ pore.
Trama of the gills regular (hyphae running parallel).
podobne: Because of its characteristic appearance this species is easily recognisable.
It can be confused only with some powdercaps (Cystoderma), but they are much smaller.

owocnik: Diameter 5–15 cm, thickness 1–2 cm, shell-shaped, hemispherical.
No stem, attached to the substrate sideways.
Colouring variable: light grey, ochre-brown, wine-red or blackish-red.
Concentric zoning of the same colour is often present.
Skin bare, upper surface of the fruit body usually uneven and wrinkled.
Margin of the fruit body very sharp and thin.
spod: In the form of elongated, angular, maze-like gill-like tubes arranged radially.
Sometimes at the base they pass into gills.
They are 0.5–1.5 cm long and whitish or greyish in colour.
Their characteristic feature is that after being crushed they change colour to flesh pink.
miazsz: Pale brownish, flexible, of cork-like consistency.
Young specimens have a sourish smell, older ones are odourless.
wysyp: Spores cylindrical, slightly curved, with a narrowed and pointed base, with 2-3 oil droplets.
podobne: Trametes versicolor has a similarly zoned, but more colourful cap, and it also differs completely in its hymenophore.
Trametes gibbosa has a similar hymenophore, but its fruit body on the upper side is much paler and often green from algae.
Daedalea quercina also has labyrinthine pores, but it grows mainly on oaks, less often on hornbeams and beeches and has a larger, thicker and only rarely zoned fruit body.

A feature by which Daedaleopsis confragosa can be easily distinguished from other similar species is the pinking of the pores when pressed, but this phenomenon occurs only in autumn on fresh fruit bodies.

owocnik: A polyporoid fungus forming spread-out or sessile fruit bodies up to 0.6 cm thick and up to 17 cm long.
Sometimes they have margins bent back for about 2 cm.
The upper surface of the fruit body is bristly or velvety and in colour from brown to black.
On it there are darker, grooved streaks on stiff hairs.
Hymenophore tubular, dirty beige, yellow-brown, greyish in colour.
The tubes are 0.5–5 mm long, their pores 1–2 mm in diameter and irregular in shape, slightly elongated or polygonal.
The flesh is pale brown.
The spore print is in colour from light to dark brown.
Spores cylindrical, measuring 8–10 × 2.5–3.5 μm.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–12 mm, at first hemispherical, then spread out, finally strongly concave, translucent with a sharp, toothed margin.
Surface whitish, bare and smooth.
spod: Gill-like and veined.
Gill-veins narrow, distant, sometimes branching and anastomosing, adnate and slightly decurrent on the stem.
trzon: Thread-like, 10–15 mm high and 0.5–1 mm thick.
Base bulbous with a delicate mycelium.
Surface white.
miazsz: Soft, membranous, without a distinct smell, with a mild taste.
podobne: A characteristic feature of this species is poorly developed, vein-like gills (so-called veined gills).
Some species of the genus Hemimycena are similar, small and white, but they have well-developed gills.
Mycena epipterygia has lemon-yellow colouring.

owocnik: They reach a height of up to 20 cm and resemble basidiomycetes in habit.
They consist of a head and a stem, hollow inside.
Head saddle-shaped with two or three irregular folds.
Surface coloured from ochre-brown to dark brown.
Stem thick, tapering towards the top, white.
Flesh with a mild taste, without distinct smell.
podobne: The false morel (Gyromitra esculenta) is distinguished by its more folded head.
Gyromitra infula and Gyromitra ambigua have the head turned upwards like an infula.

owocnik: Of the apothecium type, 1.5–4 cm wide, sessile or with a short stem, urn-shaped or cup-shaped.
In older specimens the margin often splits in a star shape.
Hymenial (inner) surface matt, grey-brown to black-brown, bare; outer surface whitish at the base, matt grey to black-brown, delicately hairy above (visible only through a hand lens).
The stem, if present, is very short, consisting of whitish folds or blunt ribs.
Flesh thin, brittle, about 1.0 mm thick, two-layered, watery grey and whitish with a mild smell and taste.
podobne: Dissingia leucomelaena has fruit bodies similar to those of Peziza cup fungi.
It differs from them in the colour of the cup; the inner surface is matt, grey-black to dark grey-brown, the outer grey-black-white.
Helvella queletii is similar, but it has a distinct, ribbed, white stem whose ribs run to the base of the cup, and it also differs in colour; the outside is lighter than the inside.
Helvella acetabulum has a similar fruit body shape, but it is brown to ochre-brown, and its ribs run from the base of the stem to the edge of the cup.

kapelusz: It is from 5 to 12 cm in diameter.
When young bell-shaped to convex, later spread flat.
In old fruit bodies concave in the middle, fleshy, concentrically covered with blackish-brown protruding scales, which fall off.
Colour brown, darker in the centre.
In the centre of the cap there are black-brown, pointed, protruding scales, which fall off in older fruit bodies.
spod: Crowded, white to cream, forked at the ends.
trzon: Height from 4 to 8 cm, diameter from 0.7 to 1.5 cm.
It is cylindrical, bulbously widened at the base, hard and compact.
At first solid, later hollow, in the lower part brown, fibrous to scaly.
A broad membranous ring, in mature specimens hanging, ragged, whitish on top, brownish underneath.
miazsz: In the cap soft, in the stem rather tough-fibrous, whitish.
It has a penetrating, unpleasant spicy smell (like Scleroderma citrinum) and a sour taste.
podobne: The most similar is Echinoderma echinaceum, which differs in its stem covered with sharp scales (below the ring) and is smaller.

inne: Cap 3–6 cm in diameter, dark brown, covered with uniformly coloured, spiny warts.
Gills cream, stem the same colour as the cap, white at the top above the ring part.
Smell of rubber.
Spores 4–6 × 2.5–3.5 μm.
Cheilocystidia are present.
The most similar is Echinoderma perplexum, which has almost fusiform spores with more or less lateral apices.

kapelusz: Diameter 2.5–6 cm, young specimens spherical, then successively hemispherical and convex, finally spread out.
Surface flesh-brown, covered with slightly darker, sharp, spiny elevations and small scales.
spod: Fairly crowded, coloured from white to cream, not forked.
trzon: Cylindrical with a rooting base.
Surface of a similar colour to the cap, covered with scales below the ring, smoother above.
Ring inconspicuous, cobweb-like and fibrillose.
It disappears quickly, leaving behind only a ring zone.
miazsz: White with a cream tint, not changing colour when damaged, without distinct smell and taste, fibrillose in the stem.
podobne: Echinoderma asperum occurs in a similar environment and is macroscopically similar.
Also similar are Echinoderma calcicola and Echinoderma hystrix.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–9(11) cm, at first hemispherical with a rolled-under margin, later flat-convex or flat.
Surface flesh-brown, with brown pyramidal spines about 1 mm high, on a cream to light brown underside.
The spines flatten and fade with age, and are also easily rubbed off.
The margin is shortly inrolled and passes into the gills.
spod: At first whitish to yellowish in colour, later light brown, free, always very close together, with short gills, in older specimens with wavy edges.
trzon: Height 5–11 cm, thickness 1–2(3) cm, cylindrical, fibrous, with a bulbous base, brown and warty, and with whitish mycelium somewhat rooting.
Surface light brown, beige, yellow-brown, smooth, with falling-off spiny scales in the lower part of the stem and a paler top.
Ring absent, at most in its place there is a scaly zone.
miazsz: In the cap whitish or cream-yellow, in the lower part of the stem brown to yellow-brown.
Smell unpleasant, similar to burnt rubber, rarely neutral and imperceptible, taste indistinct.
podobne: Echinoderma asperum, Echinoderma calcicola, Echinoderma perplexum, Echinoderma echinaceum, Macrolepiota procera.

kapelusz: Diameter 6–12 cm, shape at first semicircular, later spread out, with a conical small umbo.
Margin at first inrolled, later bent.
It is hygrophanous.
It is coloured from whitish (when dry) to dark brown when moist.
When dry it has a silky shiny surface; during drought it cracks into scales.
spod: Broad, sinuately adnate to the stem.
In young specimens they are white, then pink, in older fruit bodies brown-red.
They often have uneven, wavy edges, and are rounded at the stem.
They are moderately crowded, up to 15 mm wide, the number of gills (L) is 40-80, the number of short gills 1-7.
trzon: Height 8–13 cm, thickness up to 1 cm, club-shaped.
Surface whitish, striate, covered with long grey-brown fibres.
miazsz: White, not changing colour after damage.
Taste mild, smell rancid.

kapelusz: Diameter 1.5–4 cm, conical-bell-shaped with an inrolled margin in young fruit bodies, arched with an umbo and a straight margin in mature ones.
Surface silky, delicately fibrous, scaly at the top.
It is hygrophanous; when dry grey-cream, when moist dark brown, with a grooved margin from the gills showing through.
spod: Number 20–50, with lamellulae L = 1-5(–7), distant, fairly broad, almost free, at first pale cream, then pink, finally pink-brown.
Edges gently notched.
trzon: About 3–7 cm high and 2–5 mm thick, brittle, cylindrical, widening towards the base.
Surface grey-brown, with longitudinal white fibrils, usually longitudinally grooved.
Hyphae of the mycelium at the base.
miazsz: Thin, whitish to grey-brown in colour, with a rancid smell and taste.
podobne: There are many similar species of Entoloma.
A reliable identification of them is often possible only through microscopic analysis.
As a species with a wide distribution, the star-spored pinkgill shows great morphological variability.
Many varieties and forms of it have been distinguished.
The similar Entoloma cetratum has a similar colouring and small blunt bulges on the cap, has no grooved stalk or mealy smell and differs in the structure of the spores.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–20 cm.
It is silkily shiny, whitish, or grey-ochre, mature grey-brown, smooth, bare, slightly fibrous, slightly slimy.
Semicircular when young, later convex, finally flat.
spod: First whitish, then cream, reddish with age, moderately crowded, notched with a small tooth.
They are sinuately attached, hence the former species name of this fungus.
trzon: Height 5–12 cm, width 1–3 cm, cylindrical, solid when young, then spongy, slightly grooved and shiny.
At the base it has white, felty mycelium.
miazsz: White and shiny, not changing colour when cut.
Taste and smell insignificant, mealy-cucumber.
podobne: It can be confused with many species of fungi, especially with Entoloma conferendum, Hygrophorus penarius or Clitocybe nebularis.
The poisonous pinkgill differs from these species by the salmon colouring of the gills, an umbo on the cap in older specimens and a pinkish spore print.

There is a danger of confusing it with the edible Calocybe gambosa, which is especially easy with young specimens, and with Entoloma clypeatum, which looks similar but grows under trees of the rose family (hawthorn, apple, plum, pear).

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm.
In young specimens it is conical or bell-shaped with a small tip, with time it becomes bell-shaped-convex, finally flattened with an umbo.
Margin sharp, rolled under when young, later straightened, usually smooth, sometimes only striate from the gills showing through.
Surface smooth, its basic colour is dark brown, but it is strongly hygrophanous.
In wet weather it is coloured from olive-brown to brownish-black, in dry weather it is light brown and silky shiny.
spod: Distant, 4–5 mm wide and of varying length.
In young specimens the edge is even, in older ones crenate and ragged.
Narrowly attached, rounded at the stem.
Colour pale grey, ever darker with age.
In mature fruit bodies the gills take on a pink tinge.
trzon: Length 3–6 cm, thickness 3–8 mm.
It is brittle, hollow inside, bent, sometimes flattened.
Surface smooth, of the same colour as the cap.
Base overgrown with whitish mycelium.
podobne: There are several Entoloma species with brown caps.
The most similar are:
Entoloma clypeatum, which is larger and has flesh smelling of flour,
Entoloma sericeum, producing fruit bodies in autumn.

kapelusz: Diameter 7–20 cm, shape at first bell-shaped, then convex and flattened, often with a large umbo, fleshy, sticky when moist, quickly drying, partly hygrophanous.
Surface smooth, bare, at first grey-brown to brownish-yellow, slightly darker in the centre, slightly paler with age, beige or light brown, much darker after drying.
Margin at first inrolled, then wavy, sometimes grooved or tattered.
spod: Broad, bellied, wavy, fairly crowded, at first pale yellow, then pinkish.
Edges the same colour, ragged.
trzon: Height 5–15 cm, thickness 1–3.5 cm, cylindrical, sometimes widening towards the base, stocky, fleshy, at first solid, then spongy.
Surface along its whole length striate-fibrous to almost scaly, white to light brown.
miazsz: In the cap thick, compact, white, smell strongly mealy-rancid, taste unpleasant, mealy-rancid.
podobne: Entoloma whiteae is the largest member of the genus Entoloma.
It is also characterised by a sturdy build.
Young fruit bodies are morphologically similar to Lyophyllum decastes, but it usually grows in clusters, and moreover its gills and spores are whitish, and the spores are not angular.

owocnik: The anamorph forms bulbous sclerotia 70–100 µm in diameter, occurring singly or in small clusters, pale orange, without a cortex, developing on the surface of the host thallus, which as a result is considerably degraded.

The teleomorph forms a pale orange, spread-out, thin basidiocarp up to about 10 mm in diameter, with a granular to flocculose surface, tightly adhering to the surface of the host thallus, with an indefinite margin.
The hymenium consists of one or several layers of basidia on vertically branched, thin-walled hyphae.

Basidia 25–40 × 12–15 mm, distinctly wider than the hyphae supporting them, at first narrowly cylindrical, sometimes with a basal or lateral, ellipsoid probasidial vesicle, at maturity usually becoming club-shaped, sometimes with one thin, transverse septum in the upper 1/3.
No basal clamp connections; basal septum with a dolipore visible under the light microscope.
Each basidium has 4 sterigmata up to 6.5 µm long and 3 µm wide at the base, curved.

Basidiospores 13–17.5 (–18.5) x 8–11.5(–13.5) µm, pear-shaped or teardrop-shaped, often flattened or slightly concave on one side, colourless, smooth, usually without septa, non-amyloid, with a visible truncate apiculus 1.5–3 µm in diameter, sometimes with one thin transverse septum, the wall then clearly narrowed.
No hyphidia, cystidia or other sterile elements of the hymenium.
A fungus growing on a wood stump.
Diameter 2–9 cm, shape disc-like, cup-shaped or goblet-shaped.
It has a short, conical stem.
The sides of the fruit body do not stick to the substrate.
Surface matt, black or brown-black, smooth, after the fruit body ripens folded or covered with pits.
Flesh gelatinous and fairly compact, but during rainy weather or in older age the fruit bodies become deformed.
They may occur singly, or in small clusters (given under the name E. truncata).
podobne: Exidia nigricans is similar, but it forms larger fruit bodies, folded like a brain and stemless, attached to the substrate by their sides.
During maturation they quickly deform and form a mass spreading over the substrate.
Under the microscope these two species are indistinguishable, but DNA studies have shown that they are different species.

owocnik: When young grey, spherical or cup-shaped, later brain-like folded; upper surface finely dotted, dark, grey-brown to black.
When wet it is soft and translucently gelatinous inside, when dried it becomes hard, crust-like.
After rehydration it swells again and becomes gelatinous once more.
Each individual fruit body is attached to the substrate.
Neighbouring fruit bodies merge with one another, sometimes forming large clusters of gelatinous mass.
miazsz: Blackish to brownish, translucent, gelatinous, odourless.
podobne: Exidia pithya.
It also has black, gelatinous fruit bodies, but smaller, flat, and it grows almost exclusively on conifers.
Exidia glandulosa.
It has single, barrel-shaped or saucer-shaped fruit bodies, covered with spines on the outside.

inne: Fruit body spherical, often pitted-folded at the base, gelatinous-soft; young – yellow-brown, old – dark, reddish-brown, dried – black.
From 2 cm in height and width.

owocnik: Diameter 2–9 cm, shape disc-like, cup-shaped or goblet-shaped.
It has a short, conical stem.
The sides of the fruit body do not stick to the substrate.
Surface matt, black or brown-black, smooth, after the fruit body ripens folded or covered with pits.
Flesh gelatinous and fairly compact, but during rainy weather or in older age the fruit bodies become deformed.
They may occur singly, or in small clusters (given under the name E. truncata).
podobne: Exidia nigricans is similar, but it forms larger fruit bodies, folded like a brain and stemless, attached to the substrate by their sides.
During maturation they quickly deform and form a mass spreading over the substrate.
Under the microscope these two species are indistinguishable, but DNA studies have shown that they are different species.

owocnik: Spread out, closely attached to the substrate, leathery, thin.
Surface waxy and slightly shiny.
Morphologically it is very variable.
It takes a shape from circular or oval to irregular.
It is hygrophanous, when wet it becomes gelatinous and translucent, when dry it is whitish, pinkish, slightly violet or greyish.
The whitish colour comes from the spores covering the fruit body, which are easily rubbed off.
After drying it forms a very thin, white, red, or grey-white crust.
podobne: There are several similar species, whose common feature is a fruit body that is spread out and closely adhering to the surface, thin and waxy, whitish or pinkish in colour.
Distinguishing them can be difficult, as they show great morphological variability and also look different when dry and when moist.
The place of occurrence is important.
Exidiopsis calcea occurs mainly on conifers, usually on Norway spruce, but it has also been recorded on aspen.
It usually has a whiter fruit body.
Sebacina grisea also occurs mainly on conifers, especially on silver fir, less often on spruce; it usually has a thicker and less pink fruit body and shorter spores.
Sometimes distinguishing these species is possible only by microscopic examination.

kapelusz: Annual, 10–20 cm wide, 2–6 cm thick.
At first knobbly, then cushion-shaped, finally spatula-shaped, semicircular, kidney-shaped.
Upper surface slightly radiating, streaked and warty, pink or orange-red when young, later blood-red to purple-brown.
Young caps, exuding abundant blood-red juice, look deceptively like animal liver.
