trzon: Thickness up to 0.7 cm, height up to 10 cm.
Irregularly cylindrical, bent, hollow inside.
Colour yellowish with a slightly greenish tinge, covered (especially at the bottom) with brown fibrils.
When damaged it does not change colour.
Stems in a bundle of fruit bodies fused at the bottom.
miazsz: Thin and elastic, colour yellowish or sulphur-yellow, brown at the base of the stem.
Taste very bitter.
When damaged it does not change colour.
podobne: Hypholoma capnoides.
It is edible, has bluish gills, a mild taste and grows only on conifers.
Hypholoma lateritium.
It is larger, has a more intense colouring and grows only on the wood of broadleaved trees.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–9 cm, hemispherical when young, then arched, finally flat.
It is fleshy, smooth and bare.
Sticky in wet weather.
The centre of the cap is brick red, the margins yellow-orange.
At the margins there are fibrous-scaly, whitish-yellowish remains of the veil.
spod: Crowded, at first yellow, then olive-brown, chocolate or olive-black.
trzon: Height 2–4 cm, thickness 1.5–3 mm, cylindrical, with a ring that disappears early.
It is fibrous, pale yellow at the top, brown at the bottom.
miazsz: Yellowish, slightly bitter, without smell.
podobne: Hypholoma capnoides.
It is edible, has poppy-blue gills and occurs on the wood of conifers.
Hypholoma fasciculare does not have a brick-coloured cap, its gills are dirty greenish, it is smaller and more bitter.

kapelusz: Diameter 6–15 (exceptionally up to 30) cm, convex with a broad margin.
Surface dry, smooth, in colour from whitish to cream.
spod: Attached or slightly decurrent, broad, crowded, white.
trzon: Height 6–13 cm, thickness 2–3 cm, cylindrical, smooth or finely fibrous.
Surface white.
Ring absent.
miazsz: Smell sour, slight or sometimes slightly mealy.
Taste mild.

kapelusz: Size reaches up to 15 cm in diameter.
It is bare and smooth, semicircular with inrolled margins in young specimens, dark brown with a reddish tinge or chestnut-brown.
In older specimens the cap is spread out, fairly flat, sometimes with the margins turned upwards.
spod: Slightly notched around the stem.
Colour from pale ochre to olive-yellow.
When damaged they change colour to blue-green.
Pores at first white, later yellow to yellow-greenish.
trzon: Thickness up to 4 cm, height up to 10 cm.
Light brown, with longitudinal, darker streaks.
In young specimens the stem is usually swollen, then cylindrical.
At the site of damage it turns dark blue.
miazsz: Hard, woody in older stems.
White, slightly yellow in older specimens.
When cut it turns slightly blue.
Taste and smell pleasant.
podobne: Young bay boletes can be confused with Tylopilus felleus.
Doubts can be resolved with a taste test (the bitter bolete is bitter).
Older ones, on the other hand, are similar to Gyroporus castaneus, which, however, has a stem hollow with cavities and its flesh does not change colour when cut.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–15 cm, at first hemispherical, later convex, finally cushion-shaped, entirely flesh-red, spotted purple-red, paler at the margin.
spod: 15–25 mm long, bright yellow, quickly turning bluish in the air.
trzon: Height 5–10 cm, thickness 3–6 cm, when young bulbous-swollen to barrel-shaped, later short club-shaped, the same colour as the cap, decorated with a delicate dark purple-red reticulum.
miazsz: Yellow, sometimes wine-red at the base of the stem.
In air it turns blue-green particularly quickly and intensely.
It has a pleasant smell and a mild taste.
wysyp: Spores spindle-shaped, smooth, honey yellow, measuring 10–11 × 5.5–6 μm, spore print olive-brownish.
podobne: Similar is Rubroboletus rhodoxanthus.
It is, however, a rare species, has a whitish or fawn cap and only in places a red tinge. Its flesh also changes colour when damaged, but less intensely.

kapelusz: Diameter 10–25 cm, brown-ochre, in young fruit bodies at first white, smooth and bare.
At first convex with inrolled margins and an umbo in the centre.
On older fruit bodies the cap is funnel-shaped.
spod: First white, then ochre-cream, crowded, thin, slightly or clearly decurrent.
trzon: Height 5–15 cm, thickness 1–4 cm.
Cylindrical, solid, smooth, slightly fibrous, overgrown at the base with white felty mycelium.
It is the same colour as the cap.
Young fruit bodies often have a long stem and a very small cap.
This is because at first the stem grows much faster than the cap.
miazsz: White, firm, not changing colour when cut.
Taste slight, smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spores almost spherical, smooth, colourless, 6–8 × 5–6 µm in diameter.
podobne: The trooping funnel can be confused with the edible Aspropaxillus candidus, or with the much smaller and also edible Infundibulicybe gibba.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–15 cm, arched with a rolled-under margin and an umbo in young fruit bodies, but it quickly becomes concave and funnel-shaped with a straightened margin.
Margin sometimes wavy and speckled.
Cap thin-fleshed, with a smooth surface in pale ochre, ochre-cream or reddish-brown colour; in older fruit bodies the colour fades.
spod: Fairly crowded and running far down the stem, at first white, later yellowish.
trzon: Height 4–10 cm, thickness up to 1 cm, cylindrical, slightly widening at the bottom, soft and elastic, cottony inside in young fruit bodies, hollow in older ones.
Surface bare, whitish or pale yellow, overgrown at the base with white felt.
A characteristic feature is that the colour of the stem is lighter than the colour of the cap.
miazsz: Cream-white, with a slight almond smell, or without smell.
podobne: Infundibulicybe costata,
Paralepista flaccida, which usually has brownish spots on the cap and does not have an umbo.

trzon: Diameter up to 4 cm, at first hemispherical or conical, then flat with a distinct, sharp umbo.
Margin slightly turned in, in young fruit bodies with remnants of the veil, which however quickly disappear.
Surface smooth or slightly felty, dark brown with a hazel tinge, darker in the centre.
Height 3–5 cm, thickness below 0.3–0.6 cm, cylindrical, only slightly thicker at the base.
Surface of the same colour as the cap, but paler, almost cream, delicately frosted.
spod: Sinuately attached with lamellulae, at first grey-beige, then turning brown.
Edges even, fringed.
miazsz: White in the cap, light brown and fibrous in the stem.
Smell indeterminate, taste somewhat earthy.
podobne: Inocybe pseudoasterospora is distinguished by its stem – pale ochre along its whole length, thickened at the base with a small bulb.
Spores with several broad knobs.

kapelusz: Diameter up to 7 cm, shape at first conical, later spread out with a convex centre and a slightly turned-back margin.
Surface dry and fibrous all over except at the top.
As the fruit body matures, the fibrils become more and more visible, especially near the margin, and the cap cracks from the margins.
spod: Slightly sinuately notched at the stem.
Besides full-length gills there are lamellulae.
At first they are dirty white, then grey-ochre, finally brown.
They have even, woolly and white-fringed edges.
trzon: Height 5–9 cm, thickness 0.6–0.8 (1.2) cm, cylindrical in shape, of equal thickness with a bulb with a rim at the base.
Surface in the upper part pale, brownish, sometimes with a red tinge, in the lower part darker, rusty-brown.
Small bulb whitish.
The whole stem is frosted.
miazsz: In the cap and in the small bulb white, in the stem light brown.
It turns yellow under the influence of KOH.
It has a faint smell, according to some similar to the smell of semen, according to others sourish, similar to the smell of earth.
It is tasteless.
podobne: Inocybe rimosa.
It has a light brown cap with a sharper umbo, a whitish stem, and in mature fruit bodies it is entirely radially cracked.
Inocybe maculata.
It is only slightly cracked (the whitish cap skin is not visible beneath the cracks).

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm, at first bell-shaped convex, then flattening out, finally flat and wavy.
Margin inrolled and sharp for a long time, later straight.
Surface dry, fibrillose-fibrous, however without streaks.
Colour beige-rusty with an olive tinge, sometimes distinctly olive-brown.
spod: With short gills, broad, sinuately notched, at first yellow-olive, then rusty-cinnamon.
Edges paler, uneven.
trzon: Height 3–6 cm, thickness 0.3–0.7 cm, cylindrical, at first solid, then hollow, brittle, with a slightly thickened base.
Surface at first whitish, then brownish.
Over its whole length it is covered with fibres, sometimes forming several ring zones.
miazsz: Whitish, lemon-ochre only at the top of the cap, sometimes rusty in the stem.
It has no distinct taste, or it is slightly bitter.
Smell indistinct or slightly musty.
podobne: The bittersweet Inocybe shows great variability in the size of fruit bodies, the degree of fibrillosity of their caps and stems, and the size and shape of spores.
Albertini and Schwein report that there are summer varieties with caps with dark gills and autumn varieties with smoother caps.
In Poland the variability depends mainly on habitat conditions.
On sandy soils in the lowlands, rusty-brown specimens grow, with thinner stems and spores up to 10 µm long.
In the mountains more stocky forms occur, with a thicker stem and a more fibrillose cap.
Mallocybe terrigena is similar.
It is distinguished by protruding, dense, brown scales on a yellow stem.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–4 (6) cm, shape at first hemispherical, later flatly spread with a small umbo.
Margin at first rolled under, then straight and ragged.
The partial veil disappears fairly quickly.

Surface of young fruit bodies felty-fibrous, nut-brown in colour, in older ones becoming fibrous-funnel-shaped or streaked with large scales at the cap margin, and the original colour persists only at the top of the cap, the margins become paler.
spod: Attached to the stem, mixed (in addition to full-length gills there are short gills).
At first they are whitish, then grey-ochre, finally light brown.
Edges weakly fringed.
trzon: Height 2–5 cm, thickness 0.3–0.5 cm.
Surface at first whitish, then wax-coloured, sometimes light reddish-brownish.
It is villose-ciliate, and in the lower part covered with adhering fibrils.
miazsz: Whitish; above the gills there is a hyaline streak in it.
It has a sourish taste.
podobne: There are several similar species of Inocybe: Inocybe proximella, Inocybe lacera and Inocybe lanuginosa.
They differ little in colour and in details of the structure of the scales and fibres covering the cap and stem.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–5 cm, at first conical, sometimes irregular, then flatly spread out with a distinct umbo.
Margin thin and straight.
Small scales completely absent, the surface is covered with silky, pink-red fibrils, which sometimes form striation or delicate veining.
Colour from whitish through cream-pink to peach, only at the top sometimes shading into flesh-orange.
In young fruit bodies remnants of a hanging, cobweb-like veil are visible.
spod: Slightly attached or almost free, thin, at first light rusty, then dark olive-rusty with red spots.
Edges frosted.
trzon: Height 1.5–7 cm, thickness 0.2–0.1 cm, cylindrical, sometimes bent, with a margined bulb.
Surface delicately fibrillose, pink in the bulb, white and frosted at the top.
miazsz: In the cap fleshy; after damage turning pink in the stem and under the skin, turning rusty red in the stem.
Young fruit bodies have a fruity smell, older ones a smell of semen.
Taste mild.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–3 cm, at first bell-shaped convex, then flat with a small umbo.
Margin thin, straight, or very slightly turned under, striate.
Surface dry, smooth, or delicately fibrillose or scaly, in colour from yellowish with an olive-beige tinge to ochre-lemon, usually darker – brown – in the centre.
spod: Notched with a sinus or almost free, thin, with lamellulae.
At first beige or yellowish, then dirty grey or light brown.
Edges whitish and fringed with fine hairs.
trzon: Height 2–5 cm, thickness 0.3–0.5 cm, cylindrical, thin.
Below the soil surface it has a distinct, unmargined bulb covered with white mycelium.
Frosted under the cap.
Surface colour from white to light ochre with a delicate pinkish or ochre tinge, only the small bulb is white.
miazsz: Whitish, sometimes with a glassy zone above the gills.
No distinct taste, in the stem a smell of bitter almonds.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–6 cm, in young specimens conical-convex with a small blunt umbo, in older ones flat.
Cap margin inrolled, later straightened.
Surface dry, smooth-fibrous in young specimens, fibrillose in older ones, finally fibrillose-scaly.
Scales often (especially at the top of the cap) standing out.
Colour from grey-brown through ochre-brown to brown.
Remnants of the cortina persist at the margin for a long time.
spod: Young ones dirty white, older ones flesh brown, finally brown.
Gill edges paler.
At the stem they are notched with a sinus.
trzon: Height 3–5 cm, thickness 3–5 mm, cylindrical, solid, without a bulb, sometimes with a slightly narrowed base.
Surface of the same colour as the cap, or slightly paler and covered with fine fibrils.
miazsz: In the cap it is white to white-cream, in the stem brownish.
It has a delicate taste and a smell similar to semen.
podobne: Inocybe napipes.
It differs in its radially fibrous cap and a distinct bulb on the stem.
Mallocybe dulcamara.
The cap has an olive tinge and does not have tattered, protruding fibrils.
Inocybe lanuginosa.
It has a darker colour and a stem covered with fibres and scales.
It grows in damp places.

kapelusz: Diameter 2.5–3.5 cm, at first conical or hemispherical, then flatly spread with a small umbo, more rarely with a depressed centre.
Veil quickly disappearing.
Margin at first turned under, then straight and finally even slightly bent upwards.
Surface woolly-fibrous, in older specimens scaly, with distinctly protruding scales.
Colour from fawn-brown through light brown to brown, usually darker in the centre.
spod: Notched in a sinus-like manner, decurrent with a small tooth, with lamellulae.
At first grey-beige, then buff or ochre-brown.
Edges fringed white or light brown.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness 0.4–1 cm, more or less cylindrical, slightly bent.
Surface fibrous, sometimes tufted, the same colour as the cap, darker towards the base.
miazsz: At first whitish, then light brownish, fibrous in the stem.
Taste indistinct.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–4.5 cm, at first conical, then flatly spread out with an umbo.
Margin at first slightly inrolled, then straightening and bending upwards.
Surface smooth or somewhat felty in the centre, yellowish or ochre, fibrous-streaked and pale near the margin.
spod: Sinuately notched, with short gills.
At first pale grey, then ochre, but always with a grey tinge.
Edges delicately ciliate.
trzon: Height 3–6 cm, thickness 0.6–0.8 cm, cylindrical, with a small bulb deeply embedded in the ground that easily breaks off.
Surface in young fruit bodies whitish, then in colour from yellowish to pale ochre.
It is frosted over its whole length.
miazsz: In the cap whitish, in the stem coloured from whitish to cream and fibrous.
Smell of dust.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–4 cm, conical with a rolled-under margin in young fruit bodies, in older ones spread flat with an umbo and a straightened margin.
The top of the cap has a felty-woolly, dark brown surface, which towards the cap margin passes into a fibrous, streaked and light brown, even ochre one.
spod: Slightly decurrent on the stem, with the edge densely whitish frosted.
At first they are whitish, later darker – slightly greyish, finally ochre-brown.
Besides full-length gills there are lamellulae.
trzon: Height 5–9 cm, thickness 0.3–0.8 cm, cylindrical, but slightly flattened, widening towards the base to 10 mm (without a distinct bulb).
Surface pale, almost white in the upper and lower part, brown in the middle.
In the upper part almost smooth, in the lower part fibrillose.
miazsz: Whitish in the cap, ochre-yellowish in the stem, and brownish at the base of the stem.
It has a faint, slightly sourish smell.
podobne: Inocybe acuta.
It is distinguished from it by the brown colour of the middle part of the stem, a slight widening of its base and frequent occurrence among mosses.
Inocybe mixtilis, which has a yellow-brown cap without a distinct umbo and has no brown tints on the stem.

owocnik: Annual, attached to the substrate sideways, occurring singly or overlapping like roof tiles in small groups.
A single one is mostly up to 10 cm wide, rarely up to 35 cm, and up to 10 cm thick.
Its upper (hymenial) surface in young fruit bodies is smooth, even and matt, coloured from yellow-red to apricot, then becomes reddish-brown, somewhat folded, covered with warts and hairs.
They are bristly-felty, in wet weather slimy and sticking together in bundles.
In old specimens the upper surface becomes bare, rough, cracked, without zoning.
Margin in young fruit bodies sharp, protruding and sulphur yellow, in older ones yellow-brown, blunt, thin, wavy.
Flesh at first soft, spongy and juicy, yellowish to ochre in colour, with time rusty-brown, hard, dry and zoned, in dried specimens brittle, radially fibrous.
It is up to 8 cm thick.
When damaged it quickly turns brown.
Hymenophore tubular, sulphur yellow in young fruit bodies, ochre with age, finally grey-ochre.
There are pits in it 2–4 mm in diameter that exude a watery, bitter substance.
It has a pleasant smell and a slightly sourish taste.
It produces two types of fruit bodies: an asexual and a sexual form.
The asexual fruit body (anamorph) takes the form of a perennial, knobbly, warty, cracked growth attached by its side to the tree.
It is very strongly fused with it.
The growth has irregular shapes and can reach a diameter of up to 50 cm.
Often the tree trunk near the growth becomes thickened.
The outer layer of the fruit body is dried, hard, flaky, charred and slag-like.
Surface matt, coloured blackish-brown or black-navy, in fresh cracks with a ginger-brown tint.
In these cracks chlamydospores are produced asexually, by means of which the fungus spreads until the host dies.
They also act as resting structures.
After the tree dies, the fungus produces a second form of fruit body, the sexual fruit body (teleomorph), which produces sexual spores – basidiospores.
This fruit body is, however, hard to observe, because it develops under the bark of a tree or between layers of wood.
It is annual, flat, spread out (resupinate).
It grows next to outgrowths, is 5–10 mm thick, up to several tens of centimetres wide and covers the trunk over a length of up to several metres.
At first it is soft, with a fleshy-leathery consistency, then increasingly harder – corky and brittle.
On its thickened margin there are clusters of mycelium that pry up the bark of the tree, enabling the fruit body to grow.
At first these clusters are white and thin, then dark and thickening.
The sexual fruit body causes the trunk to split, which allows the basidiospores to escape through the resulting cracks.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm, conical or bell-shaped in young specimens, later increasingly spread out.
In the centre it has a rounded umbo.
On the margin remnants of the veil fibrils are often visible.
Margin rolled under in young fruit bodies, turned back in older ones.
Surface delicately covered radially with fibrils (streaked), but this is clearly visible only in dry weather.
In young fruit bodies it may be silky and smooth, and the fibrils are visible only right at the margin.
Colour uniformly golden or yellow-ochre, and straw yellow in dry weather.
Often on the cap margin, and sometimes also over its whole surface, small remnants of the cortina can be noticed.
spod: Usually somewhat notched in a sinus-like manner, sometimes almost free.
Colour from pale lemon through dirty olive to greyish.
Edges of the gills uneven, lighter.
trzon: Height 3–5 cm, thickness 4–7 mm, cylindrical, solid, brittle.
In young fruit bodies it is whitish, then increasingly darker, finally pale yellow-brownish, right under the stem it stays whitish.
Surface delicately dusted, base fibrous with a small bulb edged in white.
miazsz: Thin, whitish or light olive, the smell of young fruit bodies similar to fruit, of older ones to semen.
podobne: Inocybe rimosa.
It is distinctly differentiated from it by a markedly thickened bulb at the base of the stem.
Inocybe hirtella.
It does not have a margined bulb, the cap is finely scaly, and the stem is dusted over its whole length.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–9 cm, shape conically convex.
Margin thin, inrolled in young fruit bodies, straight and radially cracked in older ones.
Surface smooth, silky and dry, without small scales, but covered with delicate fibres.
In young fruit bodies it is white or pale cream, but it quickly becomes brick-red and even vermilion-red, especially in the centre of the cap.
The margins are paler.
spod: Broad, thin, fairly crowded, sinuately notched or free at the stem.
At first they are whitish, then dark olive-rusty.
When pressed they turn red.
Edges uneven, frosted.
trzon: Height 5–20 cm, thickness 0.8–2 cm, cylindrical, solid, without a bulb at the base, or at most with a small bulb.
Surface covered with whitish, pink or cinnabar fibrils, top frosted.
miazsz: White in the cap, strongly turning pink in the stem.
It has a pleasant, fruity smell and a mild taste.
podobne: Inocybe godeyi.
It has a stem with a distinct bulb
More brown specimens of the brick fibrecap may be similar to Inocybe rimosa, but the latter has not even a trace of reddish colour on the cap.
Calocybe gambosa.
Young fruit bodies are the most similar.
Older ones differ clearly in the colour of the gills

owocnik: Annual bracket fungus attached sideways to the substrate.
A single fruit body is fan-shaped or semicircular, up to 20 cm long, up to 14 cm wide and up to 2 cm thick.
Upper surface of young fruit bodies felty, of older ones bare, with a slight gloss.
It is concentrically zoned.
Young fruit bodies are red-brown or brown, older ones become violet-black from the resin covering them.
The margin is thin and always of a paler colour, often wavy and bent downwards.
spod: It develops only in the final phase of the development of the fruit body.
The tubes are about 10 mm long.
Pores round or polygonal and very small; there are 4–6 of them per 1 mm.
At first they are whitish, then increasingly darker, brown in older fruit bodies.
They darken when pressed.
miazsz: It is about 1 cm thick.
In young fruit bodies it is white and fleshy, in mature ones it becomes ochre and hard.
podobne: Ischnoderma resinosum.
It occurs on the wood of deciduous trees.
It has thicker and paler fruit bodies, and their upper surface is smoother.
There are no microscopic differences between the two species.
Bondarzewia mesenterica, which also grows on conifers, but only on their roots.

owocnik: Annual bracket fungus attached sideways to the substrate.
A single fruit body is bracket-shaped or semicircular, 6–15(30) cm wide and 1–2(3) cm thick.
The margin is thick, rounded and of a paler colour.
Upper surface of young fruit bodies felty, of older ones bare, with a slight gloss.
It is coloured from rusty red through red-brown to black-brown.
Older fruit bodies are darker.
The hymenophore often exudes dark drops.
Under the skin there is a thin resinous layer of rusty colour.
spod: It develops only in the final phase of the development of the fruit body.
The tubes are 10–15 mm long, their pores are fine (0.15–0.25 mm in diameter), in colour from white to ochre.
When pressed they change colour to reddish-brown.
miazsz: Juicy, fleshy-fibrous, several times thicker than the tube layer.
After drying it becomes corky and brittle.
podobne: Ischnoderma benzoinum.
Occurs on the wood of conifers, especially on spruce and pine.
It has thinner and darker fruit bodies.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–7 cm.
After rain cinnamon-brownish and slimy, during drought it dries from the centre towards the margins, so that the centre is pale ochre, the margin brownish, striate.
Semicircular when young, with age completely flat, smooth, bare, with a blunt umbo in the centre.
spod: Covered with a veil when young, crowded, at first whitish, then yellow-brown, finally rusty brown.
They are closely spaced and attached to the stem, sometimes slightly decurrent on it.
trzon: 5–7 cm long, 5–8 mm thick, cylindrical, bent.
It has a colour similar to the cap.
It is fibrous-tough and hollow inside.
In the upper part it has a leathery ring with numerous protruding small scales.
Below the ring on the stem there are dark brown small hairs, above the ring the stem is smooth or delicately striate.
miazsz: In the cap thin, whitish, soft and watery, in the stem hard, rusty-brown.
Taste slight, smell pleasant, resembling freshly cut wood.
wysyp: Spores 6–7 × 4–4.5 µm in diameter, egg-shaped, smooth, pale brown.
podobne: The poisonous Galerina marginata is very similar.
These two species can be told apart only by the appearance of the stem (in the Galerina species it is covered with white small hairs of the veil, which form a zigzag pattern).
Moreover, it grows mainly on stumps of conifers.
Hypholoma capnoides has gills with a bluish tinge.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–6 cm, in young specimens hemispherical or bell-shaped with an inrolled margin and a depression in the centre, in older ones becoming arched, finally flat and funnel-shaped with wavy margins.
It is hygrophanous.
Skin smooth, in adult specimens delicately flaky and with slightly grooved margins.
In wet weather it is violet or brown-violet in colour, in dry weather, or in older specimens, whitish-violet.
spod: Thick, distant, often wavy.
They are broadly adnate to the stem or only slightly decurrent.
In young specimens violet, later dusted whitish with spores.
Even when the fruit bodies are faded, their gills remain violet.
trzon: Height 3–12 cm and thickness 3–10 mm, hollow inside, fibrous, slightly thickened at the bottom.
Colour the same as the cap.
miazsz: Watery, slightly violet in wet weather, pink-brownish in dry weather, with an indistinct smell and taste.
podobne: There is a possibility of confusion with the poisonous Mycena pura.
Difference: a less slender fruit body and a characteristic smell of radish or turnip.
Laccaria amethystina may also be confused with the lilac variety of the poisonous Inocybe geophylla, which differs in the umbo on the cap and its unpleasant smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–5 cm, convex when young with an inrolled margin, later flat, finally concave and wavy-bent.
Colour orange, rusty brown, flesh pink or pink, sometimes, but rarely, orange-ochre or olive-ochre.
It is hygrophanous; when moist it is translucently grooved, when dry the grooving is not visible.
spod: Distantly spaced, broadly adnate, salmon or brown-reddish in colour.
Sometimes decurrent at the stem.
trzon: Height 2–8 cm, cylindrical, slender, often twisted, longitudinally slightly fibrous, overgrown with white mycelium at the base.
Colour the same as the cap.
miazsz: Pale reddish in the cap, stronger, more pink in the stem.
Taste and smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spores round to broadly elliptical, 7-10 µm in size, with spines up to 2 µm long.
podobne: Laccaria proxima.
It has a larger fruit body, with gills usually pink,
Laccaria bicolor, which has a violet mycelium at the base of the stem.
Cortinarius semisanguineus, which has crowded gills and a rusty-brown spore print.
Poisonous.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–8 cm, when young hemispherical, then convex, finally spread out, flat with a slightly concave centre, sometimes bent in waves.
In wet weather it is striate, in dry weather there is no striation, and the grooving of the margins is also invisible.
Surface of young fruit bodies delicately felty, later rough, covered with small, protruding scales.
Colour from yellowish-reddish through orange-red and flesh-brown to brownish-red.
In dry weather it fades and becomes pale ochre.
Quite often the cap cracks radially along the gills.
spod: They are 3–10 mm wide and attached to the stem.
Colour pink or flesh-reddish.
Besides the main gills there are intermediate lamellae.
trzon: Height 6–12 cm, thickness 5–8 mm, cylindrical in shape, often bent, thickened at the base, at first solid, later hollow.
Surface strongly fibrillose, sometimes cracked, colour red-brown or dark brown.
The base is darker than the rest of the stem and covered with white hyphae of the mycelium
miazsz: Whitish with a flesh-brownish tint, hard in the cap, cartilaginous in the stem.
Taste mild, indistinct, smell faint, indeterminate.
podobne: Laccaria bicolor.
Its most characteristic feature is the long-persisting violet colour of the stem base,
Laccaria laccata.
It is smaller and has more distant gills.
Some Laccaria species are morphologically hard to tell apart.
Laccaria laccata is the most similar to Laccaria proxima.

Sometimes it can be distinguished by its habitat – it is very common and grows in various types of forests and under various trees, whereas the larger Laccaria species only under pines; sometimes it can be distinguished by its size and outer structure – it is distinctly smaller, its cap usually does not exceed 4 cm in diameter, and it has more distant gills, usually of the same colour as the cap.
However, a reliable distinction of these species is sometimes possible only under the microscope.
The spores of Laccaria laccata are spherical or almost spherical and have distinct spines, the spores of Laccaria proxima are elliptical and have fine spines.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–8 cm, bell-shaped in young specimens, then broadly spread out, completely flat in old age, but not depressed.
Its colour ranges from cream-ochre through orange-brown to rusty brown.
Its surface is covered with fibrils and scales, and in older specimens with fibrils.
In young specimens remains of the veil hang from the cap margin.
spod: In young specimens grey-yellow, then brown-black.
They are often violet-grey in colour.
A characteristic feature of this species is that the gills exude droplets of liquid in which black-brown spores collect.
trzon: Height 5–12 cm, thickness 5–8 mm.
It is cylindrical, hollow, longitudinally fibrous and covered with fibrils.
It is coloured from ochre to brown and has a faintly marked fibrous ring zone.
Above this zone it is bare.
miazsz: Pale grey-brown, without a distinct smell.
podobne: Lacrymaria pyrotricha has a lighter, red-orange cap and a ring often occurs on its stem.
It occurs in mountain spruce forests.
It can also be confused with the smaller and common Psathyrella candolleana.

kapelusz: Diameter 6–12 (up to 15) cm, whitish-ochre or ochre-yellowish in colour, sometimes with darker, ochre-orange, concentrically zoned, with a depressed centre.
Skin on the surface felty in young fruit bodies, becoming greasy at high air humidity.
spod: Gilled, gills at first cream in colour, later ochre-yellowish, forked near the stem and connected by anastomoses.
Basidia two-spored.
trzon: Fairly short, whitish in young fruit bodies, ochre after maturing.
miazsz: It is built of roundish cells which cause its specific brittleness and irregular fracture.
It exudes white milk that does not change colour and has an acrid taste.
podobne: Among the fungi with morphologically similar fruit bodies, Lactarius zonarius is mentioned.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–20 cm, early funnel-shaped, with an inrolled and generally bent margin, older ones also lobed or coarsely crenate.
Margin rolled under for a long time and usually not straightening out completely.
It is uniformly olive-grey to grey-green and only sometimes distinctly, circularly banded; when young – strongly slimy – when older usually dry and shiny.
spod: Fairly crowded, sometimes forked, narrow and narrowed both at the margin and at the stem.
Intermediate lamellae are present.
At first the gills are white, later they become straw-coloured, finally light ochre.
In wet weather they weep.
When pressed they change colour to olive-brown.
In older specimens the gill edge becomes spotted olive-rusty.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness 1–2.5 cm, cylindrical or tapering towards the base, at first solid, later cottony or hollow.
In dry weather the surface is shiny, in wet weather sticky.
It is paler than the cap.
In older specimens the stem is covered along its whole length with shallow pits.
miazsz: Thick and hard.
It is white, only under the cap skin does it have a faint olive tinge.
In older specimens it turns brown.
Taste acrid, no distinct smell.
mleczko: It is exuded abundantly, white or watery white.
It does not change colour.
Very burning in taste.
podobne: Lactarius glutinopalens grows under firs, mostly on calcareous soils.
It has an even slimier, uniformly light grey cap, and also a more acrid white milk.
Under birches grows Lactarius vietus, which has a more violet-grey cap, also slimy, and a more acrid white milk that turns grey-green as it dries.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm, dark orange-brown or red-brown in colour.
In the centre of the cap there is always a fairly distinct umbo, and a depression around it.
In young specimens the cap is arched, then spread out.
Margins crenate and delicately wrinkled.
Covered with a dry, bare and matt skin without concentric stripes.
spod: Gilled, gills crowded, only slightly decurrent on the stem, at first light flesh-reddish in colour, when mature red-brownish, during spore deposit with a white bloom of spores.
Brown spots form when pressed.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness up to 1 cm, cylindrical, sometimes flattened.
Dark red-brown in colour, blackening at the base during ripening, hollow inside.
miazsz: With a mild, sometimes bitterish taste and a smell reminiscent of camphor or bugs (Hemiptera), and after maturing or during drying of lovage (Levisticum sp.) or chicory (Cichorium sp.).
mleczko: Fairly abundant, distant, watery white.
It has a mild taste, but leaves a bitterish aftertaste.
podobne: The characteristic features of Lactarius camphoratus are the dark colour of the cap and the spicy smell during drying.
Among fungi with morphologically similar fruit bodies the following are mentioned:
Lactarius helvus.
Liver milkcap.
It differs in the absence of a characteristic smell, flesh sulphur-yellow on the cut surface, and its milk turning yellow.

kapelusz: Diameter 8–15 cm, fleshy, with a strongly concave centre and a strongly rolled-under margin, from which gelatinised, fringe-like fragments of the veil hang.
Surface yellowish white.
spod: Slightly decurrent, creamy pink.
trzon: Short, thick, slightly rough.
miazsz: Yellowish, with a lemon smell and an acrid taste.
Milk white, when cut it immediately turns sulphur yellow, but does not give off an unpleasant smell.
podobne: Lactarius resimus has milk that behaves similarly, but the cap surface is white with yellowish spots.
Lactarius pubescens is smaller.
Lactarius scrobiculatus has a more strongly pitted stem.
Lactarius torminosus has white milk that does not change colour, and the fruit body has a smell of turpentine.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–12 cm, flesh-reddish in colour or in various shades of orange, sometimes with a touch of green.
Surface concentrically zoned, sometimes pitted-spotted.
In young fruit bodies the cap is convex, maturing concave, with a shallow depression in the centre, in old specimens funnel-shaped, for a long time with inrolled margins.
Covered with skin that is slimy in high air humidity.
spod: Gilled, gills orange-yellowish, similar to the cap, of different lengths (mixed), straight attached or slightly decurrent on the stem, thin and brittle.
When damaged they take on a slightly greenish colour.
trzon: Length 3–7 cm and 1–2.5 cm in diameter, the colour of the cap or paler, with darker pit-like spots (otherwise smooth), saturated with milk.
Cylindrical, at first solid, then hollow, narrowed at the base.
miazsz: Built of roundish cells, which cause its specific brittleness and irregular fracture.
Pale orange in colour, compact, brittle in mature fruit bodies, saturated with bright orange milk.
When damaged it turns green.
It has a slightly bitterish, astringent taste and a sweetish, fruity odour.
mleczko: Orange, gradually fading and then taking on a green colour when exposed to air.
Mild in taste, but leaves a bitter aftertaste.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–10 cm, arched in young specimens, then flat with a concave centre, funnel-shaped in old specimens.
The margin remains inrolled for a long time.
Colour reddish-orange.
In wet weather the skin is slimy, in dry weather shiny and frosted.
On the cap concentric, darker streaks, sometimes faintly visible.
After frosts the cap turns green
spod: Red-orange, brittle, fairly crowded and slightly decurrent on the stem.
When damaged they turn green.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness 1–2.5 cm, cylindrical, hard.
At first it is solid, but it quickly becomes hollow.
Colour red-orange, green-spotted.
No pits on the stem.
miazsz: It is cream, but the milk stains it orange.
Under the cap skin it is sometimes strongly grey-blue.
It has a pleasant, fruity smell and an acrid taste, but older specimens are mild in taste.
mleczko: It flows out fairly abundantly.
It is orange and does not change colour in the air for a long time, only after about 15 min does it become wine-red.
podobne: There are several similar Lactarius species.
For mushroom pickers confusing them is not very important, because all of them are edible.
Lactarius deliciosus.
It has more distinct striations on the cap and grows under pines.
Turns green only after damage
Lactarius salmonicolor.
It has orange juice that does not change colour and a cap without a trace of greenish colouring.
It grows under firs.
Lactarius porninsis.
It has a milky-white juice and grows only under larches.
Lactarius sanguifluus.
Juice wine-red, cap with an admixture of green.

kapelusz: Diameter 5 to 15 cm, shape at first flat-convex, later flat with a wide depression, sometimes with a low umbo.
Margin inrolled, straightens slowly and not completely, usually remaining slightly turned under.
Surface smooth, dry and matt.
In dry weather it sometimes becomes granular, and in older specimens it even cracks into small fields.
The skin cannot be peeled off.
It is uniformly coloured, without banding; in dry weather it is ochre-pink or fawn-pink, even with a violet tinge, in wet weather with a rusty or orange tinge.
spod: Crowded, with short gills, sometimes forked at the stem and forming anastomoses.
They are sharp both at the margin and at the stem.
At first they are whitish-yellowish, later ochre-yellow with a lemon or grey tinge.
trzon: Height 4–13 cm, thickness 0.5–4 cm, cylindrical in shape.
At first solid, later hollow.
Surface smooth, sometimes woolly, and in the top part granular-villose.
It is slightly paler than on the cap: red-ochre or yellowish-red.
miazsz: Fairly thick, somewhat brittle, ochre-reddish, sometimes with a narrow, watery band above the gills.
Smell similar to chicory or lovage (Maggi).
Taste mild, spicy.
mleczko: It flows weakly, and from older specimens not at all.
It is almost watery.
In taste it is mild, but has a bitterish aftertaste and a spicy aroma.
podobne: Lactarius camphoratus, with a similar smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–12 cm.
Convex when young with a depression in the middle and strongly inrolled, shaggy-woolly margins.
Skin when wet a little sticky, drying quickly.
Colour whitish, pale pink, yellowish or cream with spots, but without concentric zones.
spod: Narrow and very crowded, slightly decurrent.
Colour whitish, then cream with a salmon tinge.
trzon: Height 2–5 cm, thickness 1–2 cm, cylindrical, hollow, narrowed at the ground and hollow inside.
Colour whitish, with a flesh-pink sheen.
miazsz: Built of roundish cells, which cause its specific brittleness (as in all Russulaceae) and irregular fracture.
It is white, brittle, and does not change colour when cut.
It changes colour to yellow only while the fungus is drying.
Under the action of FeSO4 it changes colour to grey-yellow.
mleczko: White, not changing colour after exuding.
In older fruit bodies it flows weakly.
In taste strongly burning.
wysyp: Spores egg-shaped, colourless (hyaline), measuring 6.5–8.5 × 5.5–6.5 μm, with a finely warty-reticulate surface, without a germ pore, amyloid.
Both on the edge and on the side of the gills there are numerous spindle-shaped cystidia measuring about 40 × 7.5 μm.
podobne: The most similar is Lactarius torminosus, which also occurs under birches.
It differs in colour (it has a stronger pink tinge) and in the distinct zoning of the cap.
The somewhat similar Lactarius chrysorrheus does not have a hairy cap margin and occurs under oaks.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–8 cm, in young fruit bodies convex, then flat, after maturing slightly depressed or funnel-shaped, always without an umbo.
Margin at first inrolled, then wavy.
Surface dry, matt, coloured from reddish-brown through cinnamon-brown to flesh-brown, sometimes with delicate concentric stripes.
In dry weather it fades.
spod: Gilled, gills fairly crowded, decurrent.
At first they are whitish, later grey-yellow, finally cinnamon-brown.
On their edges there are brown spots; in mature fruit bodies they are dusted with spores.
trzon: Height 3–10 cm, thickness 0.6–1.7 cm, cylindrical.
Surface smooth, of a similar colour to the cap, red at the base.
When pressed it changes colour to brown-red.
miazsz: It is built of roundish cells which cause its specific brittleness and irregular fracture.
Taste mild, sometimes a slightly bitter smell reminiscent of cod liver oil or true bugs (Hemiptera).
mleczko: Young fruit bodies exude milk abundantly, older ones weakly.
It is white with a cream tint, mild in taste, but after longer tasting it leaves a bitterish aftertaste.
podobne: Among the fungi with morphologically similar fruit bodies, the following species are mentioned: Lactarius subdulcis, Lactarius lacunarum, Lactarius rufus, Lactarius rubrocinctus, Lactarius camphoratus.

kapelusz: Young – hemispherical and umbilicate, early broadly funnel-shaped with an inrolled margin, pure white, faintly streaked; young – strongly slimy; turning yellow when pressed. 8–15 cm in diameter.
spod: Cream-white; old ones with orange spots; narrow, thick and crowded, fully attached to the stem and forked.
trzon: Lemon-yellow, delicately mossy, with dark, watery-spotted pits; very thick and short.
miazsz: White, fairly hard, with milk of a very acrid taste, white in air, after about 10 seconds turning sulphur yellow.
podobne: It is confused with Lactarius scrobiculatus, which is much more common in Poland, but which has a pale lemon-yellow cap with clearly visible zones.
Lactarius citriolens is also similar, but it is distinguished by its lemon smell and often pitted stem.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–8 cm, broadly conical with an inrolled margin when young, later flatly arched (usually with an umbo in the centre), finally somewhat funnel-shaped.
Colour uniformly red-brown, skin smooth and without striation.
spod: About 5 mm wide, crowded and slightly decurrent on the stem.
Yellowish in young specimens, then pale cream, flesh-ochre in older ones.
They often have red speckles.
In older specimens they are dusted with white spores.
trzon: Height 3–12 cm, width 8–18 mm.
It is cylindrical and brittle, spongy in young specimens, then hollow.
Colour at first whitish, then light red-brown.
miazsz: Fairly thin, red-brown in colour.
During drying it gives off a strong spicy smell.
mleczko: It flows out fairly abundantly.
It is sparse, watery white, mild in taste, but leaves a bitter aftertaste.
podobne: There are many Lactarius species with a brown cap.
The most similar is Lactarius hysginus, but it has a cap with a greasy surface.
Lactarius camphoratus is also similar.
It can be distinguished by its smell (it smells of chicory or Maggi seasoning) and by its milk with a mild taste.
The rufous milkcap is most easily distinguished from these species by the pointed umbo in the centre of the cap, the burning taste and its mass occurrence.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–15 cm, convex in young specimens, then flat with a concave centre.
Surface orange-yellow, peach-yellow or orange in colour, concentrically zoned with red-orange bands.
In wet weather wine-brown spots may appear.
There is no green colour, only in older fruit bodies may a greenish tinge appear.
Margin rolled under and slightly frosted, but in older fruit bodies it becomes smooth.
spod: Slightly decurrent, moderately crowded, sometimes forking at the stem.
In young fruit bodies they are pale ochre with an orange tinge.
When damaged they do not turn green, at most they become more red.
trzon: Height 3–6 cm, thickness 1–2.5 cm, cylindrical, brittle.
At first it is solid, but it quickly becomes hollow.
Colour as in the cap, surface delicately frosted.
miazsz: Cream-coloured; when damaged, orange, somewhat bitter milk appears immediately.
After about 10 minutes it changes colour to vermilion, after 1–2 hours to orange-brown or wine-red.
It gives off a faint, fruity smell.
podobne: There are several very similar Lactarius species.
Mushroom pickers usually do not distinguish them, and distinguishing them by appearance alone is difficult, and sometimes even impossible.
These are: Lactarius deliciosus, Lactarius deterrimus, Lactarius porninsis, Lactarius sanguifluus and Lactarius semisanguineus.

The most characteristic features of Lactarius salmonicolor are: the place of occurrence (under firs), orange juice (in small amounts), a fruit body without traces of green colour and not turning green after damage.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–7 cm, at first convex with a conical umbo and a turned-under margin, later gradually flattening, finally flat with a straight margin, sometimes shortly crenate and slimy.
Surface smooth, dull, uniformly coloured, without streaks, at first red-brown, chestnut, then paling, more fawn.
spod: Crowded, with short gills, at first whitish, then pale ochre with a coffee tinge, turning grey-reddish after damage.
trzon: Height 5–7 cm and diameter 0.3–1 cm, cylindrical, sometimes channelled in older specimens.
Surface at first pale yellowish, but quickly taking on the colour of the cap, with mycelium at the base.
miazsz: Whitish-flesh-coloured with a reddish tint, darker in the stem.
Taste mild, smell similar to that of bugs (Hemiptera).
The milk is at first released abundantly, is watery white or white, does not change colour, is at first mild in taste, but after some time slightly bitter and acrid.
podobne: Lactarius aurantiacus has milk with an indistinct smell, without a bitterish aftertaste, and grows in coniferous forests.
Also similar is Lactarius quietus.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm, at first flat, but quickly spread out and depressed, usually with a small umbo.
Margin thin, stays rolled under for a long time.
Surface matt when dry, shiny when moist, sometimes rough.
Colour orange-rufous with a reddish tinge, sometimes cinnamon-brown.
spod: Broadly attached, cream in young specimens, later clay-pink.
trzon: Height 2–8 cm, thickness 3–10 mm, cylindrical or club-shaped, at first solid, later hollow.
Colour at first rusty-brown, later ochre, cinnamon, finally dark brick-red.
Paler in the upper part.
miazsz: Built of roundish cells, which cause its specific brittleness (as in all Russulaceae) and irregular fracture.
It usually has a mild, but sometimes somewhat acrid or bitter taste.
mleczko: In young fruit bodies it flows out abundantly, in older ones hardly at all.
It is watery white, and on the flesh it changes to a sulphur colour. At first it has a mild taste, but leaves a bitter aftertaste on the tongue.
podobne: There are several species of small milkcaps similar in outward appearance.
The place of occurrence and the taste and colour change of the milk play an important role in telling them apart.

The similar Lactarius decipiens grows under oaks, and its milk is very acrid in taste and turns pale pink; Lactarius aurantiacus grows higher in the mountains, only under spruces, and its milk does not change colour.
Among fungi with morphologically similar fruit bodies, Lactarius obscuratus, which develops in the presence of alders, is also mentioned.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–10 (up to 15) cm, with a central depression, covered with a felty skin that becomes slightly sticky in high air humidity.
The cap margin is mostly inrolled, covered with woolly fibrils hanging from it.
Cap colour flesh-pink, brown-red, in older specimens fading to orange-ochre.
spod: Gilled, gills light cream or white, with smooth edges, closely spaced (with lamellulae), slightly decurrent on the stem.
trzon: Cylindrical, 4–8 cm long and about 1.2 cm in diameter, pale pink, ochre-pink or white, solid in young fruit bodies, later hollow inside.
miazsz: Built of roundish cells, which cause its specific brittleness and irregular fracture.
White, hard, with a fruity or turpentine-like smell and an acrid, burning taste.
Under the action of FeSO4 it becomes grey-yellowish.
mleczko: At first it flows out abundantly.
It is white and does not change colour in the air. It burns strongly on the tongue and in the throat.
podobne: It is very similar to the edible Lactarius deliciosus, which however does not have woolly fibrils on the cap, has a mild taste, and its milk is orange in colour.
Lactifluus bertillonii has a similar woolly covering and acrid taste, but its fruit bodies are much paler.
Also similar and likewise having an acrid taste is Lactarius acerrimus, but it has forked-connected gills and turns brown when damaged.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–15 cm, low-arched in young specimens, spread out and depressed in the centre in older ones.
It is hard, the margins are rolled back for a long time, no umbo.
Surface slippery, without zoning, or with faintly visible zoning.
Colour from dirty olive-green to blackish-brown.
spod: Narrow and crowded, of various lengths, slightly decurrent on the stem.
First whitish then cream-yellow, with brown spots in old age.
Darkening when damaged.
They exude abundant white milk with a very burning taste, which does not change colour in the air.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness up to 2.5 cm, cylindrical, at first solid, later hollow.
Surface shiny when dry, slippery in wet weather, sometimes rough or pitted.
Colour from pale olive through greenish to dirty olive.
miazsz: Thick and hard, white, only weakly olive under the skin of the cap.
In older specimens the flesh turns brown.
It has an acrid taste and a faint smell.
mleczko: It is exuded abundantly.
It is white or watery white, does not change colour in the air.
In taste it is very burning.
podobne: It differs considerably in colour from other milkcaps and is generally easy to recognise.
Lactarius blennius is somewhat similar, but it is smaller, has a bell-shaped cap covered with banded patches, does not have such dark tones and occurs under beeches.

kapelusz: White in colour.
Size from 10 to 20 cm.
A delicate felt on the surface.
Light orange spots often appear on it.
trzon: White in colour.
Massive, stocky, thick.
From 30–80 mm long.
When pressed, orange spots appear.
spod: Sparsely spaced, but long.
podobne: Externally this species cannot be distinguished from Lactifluus vellereus, whose milk also has an acrid taste.
For this reason it is identified with it by mushroom pickers.
It can be recognised only by microscopic details of anatomical structure and by the reaction with KOH; its milk changes colour to orange under KOH, in the similar milkcap it does not.

kapelusz: Dry and smooth, without gloss.
Diameter 6–20 cm.
Colour pure white with a faint cream tinge.
In older individuals injured spots are brown in colour.
A flatly domed cap occurs in young individuals; in older ones the cap becomes broadly funnel-shaped with an inrolled margin.
spod: Very crowded, thin, narrow, shortly decurrent on the stem, forked.
At first they are white, later they become yellowish.
trzon: Cylindrical in shape, height 3–9 cm, width 1–3 cm, white, later partly spotted.
It is solid, thinner below, hard and smooth.
miazsz: At first white, then yellowish, firm, hard and brittle.
mleczko: It is released abundantly and is white.
While drying it turns slightly yellow, and under the action of KOH it turns yellow.
In taste it is acrid, burning.
podobne: Lactifluus vellereus – commonly confused by mushroom pickers with the white milkcap.
It differs from it in its more distant gills, is larger and has a felty-suede-like cap
Lactifluus glaucescens – its milk and damaged spots change colour to blue-green after some time.
Russula delica – has a much shorter stem and does not exude milk

kapelusz: Diameter 10–25 cm, in young specimens low-arched with inrolled margins, in older ones it becomes depressed in the centre and deepened or funnel-shaped.
It has sharp margins, is hard and thick-fleshed.
Its skin is dull, white to pale ochre.
trzon: Cylindrical, solid, short and thick, reaching about 6 cm in height and up to 2 cm in thickness.
At first its skin is felty, later it becomes bald.
Colour the same as the cap.
spod: White, then ochre-yellow, fairly sparse and thick.
In older specimens they are decurrent on the stem.
miazsz: Thick, hard, cream-yellowish when cut.
The flesh itself has a mild taste, but it exudes a white milk, slowly turning yellow in the air, with an acrid taste.
The flesh is built of roundish cells, which causes the specific brittleness (typical of all Russulaceae) and the irregular fracture.
mleczko: White and not changing colour.
At first it flows out abundantly.
The taste is mild, or only slightly bitter, in any case not burning.
podobne: A very similar mushroom is the edible Lactifluus piperatus with thin gills and white, weakly burning milk, and Lactifluus glaucescens, whose milk is blue-green.
Compare also with the edible Russula delica, without milk.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–15 cm, when young convex with slightly inrolled margins, later almost flat with a depression in the centre, finally shallowly concave.
Margins at first rolled under, later curved under, finally straightened.
No umbo.
Surface smooth, without striation, red-orange, yellow-red, orange-brown in colour.
spod: Fairly crowded, adnate-decurrent.
At first they are white, later pale yellowish and pale ochre.
When damaged they change colour to rusty brown.
trzon: Height 6–12 cm, thickness 1–3.5 cm, cylindrical, solid, smooth, bare.
It is much paler than the cap, usually orange-yellowish in colour.
miazsz: Firm, whitish in young specimens, pale yellow to pale ochre in older ones.
It has a fairly strong smell resembling herring.
mleczko: Milk very abundant, white, not changing colour in the air.
Mild in taste, but leaves a bitter aftertaste.
podobne: There are many similar species of orange milkcaps that are difficult to tell apart externally, e.g. Lactarius subdulcis, Lactarius aurantiacus.
The most reliable feature for distinguishing the delicious milk cap is its milk, which, unlike in other Lactarius species, is not burning and bitter.
It is also easy to recognise thanks to its uniformly rusty-orange coloured cap.

kapelusz: Usually without a stem, thick-fleshed, attached sideways to the tree, 10–40 cm in diameter.
Fruit bodies often grow in overlapping tiers, one above another.
Young specimens often have a bulb-like shape, later they become fan-shaped, hemispherical or irregularly deformed.
Upper surface hilly, uneven, radially wrinkled.
Colour sulphur-yellow to orange (often with a pink tinge), which fades with age.
Margin irregular, wavy, inrolled.
Fruit bodies with a sharp margin are also found.
The margin is often lemon-coloured.
spod: Tubular, not separating from the flesh.
Tubes short (up to 1.5–5 mm long), sulphur yellow in colour.
Tube pores very small (3–5 per mm), at first sulphur yellow, then ochre-yellow.
miazsz: Colour white to cream-yellow, soft and juicy in young specimens, brittle in older ones.
In taste pleasant, slightly sour, smell mushroomy.
wysyp: Light yellow, quickly fading to white.
Spores colourless, smooth, egg-shaped to oval or teardrop-shaped.
They have a sharply pointed base and droplets in the centre.

kapelusz: Diameter 7–14 cm, shape at first hemispherical, later flatly spread, and cushion-shaped.
Surface bare, pitted and often wrinkled, and in older specimens cracked into small fields, especially in prolonged dry weather.
Colour in shades of brown: yellow-brown, grey-brown, olive-brown, dark brown, blackish-brown.
spod: Very long (up to 2 cm) and deeply notched at the stem.
At first they are whitish, later yellowish, olive-yellow and olive-blue.
Pores round, 1-2 per 1 mm.
When pressed they darken and change colour, at first to grey-brown, later to black.
trzon: Height 5–14 cm, thickness 1–3 cm, shape more or less cylindrical, thinner at the top, thickened at the bottom and widened in a club-like manner.
Surface whitish and covered with blackish, fibrous fibrils or small scales.
In the upper part it is often wrinkled.
When pressed it turns black.
miazsz: Whitish-yellow, when damaged it changes colour to pink, then grey-violet, and after some time turns black.
Taste and smell pleasant, mushroomy.
podobne: Leccinellum crocipodium, but it is paler,
Leccinum scabrum.
It grows only under birches.
Its cap is always smooth and the flesh does not turn black.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–15 cm.
Spherical when young, then hemispherical, finally becomes low-arched.
Colour orange-red, red-orange, dark or brick red.
Margin of the cap thin; the skin at the edge of older specimens usually hangs beyond the tubes as a thin membrane.
spod: Greyish with an olive tinge.
Pores round, small, at first white, then greyish ochre, finally olive.
trzon: 5–18 cm tall, cylindrical, solid, wider at the bottom.
It is whitish and covered, when young, with whitish and later orange-red scales.
Under the cap the scales remain white for a long time.
miazsz: Thick, hard, juicy, white, darkening when cut.
Taste insignificant, mild, smell indistinct.
In older specimens the flesh in the stem becomes bast-like, whereas in the cap it is softer and watery.
wysyp: Spores 13-17 × 4-5 µm in diameter, smooth, yellowish-brown.
podobne: Leccinum versipelle is very similar.
It is paler and grows under birches.
It is easiest to recognise by the black scales on the stem.
Leccinum vulpinum grows only under pines, Leccinum piceinum only under spruces.

kapelusz: 4–8 cm in diameter, round, usually regular, sometimes only slightly deformed with a wavy margin.
At first it is convex, when mature arched, but never becomes quite flat.
Surface very delicately tomentose, in various shades of brown, but whitish albino forms are also found.
spod: Broadly attached to the stem, 1 to 1.5 cm long and 0.5 mm in diameter, round, in colour from dirty white to grey-brown.
Pores of the same colour.
When squeezed they do not turn blue, but slowly turn brown.
trzon: Thickness 1–2.5 cm, height 7–14 cm.
Shape at first barrel-shaped, then slightly club-shaped, narrowing towards the apex.
miazsz: Flesh at the base of the stem white, always blue when damaged (although often only in a very limited area).
It is blue also in places nibbled by snails or insects.
At the top it is white, sometimes turning pink after damage.
podobne: In Leccinum scabrum the stem base does not turn blue when damaged, and it is usually larger than the bluish-stemmed Leccinum.
There are also differences in microscopic features.
The orange-yellow Leccinum versipelle has a much more orange cap and blue-green spots at the stem base.

kapelusz: Diameter up to 15 cm, hemispherical in young specimens, then cushion-flattened.
It is fleshy, in dry weather dry, dull and felty, in wet weather the cap surface is sticky.
When young the surface is smooth, with time it becomes wrinkled.
Colour from red-grey to dark brown, with yellow speckles at the margin.
Surface scaly and fibrously felty.
spod: Up to 30 millimetres long, deeply notched at the stem.
Colour from white in young to grey in older specimens.
Pores roundish, in older individuals grey-olive.
The pores turn brown when pressed.
trzon: Thickness up to 3 cm, height up to 15 cm, cylindrical.
It is white or cream and covered with numerous small scales and granules, which in young specimens are pale brown, in older ones blackish, especially in the lower part of the stem.
miazsz: In the cap white, salmon when cut, in the upper part of the stem grey-violet, turning blue at the base.
Taste and smell pleasant.
podobne: Leccinum scabrum has a smooth cap skin and its flesh does not change colour.
Grows under birches.
Leccinum variicolor also has a smooth cap skin, with light green flesh at the base of the stem.
The flesh of the cap turns pink when cut.
Grows under birches.

kapelusz: Cap white or whitish, 5–15 cm in diameter.
spod: Tubes whitish, turning brown when pressed.
trzon: Whitish with white or grey scales.
miazsz: Flesh white, usually turning pink, sometimes bluish at the base.
podobne: Similar is Leccinum rotundifoliae, which has a similar colour, but prefers dry areas and does not turn blue at the base of the stem.
Albino forms of other Leccinum species growing under birch may also be similar.

kapelusz: Diameter up to 25 cm, convex in young specimens, then cushion-like flattened.
Surface dull, orange-red or orange-brown, fading with age.
spod: At first yellowish-white, later greyish, darkening when crushed.
Pores round, small.
trzon: Thickness up to 5 cm, height 8–20 cm.
Shape at first barrel-shaped, then cylindrical.
Surface white with protruding white fibres, which then turn rusty from the spores.
miazsz: White, hard and firm in young fruit bodies, partly fibrous in older ones.
When damaged it turns red, then greyish.
Taste mild, smell faint, uncharacteristic.

kapelusz: Diameter up to 20 cm, semicircular to cushion-shaped in young specimens, smooth in older ones.
In wet weather the surface of the cap is slippery, slightly slimy.
Colour from light brown to dark brown.
trzon: Thickness up to 3.5 cm, height up to 17 cm.
Solid, cylindrical, slender, tapering towards the cap.
White, covered with numerous dark brown to black fibrils.
spod: Up to 25 mm long, deeply notched at the stem.
Colour from whitish in young specimens to grey-brown in older ones.
Pores almost round and small.
The tubes do not change colour when damaged.
miazsz: White to white-cream, may be white-greenish at the base.
Fibrous, firm in young specimens, to soft, watery in old ones.
Does not change colour when damaged.
Taste and smell pleasant, faint.
podobne: Quite often it is confused with the similar-looking Tylopilus felleus, which has a bitter taste and is inedible – this species has no fibrils on the stem, but a distinct brown reticulum.
Leccinellum pseudoscabrum is also similar, but it grows only under hornbeams and its flesh, when damaged, turns a colour from dirty pink to blackish.
Also under birches, but in wetter places, grows the similar Leccinum variicolor.
On heaths a similar species occurs, but with very pale, almost white colouring: Leccinum holopus.

kapelusz: Brick-orange or orange-yellow.
It has a diameter of 5–15 cm, is cushion-shaped convex, usually tufted and rough; on its margin membranous remains of the hanging skin are visible
spod: Tubes whitish with a grey tinge.
trzon: It is 6–15 cm long and 1–3 cm thick.
Surface white or pale grey, covered with fine black scales, which turn brown in older specimens.
miazsz: When cut the flesh turns pink-grey-violet, and in the lower part of the stem green-bluish.
This colour change may also occur in the orange oak bolete.
podobne: Leccinum aurantiacum is very similar.
It is easiest to tell apart by the scales on the stem; Leccinum aurantiacum has at first whitish scales, later red-brown, but they are never black.
It also has a more intense, bright red cap and grows only under aspen.
Also similar are Leccinum vulpinum and Leccinum piceinum.
Mushroom pickers often do not distinguish the Leccinum species, but from a practical point of view this makes no significant difference, since all of them are tasty edible mushrooms.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–7 cm, colour at first flesh-brown, later brown-reddish, and in older specimens yellow-brown or ochre.
When young it is funnel-shaped or horn-shaped, later becoming shell-shaped, spatula-shaped or gill-like.
It is bare, thin, springy and delicately wrinkled.
It often has irregularly bent margins.
trzon: Height 2–8 cm, thickness 5–10 mm, colour flesh-reddish and red-brown below.
It is usually eccentric, i.e. not attached exactly in the centre of the cap, but somewhat to the side.
It is solid, ribbed-wrinkled, bare and springy.
The stems of neighbouring fruit bodies are often fused.
spod: At first whitish, later brownish, deeply decurrent down the stem all the way to its base.
They have a toothed or notched edge.
miazsz: Colour white to flesh-brown.
It is hard, springy and has an aniseed smell and a mild taste.
wysyp: Spores: 4 – 6 × 4 μm, almost spherical, delicately dotted.
In Poland there also occur: Lentinellus flabelliformis, Lentinellus ursinus and Lentinellus vulpinus.
All these species differ from Lentinellus cochleatus in lacking the aniseed smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–4, exceptionally up to 8 cm, thickness 1–4 mm, shape round, convex and slightly funnel-shaped.
Margin sharp, rolled under and covered with bristles.
Surface rough and densely covered with scales.
It is coloured from light brown through ochre-brown to yellow-brown.
During drying the surface becomes concentrically wrinkled.
A characteristic feature is that the hairs protrude clearly beyond the cap margin.
spod: Tubular.
Tubes slightly decurrent, up to 3 mm long.
Pores white or cream, polygonal and elongated, 1–2 mm long and 0.5–1 mm wide.
Near the margin of the cap the pores are small.
The pores are large and clearly arranged in radial rows.
trzon: Height 3–6 cm, thickness 2-4, exceptionally up to 7 mm.
It is central or almost central, cylindrical, solid, slightly thicker at the base.
Surface light brown in colour, covered with small scales and felty.
miazsz: Dry, hard and brittle, 1–2 mm thick in the cap.
Taste mild, smell indistinct.
podobne: Lentinus brumalis also has large and similar pores, but is darker and does not have a fringed cap margin.
Neofavolus alveolaris also has large pores, but occurs mainly on ash,
Lentinus substrictus has a hairy or felty cap, pores fine.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–8 cm, shape round and spread out flat, slightly funnel-shaped in older specimens.
Surface bare, delicately felty, or scaly, cap margin sometimes hairy.
Colour from dark brown to almost black.
spod: Decurrent, up to 1 mm long.
Pores white or cream, angular, 2–3 mm across.
trzon: Height 3–6 cm, thickness about 0.5 cm.
It is central or almost central.
Surface bare, colour from light brown to grey-brown.
miazsz: White, elastic, thin, with a faint sour smell.
podobne: Lentinus substrictus, but its fruit bodies appear only from spring to summer.
It has small pores, a zigzag stem, and a shaggy or hairy cap,
Lentinus arcularius also has large pores, but a paler cap with clearly visible bristles at the margin.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–12 cm, thickness 0.2–0.8 cm, shape round, flat or slightly convex, sometimes with a point, rarely concave.
Margin sharp, thin, inrolled, sometimes wavy or lobed.
Surface matt, covered with smaller or larger scales, and in older specimens covered with a network of cracks.
It is bristly-haired over the whole surface or only at the margins.
Colour very variable; it may be yellow, rusty, grey-brown, tobacco, fawn or almost black.
spod: Tubular.
Tubes 0.5–2 mm long, with very thin walls and slightly decurrent.
Pores very fine, regular.
They are 0.05–0.2 mm in diameter (4-6 of them fit in 1 mm).
Colour clearly paler than the cap.
trzon: Usually central, less often eccentric.
Height 2–3 (exceptionally up to 6) cm, thickness 0.2–0.7 cm.
It is hard, sometimes arched, cylindrical, sometimes with a thickened base.
Surface smooth, fibrous-scaly or covered with short, bristly hairs, colour nut-brown, yellow-grey to light chestnut.
podobne: Lentinus brumalis.
It has distinctly larger pores and appears mainly in winter and spring.
Its stem is not so hairy.
Lentinus arcularius.
It has large pores.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–9 cm, arched when young, then depressed, finally funnel-shaped.
Surface when dry uniformly grey-brown, olive-brown or blackish in colour.
In older specimens the skin cracks, producing concentrically arranged small fields contrasting with the white or cream-ochre background.
spod: Broad, crowded, deeply decurrent on the stem.
They have delicately toothed edges.
At first they are whitish, then cream, finally yellowish.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness 4–8 mm, cylindrical.
It is central or eccentric, scaly, whitish in the upper part, yellowish in the middle, grey-brown at the base.
Sometimes it has a membranous ring in the upper part, but as a rule it quickly disappears.
miazsz: White or yellowish, springy, and in mature fruit bodies springy-leathery.
Taste indistinct, smell intense.

owocnik: Branched like a shrub; 2–6 cm wide, 3–10 cm high.
It grows from a thin white-cream base branching into thin and parallel twigs.
Cords of mycelium usually grow from the base.
The branches are fairly dense and upright.
They are pale yellow, cinnamon, ochre-brown or brown in colour.
When damaged they turn reddish-brown.
miazsz: White, when damaged or crushed it turns reddish-brown.
Smell slightly sourish, tips of the branches bitter in taste
wysyp: Spores elliptical, elongated, with a rough surface, measuring 7.5–10.5 × 3.5–5.5 μm.
podobne: The stiff coral fungus can be confused with many species of other coral fungi.
Similar are, among others:
Phaeoclavulina flaccida.
Occurs only in coniferous forests.
Telling these species apart is possible only under the microscope and by reaction with KOH.
Ramaria eumorpha.
Occurs mainly in coniferous forests and does not change colour after damage.
Ramaria formosa.
It has shorter branches and grows mainly under beeches.
Artomyces pyxidatus has branch tips widened in a cup-like manner.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–4 cm, at first conical-bell-shaped, then convex, slightly concave in older specimens.
Surface in colour from cream-yellow to ochre, covered with radially arranged fibrils or scales of olive or dark brown colour, and in the centre of the cap chestnut to brown-black.
The margin in young fruit bodies is rolled under, with hanging white remains of the veil, in older ones straightened.
trzon: Height from 2 to 6 cm, diameter from 0.15 to 0.5 cm, cylindrical, only slightly widening towards the base, at first solid, then hollow.
No ring, only an annular zone is present.
The surface above this zone is smooth, cream, below this zone darker, covered with fibrils of colour from fawn to brown.
White mycelium often at the base.
spod: Free, broad, moderately crowded, coloured from white to cream, sometimes with a pink tint.
Intermediate lamellae are present.
Gill edges even, finely toothed.
miazsz: With an indistinct mushroomy or fruity smell.
podobne: Echinoderma asperum is similarly coloured, but it has spreading scales and is larger.
Lepiota castanea has different scales and smaller spores.

kapelusz: Diameter from 3 to 6 cm, at first convex with a blunt umbo, later spread out, slightly concave in older specimens, with brown, wine-brown or violet-brown scales on a pale pink background.
Skin cracked into granular small scales.
trzon: Height from 3 to 5 cm, diameter from 0.3 to 0.8 cm, cylindrical, with a narrow ring that disappears in mature fruit bodies, whitish above the ring, pinkish-brown to light violet below it, with several interrupted, ring-like, brown scales arranged one above the other.
spod: Free at the stem, pale cream.
The edge of the gills is very finely crenate.
miazsz: White, turning slightly red, with a fruity smell.
podobne: The poisonous Lepiota brunneolilacea, which has a green-grey ring and grows on sandy soils.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–4.5 cm, at first convex, then flat with a blunt small umbo.
Surface orange-brown to red-brown, concentrically cracked into granular small scales on a white or cream background.
Fibrous scales with bent-back ends.
Margin lighter and less scaly.
trzon: Height 4 to 6 cm, diameter 0.18 to 0.3 cm, cylindrical, only slightly widening towards the base, at first solid, then hollow.
A ring is usually absent, only a ring zone is present at 2/3 of the height.
The surface above this zone is smooth, white, below this zone scaly, light brown to brown.
Small scales arranged in a ring, of the same colour as on the cap.
White mycelial cords grow from the base.
spod: Free, bellied, crowded, 3 mm wide, with smooth edges.
Colour from white to cream.
miazsz: White, with a smell similar to that of the stinking dapperling.
podobne: Lepiota brunneoincarnata, which has a cap with a violet tinge and a stem that is zonally scaly below the ring,
Lepiota pseudohelveola has a membranous ring, and the cap has no reddish tones,
Lepiota boudieri has a less scaly cap and an unpleasant smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–7 cm.
Young – egg-shaped, later bell-shaped, finally flat, with a blunt smooth rusty-brown umbo in the centre.
Surface whitish, white-cream or yellowish with ochre-yellow to brownish hairy scales arranged concentrically.
Remains of the veil hang from the margin of the cap.
spod: Free at the stem, crowded, white or pale yellowish.
trzon: Height from 4 to 10 cm, diameter from 0.5 to 1 cm.
Shape cylindrical, thickened at the bottom, can be broken out, tubular.
It has a ring, but it quickly disappears.
Above the ring the surface is smooth, below it on a white background covered with woolly, yellowish or brownish scales.
Older specimens lose their scales.
miazsz: White to pale ochre.
Smell unpleasant, taste mild.
wysyp: Spores spindle-shaped or almond-shaped, smooth, measuring 11–18.5 × 4–6.5 μm.
podobne: A characteristic feature allowing this species to be distinguished from several similar dapperlings is the strongly woolly sheath of the stem.
Lepiota ignivolvata is similar (especially from above), but the stem has no woolly fibrils, rather an orange-brown ring zone.
Lepiota magnispora is also similar, which on the cap has, on an ochre background, bright yellow to brownish scales and a yellowish-ochre stem.

kapelusz: 3–4 cm in diameter.
It emerges from the soil at first in the form of a closed cone and gradually develops into a spread-out cap with a distinct, umbo-like centre.
The umbo has an intense brown-red or dark ochre colour.
Surface of the rest of the cap whitish, covered with light ochre scales.
In places rich in nitrogen compounds (e.g. on compost heaps) it can produce very large fruit bodies with a cap diameter of up to 8 cm.
spod: Whitish, not attached to the stem, pressed together and slightly bulging.
trzon: Slender, cylindrical, club-shaped and thickened at the base.
It does not exceed 7 cm in height and about 0.5 cm in thickness.
Surface creamy white, covered with sparse small hairs coloured like the cap.
In younger individuals there is under the cap a thin, membranous ring raised in a funnel shape, which disappears with age.
The stem is at first solid, in older specimens hollow.
miazsz: White, flesh-pink only in the cortex of the stem.
It gives off a strong, unpleasant smell similar to that of puffballs.
wysyp: Spores wedge-shaped or spherical, smooth, measuring 5–8 × 3–5 μm, strongly or weakly dextrinoid.
Cheilocystidia club-shaped, measuring up to about 25 × 10 μ, pleurocystidia absent.
podobne: Lepiota clypeolaria, which has a fibrous structure on the stem.
There are many morphologically similar species of Lepiota (e.g. L. castanea, L. boudieri).
The stinking dapperling can be distinguished from them by its exceptionally well-developed white ring.
However, specimens in which the ring has disappeared can be reliably identified only by microscopic examination.
This Lepiota species is, in morphology and fusiform spores, very similar to Lepiota clypeolaria.
In the XIX century it was regarded by one mycologist as a white variety of this species.

kapelusz: Diameter 1.5–3 cm, at first convex, then flat with a blunt umbo.
Surface white with a darker, almost black centre.
It is covered with concentrically arranged dark brown scales, large in relation to the cap diameter.
trzon: Height 2.5 to 4 cm, diameter 0.2 to 0.4 cm, cylindrical.
The ring is white-cream on the upper side, brown on the lower.
spod: Free, crowded, at first white, then darker.
miazsz: White, thin, tasteless, with an earthy smell.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid to ovoid, smooth, amyloid, measuring 6.5–8 × 3.5–4 μm.
podobne: Lepiota pseudolilacea.
It has scales in colour from grey-brown to dirty brown.
Lepiota cristata.
It is larger, has a lighter cap and an unpleasant smell.

kapelusz: Diameter up to 3.5 cm, at first hemispherical, then flat with a small umbo, usually irregular.
Surface white with a copper or reddish tinge, covered with small scales, denser in the centre of the cap.
spod: Free, fairly crowded, white.
trzon: Height up to 6 cm, with a bulb at the base, hollow inside.
Surface fibrillose, white-brown, covered with white scales and a short-lived, fibrous, narrow and poorly developed ring.
miazsz: White, changing colour to reddish when damaged, reddish under the umbo of the cap and at the periphery of the stem.
Smell faint, sometimes indistinct, taste at first mushroomy, then metallic.
podobne: It belongs to the section Brunoincarnata of the small Lepiota.
Lepiota subincarnata is similar, but has larger spores and a cap of a different colour, although it can sometimes be pinkish.

kapelusz: 1.5–3 cm in diameter, at first convex, later broadly bell-shaped.
Surface dry, with a purple-brown to dark brown centre as it matures, and in the remaining part covered with small scales of the same colour on a whitish or pinkish background.
spod: Free, crowded, with numerous intermediate lamellae, white.
trzon: Height 2–4 cm, thickness 2–4 mm, more or less cylindrical.
Surface bare, pinkish to purple in young specimens.
It has a persistent, collar-like ring, the underside of which is brown and ragged.
miazsz: Thin, white in the cap, sometimes pinkish in the stem.
Smell: pleasant (aromatic) or indistinct.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–6 cm, at first bell-shaped, then flat-convex.
Surface pink-ochre to light brown, red-brownish only in the centre of the cap, radially fibrillose.
Margins with hanging remains of the veil.
spod: Free, crowded, whitish.
trzon: Height 4–10 cm, thickness 0.3–1 cm, shape cylindrical, slightly thickened at the base.
Surface fibrous, covered with the same fibrils as on the cap.
It has a flocculose ring zone or a ring, which, however, often disappears.
Abundant white mycelium at the base of the stem.
miazsz: Thin, in colour from white to yellowish-brown, tasteless.
Smell unpleasant.
whitish, yellow-brownish in the stem; smell unpleasant, taste neutral.
podobne: Lepiota clypeolaria is the most similar.
It is similarly hairy-fibrous, but Lepiota magnispora is distinguished by more yellow colours and a more contrasting cap centre.
Lepiota clypeolaria is the most similar.
It is similarly hairy-fibrous, but Lepiota magnispora is distinguished by more yellow colours and a more contrasting cap centre.

kapelusz: Diameter 2.5–5 cm, at first conical, then convex, finally flattened, with a distinct umbo.
Dark brown in the centre with slightly bristling scales, otherwise covered with light brown scales with a pink tinge, on a whitish background.
spod: Free, moderately crowded, white.
trzon: Height 4–6 cm, cylindrical, slightly curved and thickened at the base, covered with small scales below the ring.
miazsz: Whitish with a slight smell and aftertaste of cinnamon.
podobne: Lepiota lilacea differs among other things by its fruity smell; the stinking parasol has an unpleasant, somewhat garlicky smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–3.5 cm, at first hemispherical, then flat-convex with a small umbo.
