Surface whitish, covered with pink-brown, small, woolly scales, which often form irregularly concentric rings.
The small scales are darkest in the centre, towards the margin increasingly paler and more sparsely distributed.
Margin with hanging, flocculose remains of the veil.
spod: Free, crowded, white-cream.
Under a hand lens, cheilocystidia can be seen on the edges.
trzon: Height 2.5–5 cm, thickness 0.4–0.9 cm, cylindrical, base bulbous.
Surface with a pinkish tinge.
Ring zone indistinct.
Above this zone the surface is smooth, below it covered with fibrous scales.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid; smooth, amyloid, measuring 6–7.5 × 3–4 μm.
podobne: A characteristic feature of the pinkish dapperling is the pinkish colouring of the cap and stem.
It may, however, be confused with other species:
Lepiota ignivolvata.
It is distinguished by a light, orange or red-brown ring on the stem.
Lepiota cristata.
It is usually larger and has brownish scales.

kapelusz: Conical, with age bell-shaped to spread out; diameter from 1 to 8 cm, shiny, sulphur yellow in colour.
Surface covered with fibrous scales, bare and striate at the margins.
Margin wavily furrowed.
spod: Broad, light yellow to sulphur yellow.
trzon: The colour of the cap, brittle, with a thin ring.
Cylindrical, widening towards the base; up to 10 cm long.
miazsz: Thin, sulphur-yellow, with a weak, slightly unpleasant smell.
podobne: In pots and greenhouses other, similar species of exotic fungi may grow, such as Leucocoprinus cretatus, which differs in colour (white).

kapelusz: Diameter 5–10 cm, in young specimens closed, spherical in shape, later hemispherical-arched, finally flat, not hygrophanous.
Margin smooth and without striations.
Surface silky-smooth, lime-white to dirty white, later pale cream, greyish, sometimes with a flesh-coloured or violetish tinge.
In sunny places the surface often cracks into small fields.
spod: Crowded, free, white in young specimens, pinkish in older ones.
trzon: Height 6–12 cm, thickness 1–2 cm, easily separating from the cap, cylindrical, base thickened or bulbous.
At first solid, later tubular.
In the upper part it has a white, leathery ring hanging downwards.
Surface white, shiny.
miazsz: White, sometimes slightly yellowish, turning brown in older fruit bodies.
Taste mild, smell mushroomy.
podobne: morphologically, various species of Agaricus are very similar, but all of them have pink gills from the very beginning, becoming darker and darker with time, chocolate brown in mature fruit bodies,
Amanita virosa always has white gills, and at the base of the stem it has a volva
The white-coloured Volvariella gloiocephala.
They differ in the stem, which has a leathery volva at the base.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm.
At first convex with an inrolled margin, later arched, in time spread out and shallowly depressed in the centre, finally funnel-shaped.
Surface without grooves, delicately fibrous and silky-shiny.
Colour white or dirty white, in old specimens it becomes light flesh-coloured.
It is hygrophanous; when wet, water-soaked, darker patches appear on the surface.
spod: Broadly attached and decurrent with a small tooth.
Edges white and even.
trzon: Height 3–5 cm, thickness 2–4 mm, cylindrical in shape, usually slightly widened at the bottom, often bent, springy.
Surface longitudinally fibrous, white.
miazsz: Thin, whitish, without a distinct taste and with an aromatic smell.
podobne: Clitocybe rivulosa, which has a frosted cap with concentrically arranged flesh-cream patches on its surface.
Clitocybe phyllophila.
It is larger, its gills are only weakly decurrent and there are no colour changes on the cap.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–10 cm, when young hemispherical, then convex with an inrolled margin.
In old age it becomes spread out with a sharp and often irregularly wavy margin.
Surface smooth, matt, suede-like shiny, coloured from white to light grey
spod: Very crowded, notched, or shortly decurrent on the stem.
Edges even.
White when young, then cream.
trzon: Height 4–12 cm, thickness up to 2 cm, cylindrical with a narrowed base, solid when young, then hollow.
Colour white, turning yellow only in older specimens, surface dull and scaly.
miazsz: White, not changing colour when cut, firm, flexible.
Taste slight, smell indistinct.
podobne: Clitocybe phyllophila – is smaller, has felt at the base of the stem and an aniseed smell.
Clitocybe rivulosa – is smaller, funnel-shaped when mature, and turns pink-red after damage.
Clitopilus prunulus – has pinkish gills.
Leucocybe connata is often confused with white funnel caps.
It can be reliably distinguished from them by the reaction with ferrous sulphate: in it the funnel caps turn violet, the chalky funnel cap does not undergo this reaction.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–20 mm, shape at first arched, later a small depression forms in the centre, finally the cap becomes funnel-shaped.
Surface smooth, matt, frosted, olive, yellow-ochre, yellowish in colour; fruit bodies of greenish, whitish or brownish colour also occur.
The cap is translucent and grooved up to ¾ of the radius, usually darker in the centre.
Margin sharp, wavy, toothed.
spod: Gilled.
Gills broad, triangular, decurrent on the stem.
They are pale ochre in colour and have smooth edges.
trzon: Height 13–20 mm, thickness 1–1.5 mm, shape cylindrical at the bottom, widening conically in the upper part and smoothly passing into the cap.
It is at first solid, then tubular.
Surface smooth, light brown, darker on top, whitish and felty below.
miazsz: Thin, soft, watery, brown-yellow, without distinct taste and smell.
podobne: Similar is the so-called Lichenomphalia hudsonii, which has smaller fruit bodies with a moist, pink-violet stem.

owocnik: Inversely pear-shaped or spherical, 2–6 cm in diameter.
Their lower part is shortly narrowed and joined to the substrate by whitish hyphae of mycelium.
The outer covering (exoperidium) is at first light brown, dark brown, finally umber.
It has dense, sharp, wedge-shaped and angular spines up to 5 mm long.
These spines do not touch at their tips.
After they fall off, a net-like pattern remains in the form of polygonal areolae.
The spines at the base of the fruit body are much shorter.
The endoperidium is soft, papery, at first white, then light cream, light brown, finally ochre-brown.
The mature fruit body bursts open through a circular opening at the top.
The subgleba is small, fairly compact, with small chambers.
At first it is white, then grey-violet.
As the fruit body matures it gradually passes into the columella.
The interior of the fruit body is filled with gleba.
At first it is white, then grey-violet, finally chocolate-brown.
podobne: Lycoperdon echinatum can be confused with Lycoperdon umbrinum, which is also in brownish shades, but has shorter spines.

owocnik: Height mostly 8–12 cm, sometimes up to 15 cm, but exceptional specimens up to 26 cm tall have occurred.
Width up to 5.5, sometimes up to 9.5 cm.
Shape club-shaped or cudgel-shaped, sometimes inversely pear-shaped.
The base is sometimes folded or pitted.
The outer covering (exoperidium) in young specimens is white, matt and smooth, later rough, finely granular and scabby.
In mature fruit bodies it becomes light brown or nut-brown.
The top part of the fruit body is covered with delicate spines clustered in a cone.
The spines fall off easily, leaving behind only a faintly visible pattern.
The inner covering (endoperidium) is thin, smooth, in colour from ochre through grey-brown to rusty-brown.
Both veils, as the fruit body matures, break up together with the flocculent gleba inside into fragments that persist for quite a long time on the substrate nearby.
After they fall off, a fairly durable, column-shaped or cup-shaped brown subgleba remains.
podobne: Bovistella utriformis.
It has a distinctly shorter stem
Lycoperdon perlatum.
It has conical spines that fall off easily when touched.

A characteristic feature distinguishing the mosaic puffball from similar species is the fact that its mature fruit body does not open with a hole at the top, but disintegrates almost entirely into fragments.
Microscopically it is distinguished by the warty spores and the non-septate hairs.

owocnik: Diameter up to 4 cm, height 3–6 cm, shape spherical or pear-shaped.
At the base there is a tuft of hyphae.
Surface matt, papery, in colour from cream to grey-brown.
It is covered with numerous large spines that are dark from the very beginning; light brown in young fruit bodies, brown in older ones.
The spines are 2–3 mm tall and grow on cones with blackish tips. After the spines fall off, a net-like structure remains on the endoperidium (as in Lycoperdon perlatum).
The gleba is at first yellow-olive, then becomes brown.
Subgleba at first light brown, then grey-brown with an olive or violet tint.
It forms relatively large chambers with a well-developed columella.
It has an unpleasant, metallic smell.
Height 3–7 cm, diameter 2–4 cm, shape club-shaped or pear-shaped, with a rounded apex or one ending in a hump.
It is covered with warty spines.
At first the whole fruit body is white, when mature it becomes ochre or brown and bald.
The spines break off easily when touched, leaving roundish pits.

In a mature fruit body its whole interior turns into an enormous quantity of spores, the fruit body splits at the top and the spores are released through the resulting opening (under the influence of wind or touch by animals or people).
Even raindrops 1 mm in diameter are sufficient to eject the spores.
A single gust of wind can release as many as 1 million spores.
The lower part of the fruit body is the subsoil.
At first it is white, during ripening it darkens and becomes light brown, at the same time gradually turning into gleba and columella.
The gleba occupying the upper part of the fruit body is at first white, later gradually yellow, olive and grey-brown.
podobne: Lycoperdon nigrescens, but it has dark spines from the beginning
Lycoperdon excipuliforme.
It is distinguished by star-shaped spines.

owocnik: Diameter up to 5 cm, height up to 5 cm.
Young fruit bodies are spherical, but quickly become inversely pear-shaped, lens-shaped, or take on the shape of a flattened spinning top.
The outer covering (exoperidium) remains white and matt for a long time.
On it there are sphaerocytes and small granular spines gathered in star-shaped clusters.
During the development of the fruit body these spines gradually fall off.
The inner covering (endoperidium) is smooth, brittle, parchment-like, at first white, later brownish, finally grey-brown.
After the spores mature it opens at the top, then falls away in pieces down to the diaphragm.
Gleba without a columella.
In young fruit bodies it is white, then becomes olive-brown, finally grey-brown.
The lower, sterile part of the gleba (the so-called subgleba) is chambered, white in young fruit bodies, later increasingly darker, finally dark brown.
Between the gleba and the subgleba there is a clearly visible, shiny diaphragm.
podobne: The most characteristic features of this small puffball are the clear separation of the gleba from the subgleba, the way the fruit body opens and the absence of a true capillitium.
Similar are:
Bovistella utriformis.
Its surface cracks into small patches.
Lycoperdon mamiforme.
The ectoperidium peels off early.

owocnik: Up to 15 cm in diameter and of a short club-shaped or spherical-bulbous shape.
At the top it is usually slightly flattened, it may also be wrinkled or shallowly pitted.
It is surrounded by a two-layered peridium.
Its outer layer (exoperidium) is at first white and felty, then grey-brown and cracked into polygonal patches about 5 mm in diameter, or pyramids formed from joined spines.
During the ripening of the fruit body the exoperidium flakes off and falls away, exposing the endoperidium of papery consistency and grey-brown, nut-brown, olive-brown or brown colour.
After the spores have ripened, the endoperidium splits at the top into irregular lobes, which fall off completely or partly down to the boundary with the subgleba.
It is well developed, at first whitish, then grey-brown, finally brown.
A thin, brown pseudodiaphragm separates it from the soil.
The gleba in the upper part of the fruit body is at first whitish, then olive, finally dark brown.
The lower part of the fruit body (the subiculum) is quite durable and often persists on the ground until the next summer.
podobne: Calvatia turneri.
It is smaller and in Poland occurs only in the mountains.
Lycoperdon excipuliforme, especially stemless specimens
Calvatia cyathiformis.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–10 cm.
Young it is hemispherically convex with slightly inrolled margins, mature flat with sharp margins and slightly wavy.
It is grey, grey-brown to olive-brown-blackish, silky shiny and radially delicately fibrous.
spod: At first white, then greyish-cream, moderately crowded, notched with a tooth at the stem.
They are of unequal length and slightly decurrent.
trzon: Length 7–13 cm, thickness 1–2 cm.
It is irregularly cylindrical, solid and usually curved.
Sometimes it is eccentric.
Surface whitish, silkily shiny (with time becoming brown at the bottom), bare or delicately fibrous.
miazsz: White, not changing colour when cut, firm, flexible.
Taste slight, smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spores 5–7 µm in diameter, spherical, smooth, colourless.
podobne: Lyophyllum fumosum.
It has a darker cap, a mealy smell and is more fleshy.
Lyophyllum loricatum.
It has a darker cap and is cartilaginous.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm, at first bell-shaped, later convex to flat.
Surface smooth and velvety, colour from reddish-brown to dark chestnut.
The margins are lighter – yellow-brown or flesh-pink, but their lighter colour quickly fades and in older specimens the margins of the cap are coloured the same as the cap.
spod: Fairly crowded, bulging, sinuately notched at the stem, at first whitish, later ochre, ochre-pink, salmon.
trzon: Height 4–8 cm, thickness 0.5 cm, cylindrical, hard, cartilaginous.
Surface white-mossy, in colour from dark red-brown to black-brown, paler only right under the cap.
miazsz: Dark brown, with a characteristic smell similar to cucumbers or herrings.
Taste mild.
Some even consider that it has a smell of fish oil.
It is so intense that after taking the mushroom in the hand it lingers on the fingers for a long time.
podobne: The smell is so characteristic that it allows this species to be told apart from other similar ones without error.
Some morphological features are also characteristic: a dark brown cap with a surface velvety to the touch and clearly paler margins in young fruit bodies, a very dark, often black stem.

inne: Height from 5 to 15 cm.
The colour of the fungus is white to cream.
Cap convex, vaulted with a convex centre, up to 10 cm in diameter.
Surface with a brownish centre, covered with scales from ochre-yellow to pale brown in colour.
Gills white to cream in colour, stem smooth, cylindrical, with a bulbous base and a ring.
Spores smooth, hyaline, ellipsoid.
Spore print white, cream or yellowish.
Ring whitish to white.
Flesh white, fibrous and does not change colour.
Macrolepiota (the white-stemmed parasol) is similar to Macrolepiota procera, but the latter is larger.

kapelusz: Diameter from 5 to 12 cm, young – ovoid, later convex to spread out, light brown, pale flesh-ochre, skin at first star-like cracked, in mature fruit bodies remaining so only in the middle, where it is also darker, elsewhere delicately densely, radially and granularly scaly, with a paler background showing through between the scales.
spod: Free from the stem, white.
trzon: Height 10 to 15 cm, diameter 0.8 to 1.5 cm, cylindrical, with a bulbous base (up to 2.5 cm), can be broken off, smooth or slightly streaked, bast-like, tubular, light brownish wood colour.
It has a distinct double ring that can be slid along the stem.
miazsz: Whitish, taste slightly nutty.
podobne: Macrolepiota procera has larger fruit bodies and a cap covered with thick scales overlapping like roof tiles.
Edible.
Macrolepiota excoriata has a paler stem and small scales on the cap.
Edible.

kapelusz: Umbrella-shaped, 10–30 cm in diameter, with an umbo in the centre, with cracked, flaking skin.
Egg-shaped and closed when young, then conical, low-arched, finally flat and spread out.
In young ones the cap is entirely brown, in older ones whitish with large brown scales.
Cap margin ragged, usually white.
spod: Gills crowded, broad, not reaching the stem.
In older specimens they have an ochre bloom.
trzon: 15–40 cm long and up to 2 cm thick, cylindrical, ending below in a bulb up to 4 cm in diameter.
It is easy to break off.
At first it is solid and spongy, in older fruit bodies hollow inside.
It has a movable ring.
Above the ring the skin of the stem is whitish-brown and smooth, below there are darker transverse bands.
miazsz: In the cap soft, in the stem fibrous.
It is white, does not change colour after damage.
Taste mild, pleasant.
It gives off a delicate mushroomy-fruity smell.
podobne: Most similar is the so-called Chlorophyllum rhacodes.
It differs in lacking scales on the stem, and its flesh turns red when damaged.
Macrolepiota konradii is also very similar; it is much smaller, has fewer but larger patches on the cap and a different pattern on the stem.
It is most often not distinguished by mushroom pickers, but such a mistake is not dangerous.

Inexperienced mushroom pickers sometimes confuse Macrolepiota procera with the deadly poisonous death cap (Amanita phalloides), mainly with its white varieties, and for this reason many mushroom pickers do not collect it.
Cases of serious poisoning by Amanita pantherina and by fungi of the genus Lepiota, mistakenly taken for the parasol mushroom, have been recorded.
Also similar and poisonous is Chlorophyllum molybdites (the so-called poisonous blue-gill).
This species comes from North America and does not occur in Poland.

owocnik: Thin and slender, up to 300 mm tall, but usually not exceeding 20 cm in height. Diameter 5- 10 mm.
Rod-shaped, narrowly club-shaped, sometimes cylindrical, slender, elongated, at first pale yellow, darkening with age and becoming yellow-brown, brownish, red-brown to brown.
Single, unbranched, apex not forked, rounded or pointed.
Hollow inside, walls thin.
The hymenial layer is on the outside of the fruit body, occupying the surface of about 2/3 of its height in the upper part.
It looks as if it were lightly dusted.
trzon: There is no stem as such, but the lower part of the fruit body, about 1/3 of its height at the base, is sterile – it has no hymenium and therefore does not produce spores.
Its colouring is slightly darker than the rest of the fruit body, and the surface visibly smoother.
miazsz: In young fruit bodies it is hard and stiff, with age it becomes softer.
Taste and smell imperceptible.
podobne: The tubular club fungus is a fungus of characteristic appearance and large size.
Other species of similar habit produce much smaller fruit bodies, measuring from a few millimetres to a few centimetres.
Typhula filiformis is considerably smaller, only up to 5 cm long, and its fruit bodies are much narrower.
Growing among fallen leaves, sometimes in hundreds and thousands of specimens.
Typhula contorta is similar, but its fruit bodies are smaller and twisted around their own axis.

owocnik: Very thin and slender; usually single, sometimes forked at the top; smooth and hollow inside; ochre-yellow to flesh-brown, slightly fibrillose-felty at the base.
It is up to 5 cm tall, but only 1–2 mm thick.
podobne: Typhula fistulosa occurs in late autumn on fallen leaves, but is much larger (up to 20–30 cm high and about 5–10 mm thick).
It usually grows singly and is relatively rare.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–4 (up to 6) cm, leather-yellow or ochre-brownish in colour (paler, whitish when dry), hygrophanous, with a margin striate from the gills showing through, smooth and bare.
Conical when young, later convex, flat in the mature fruit body, often with a blunt umbo in the centre.
spod: Gills very distant, whitish, ochre after rain, cream during drought, somewhat darker after wetting.
trzon: Height 6–7 cm, thickness about 0.5 cm.
It is cylindrical, solid, flexible, not brittle, pale ochre, whitish yellowish.
miazsz: Pale yellow.
Thin, white, not changing colour when cut.
It has a pleasant mushroomy smell and a delicate taste.
podobne: some funnel caps (Clitocybe).
They differ in having adnate and strongly decurrent gills.
They also have a less elastic stem, more crowded gills, a frosted cap and a different smell.
Gymnopus peronata.

kapelusz: Diameter 6–15 mm, shape hemispherical and deeply notched, so that it resembles a cake mould.
Surface bare, whitish, with an ochre-brown depression in the centre
spod: Whitish, with a regular trama, very widely spaced.
At the stem they grow together forming a collar around it.
trzon: Shiny, thread-like, red-brown in colour (lighter near the cap, blackish at the base).
miazsz: Very thin, without smell or taste.
podobne: There are many similar, small Marasmius species living on leaves and woody debris.
Marasmius rotula can be recognised fairly easily by the characteristic collar ("collarium") formed by its gills around the stem.
Similar are:
Marasmius epiphyllus.
It grows on leaves and has a milk-white, more spread-out cap.
Older caps are wrinkled.
It is easily distinguished by the gills, which are very narrow, almost vein-like
Marasmius tremulae.
Very small, grows on aspen leaves.
It has other microscopic features (among others two-spored basidia and cylindrical spores).
Marasmius bulliardii.
It is beige or ochre in colour, cap semicircular.
Marasmius setaceus.
It grows on leaves, is smaller, often has a yellowish centre of the cap and differs in microscopic features.

owocnik: Diameter 5–15 cm.
It is irregularly, wavily or brain-like bent, with lobes bent down to the base of the stem or strongly fused with it.
Its colour is from pale olive-yellow to ochre-yellow, darkening as it matures.
Hollow in the centre, whitish.
trzon: White or pale ochre; thick, relatively short, narrowing towards the base, less often somewhat bulbous, wavy-furrowed, with a smooth surface; chambered and hollow inside.
It is from 1/5 to 1/4 of the height of the head long and often just as wide as it.
It passes smoothly into the head.
miazsz: White, waxy and very brittle, with a mild taste, without smell.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid, with a finely warty surface, measuring 18–24 × 8–10 µm.
They are thickened at the ends.
podobne: Gyromitra esculenta is very similar.
It is much more common, smaller and usually darker in colour.

These features are not sufficient, however, to distinguish these species reliably; the fruit bodies of Gyromitra gigas are not large straight away, smaller specimens also occur among mature fruit bodies, and in Gyromitra esculenta similar, light-brown-coloured specimens occur.
These species can be reliably distinguished only by microscopic examination; in Gyromitra esculenta the spores are smooth and without thickenings at the ends.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–15 cm, hemispherical in young specimens, later flat-convex, finally flat and radially cracked.
It often has a small, blunt umbo.
Surface with distinct, fused fibrils, colour brown-grey, olive, grey-brown, smoke-brown.
spod: Very broad, distant and sinuately notched.
Their colour is from white to dirty white, sometimes they are veined in the lower part.
They have toothed or crenate edges and are rounded at the stem.
Springtails often live between the gills.
trzon: Height 6–15 cm, thickness 1–2 cm.
It is longitudinally fibrous, at first whitish, then grey-brown, paler than the cap.
At the stem base there are large rhizomorphs, which can reach a length of several metres.
They grow through the wood and soil, and the fruit bodies often appear only at some distance from the organic matter on which the fungus feeds.
miazsz: White and rather fibrous-tough.
Thin, so that the cap seen against the sun is translucent.
Taste mild, smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spores almost spherical, smooth, measuring 7–8 × 6–7 μm.
podobne: Pluteus cervinus.
It has free gills, which in older fruit bodies change colour to flesh-pink, brittle flesh and a salmon-pink spore print.
On the cystidia it has horn-like projections and it has denser gills.
Clitocybula lacerata.
It grows in the mountains on dead spruce wood, usually in clumps, and has smaller fruit bodies of a somewhat funnel-like shape.

owocnik: They always occur in groups, often numerous, and are arranged in overlapping tiers or fuse together.
They attach to the substrate by their side or by the whole base.
A single fruit body is spread out or spread out and bent back, bracket-shaped or semicircular, and is (2) 3-8 (10) cm wide and up to 2 cm thick.

Upper surface uneven, warty, radially folded and furrowed, velvety and yellow on young fruit bodies, later bare and increasingly darker: light ochre-brown, yellow-brown, reddish-brown, dark brown, finally almost black.
In young fruit bodies the margin is round, in older ones sharp, and it breaks off when bent back.
spod: Tubular.
Tubes 3–10 mm long, forming only one layer.
They are coloured from umber-cinnamon to ginger-rusty, in older fruit bodies they turn buff.
Pores round or angular, small (2-4 per 1 mm).
They are grey and covered with a greyish bloom, in older fruit bodies they become yellow-brown or rusty-red.
miazsz: Flesh rusty brown, watery and fleshy in young fruit bodies, then becoming increasingly dry, hard, corky and brittle.
It is up to 1 cm thick.
podobne: Mensularia nodulosa is morphologically similar and also forms clusters of fruit bodies, but it develops mainly on beeches, has smaller fruit bodies, and has long, awl-shaped setae in the hymenium.

owocnik: It is one of the largest tree-dwelling fungi, whose single rosettes reach a weight of up to a dozen or so kilograms, and clusters of fruit bodies at one trunk up to several tens of kilograms.
Annual fruit bodies, large, reaching a diameter of 30 to 80 cm, with many overlapping, fan-shaped or semicircular caps growing from a common base, sometimes on short stems.
Surface of the caps at first yellow-brown, later brownish, chestnut, distinctly concentrically banded, covered with small scales.
The margin of the caps is lighter, cream, rounded, wavy with age.
spod: Short, whitish, turning brown after damage and then blackening.
Pores very small, circular, about 0.3 mm in diameter.
miazsz: White, fibrous-tough, fibrous, turning black on a section, with a strong mushroomy smell and a sourish taste.
podobne: Grifola frondosa, which occurs almost exclusively on oaks and has much smaller and narrower caps.
Bondarzewia mesenterica, which grows at the base of fir trees and is characterised by large, angular and uneven pores and by flesh that does not blacken on cutting.

owocnik: An annual jelly-like (tremelloid) fungus 1–5 cm wide, exceptionally up to 12 cm, up to 3 cm thick.
Shape semicircular, spread out or spread out and reflexed.
It is attached to the substrate sideways.
On a vertical substrate it forms fan-shaped, semicircular or shell-shaped lobes with wavy margins.
Upper surface rough, mossy, coloured from whitish through cream to yellow-orange.
Cap margin sharp, wavy, rolled under and without hymenophore over a width of about 5 mm.
spod: Tubular, in the form of irregular pits (labyrinths), yellow-ochre, pink or rusty-brown.
The tubes form only one layer and are separated from the flesh by a darker line.
Edges of the tubes smooth in young fruit bodies, toothed in older ones.
The pits are surrounded by fine folds in the form of a net.
There are 2-4 pores per mm.
They are round to elongated in shape, sometimes irregular.
miazsz: Soft and gelatinous in young fruit bodies, elastic, rubbery, fleshy in older ones, finally waxy-gelatinous, fleshy-waxy in older individuals, in colour from whitish to orange-yellow.
podobne: Phlebia radiata has a similar waxy-gelatinous consistency, but its fruit bodies are usually spread out and it does not form such a distinctly maze-like hymenophore.

owocnik: Mostly 3–10 cm tall and 3–7 cm in diameter, beige or ochre in colour (sometimes grey or almost black), of oval or conical habit (hollow inside), attached to the stem, with irregular alveoli (pits) on the surface, between which the ribs are arranged in a way that does not distinguish any direction.
trzon: 2–6 cm long and 2–4 cm in diameter.
Cream, yellow or whitish in colour, hollow inside, with a rough or granular surface.
In mature fruit bodies the base of the stem is widened and folded.
miazsz: Whitish, brittle, of waxy consistency, mild taste and spicy fragrance.
podobne: Gyromitra esculenta and Gyromitra gigas – have a head that is not so elongated but broad and folded like a brain,
Morchella crassipes – is larger and has a thick stem, which moreover is granular and warty at the top.

owocnik: Conical in shape, sometimes egg-shaped, in different specimens markedly different in size.
Height 3–15 cm, diameter 2–9 cm.
Surface ribbed; between tall and thin vertical ribs there are alveoli forming vertical rows of 12-20, separated by low ridges.

The ribs are in colour from pale to dark grey, with age becoming dark grey-brown to almost black, the alveoli from grey to dark grey when immature, to grey-brown, greyish-olive or brownish-yellow when mature.
trzon: 3–10 cm high and 2–6 wide, hollow inside, very brittle.
Surface smooth, bare, crenate in mature specimens, at first whitish, then yellowish or ochre.
It is often slightly thicker near the base.
Its whitish to pale brownish surface is smooth or finely mealy with whitish granules.
miazsz: The flesh is whitish to watery brown, 1–3 mm thick in the hollow cap; in the stem this tissue is sometimes arranged in chambers or layers.
The sterile inner surface of the cap is whitish and hairy (covered with short, soft hairs).

owocnik: Shape from bell-shaped to bell-conical, in different specimens markedly different in size.
Height 2–8 cm, diameter 1.4 cm.
It is attached to the stem with its upper part; the lower 1/3 to 1/2 is free.
Surface ribbed, between the tall and thin vertical ribs there are alveoli forming vertical rows separated by low ridges.
The alveoli are coloured from yellow-brown through light brown to olive-brown, the ribs and ridges from dark brown to blackish-brown.
trzon: Tall in relation to the head (5–12 cm) and thick (1–3 cm), hollow inside, very brittle.
Surface smooth, bare, crenate in mature specimens, at first whitish, then yellowish or ochre.
miazsz: 2–3 mm thick, waxy, brittle, white.
Smell pleasant, spicy, fairly strong.
podobne: Morchella elata is distinguished by its dusted stem.
Verpa bohemica has a head attached only at the apex.

owocnik: Mostly 3–10 cm tall and 3–7 cm in diameter, beige or ochre in colour (sometimes grey or almost black), of oval or conical habit (hollow inside), attached to the stem, with irregular alveoli (pits) on the surface, between which the ribs are arranged in a way that does not distinguish any direction.
trzon: 2–6 cm long and 2–4 cm in diameter.
Cream, yellow or whitish in colour, hollow inside, with a rough or granular surface.
In mature fruit bodies the base of the stem is widened and folded.
miazsz: Whitish, brittle, of waxy consistency, mild taste and spicy fragrance.
podobne: Gyromitra esculenta and Gyromitra gigas – have a head that is not so elongated but broad and folded like a brain,
Morchella crassipes – is larger and has a thick stem, which moreover is granular and warty at the top.

owocnik: It forms slender, club-shaped fruit bodies measuring 5–17 × 1–2(3) mm.
They are mostly single, rarely branched.
They are in colour from white to cream, older fruit bodies sometimes have a pinkish tinge.
At the top they are mostly darker.
The fruit body grows from a delicate primary thallus forming a thin layer on the surface of the trunk, composed of white hyphae of the fungus and green algae of the genus Coccomyxa.
Young fruit bodies (the so-called egg): ovoid, up to about 4 cm tall and 2.5 cm wide, whitish.
The mature fruit body reaches 16 cm in height and 1 cm in thickness.
Cap cone-shaped, covered with a sticky dark olive spore mass.
After the spores have been shed, the upper part of the cap and the upper part of the stem are apricot or yellow-orange.
The smell of young fruit bodies is pleasant, resembling the smell of tobacco or fruit; older individuals have an odour similar to that of the stinkhorn (Phallus impudicus), but much weaker.
podobne: Mutinus ravenelii.

owocnik: At first it takes the form of an egg measuring 2–1.5 cm, covered with a white and smooth peridium.
The developing fruit body pierces the upper part of the peridium and grows upwards forming a cylindrical receptacle.
Sometimes part of the torn peridium remains at the top of the receptacle, forming a kind of little cap.
Height of the receptacle 6–7 cm, exceptionally up to 10 cm, thickness 1 cm.
It is cylindrical in shape, with a slightly narrowed base and a pointed top.
Inside, the receptacle is hollow; sometimes there is a small opening at the top.
The lower, sterile part of the receptacle is whitish with a raspberry tinge, sometimes completely white.
The upper, fertile part is strongly raspberry-coloured and covered with an olive-green, slimy spore mass, which produces a strong and very unpleasant smell similar to that of faeces or rotting meat.
With this smell it attracts carrion-feeding insects, which land on the fruit body, and spores stick to their legs, being carried by the insects often over considerable distances.
It has also been observed that the fruit bodies of this fungus are eagerly eaten by dogs without harm to their health.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–25 (–38) mm, shape conical, bell-shaped or parabolic with a small umbo, shallowly furrowed, slightly translucent-striate.
Surface dusted, in the centre coloured from dark red through orange-brown to grey-brown, paler near the margin – whitish or greyish, with yellow-red to orange-red spots.
spod: 15–20 of them reaching the stem, narrow, with yellow-red to orange-red spots.
trzon: Height 50–95 mm, thickness 1–2 mm, cylindrical, hollow inside, straight or slightly bent, firm.
Surface delicately or strongly hairy, more or less shiny, at the base in colour from bright orange to reddish, rooting.
When cut it exudes saffron-red milk.
The base is densely covered with long, thick fibres, whitish to orange-yellow in colour.
miazsz: Without a distinct smell.
podobne: The most characteristic features of Mycena crocata are spots in colours from yellow-red to orange-red, and reddish milk in the stem.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–3 cm, at first bell-shaped, later bell-shaped to arched and usually with a flat umbo.
The stripes of the gills show through.
Margin toothed.
Surface smooth, radially grooved, sticky and slippery.
It has a very varied colour; yellow-greenish, yellow-brown, greenish, ochre or grey-yellowish.
The top of the cap is darker than the margins. Hygrophanous – whitish when dry.
In mature fruit bodies it is sometimes covered with brown spots.
When pressed it discolours to brown-red.
The skin is rubbery, easily peeled off the whole cap.
The lemon Mycena shows a great variety of colour forms.
In Poland, besides the typical form, two varieties have been described: green-stemmed (var. epipterygioides) and tree-dwelling (var. viscosa).
spod: Gilled; gills whitish or greyish, sometimes with brownish spots, broadly attached or decurrent on the stem, with a regular trama.
Gill edges gelatinous and easily separating.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness 1–3 mm, cylindrical, hollow inside, smooth, slippery, yellowish or green-yellowish in colour.
Like the cap it is covered with a slippery skin that is easily separated.
In young fruit bodies the whole surface is mealy, in older ones only the top and the base of the stem.
miazsz: Thin, white, with a musty taste and a smell somewhat similar to that of cucumbers.
podobne: Despite the great variety in cap colouring, the yellowstem Mycena is fairly easy to distinguish; it is characterised by a yellow stem and a gelatinous, easily peelable cap skin.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–6 cm, conical-bell-shaped in young specimens, flat with a small umbo in older ones, indistinctly wrinkled, bare.
It is horn-brownish, grey-brown or flesh-brownish in colour, darker in the centre.
spod: Gilled, gills distant, at first whitish, then always slightly pinkish or beige-pink, with a regular trama, sinuately adnate to the stem and joined by veins.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness 2–4 mm, cylindrical and hollow inside, hard, smooth, shiny, with a rooting base.
Colour whitish or greyish.
miazsz: In the stem tough-fibrous, with a weak mealy smell released on rubbing.
Taste of cucumber and meal.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid, measuring 9–12 × 6.5–9 μm and with a smooth surface, without a germ pore.
podobne: Mycena polygramma – is clearly distinguished by its furrowed stem, and in adult specimens the gills are not pinkish.
Mycena inclinata is distinguished by its cucumber-like smell and also does not have pink gills.
Mycena tintinnabulum grows only on deciduous trees and the fruit bodies appear only in late autumn and in winter.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–3 cm, hemispherical in young fruit bodies, later bell-shaped, in older ones conical-bell-shaped with an umbo.
Margin slightly toothed and usually hung with colourless hyphae (as if with a trim).
Surface smooth, grooved up to half of the cap, colour from flesh brown through reddish brown to pink-brown.
The centre is usually darker.
Damaged places turn blood red.
spod: Decurrent with a tooth on the stem or adnate to it.
Colour in young fruit bodies from whitish to pink, darker in older ones.
Edges smooth.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness up to 3.5 mm, cylindrical, hollow inside.
Surface of a similar colour to the cap, entirely covered with small flakes, so that it looks frosted.
Stem base usually felty.
miazsz: Very thin, a blood-red liquid comes out of the damaged one.
Taste mild, smell indistinct.
podobne: Mycena haematopus is easy to distinguish from other Mycena species thanks to the blood-red fluid that exudes from a pressed or otherwise damaged spot.
In dry weather it may not exude the characteristic blood-red milk, but even then it is easy to distinguish by its frosted stem and the usually shaggy margin of the cap.
Mycena sanguinolenta is similar, for example, but is much smaller and does not grow on wood.

kapelusz: Diameter 15–50 mm, at first hemispherical or bell-shaped, then flat-convex, shallowly grooved, translucently striate.
It is hygrophanous.
Surface bare, slightly slimy when moist, in colour from date-brown to pale purple-brown or pale lilac-brown.
When dry, from the centre outwards pale ochre or beige with or without a pinkish tinge.
spod: 29–50 reaching the stem, ventricose, narrowly attached or decurrent with a small tooth, smooth or transversely ribbed, pale lilac grey-brown, pale violet-brown, densely dotted with dark violet-brown dots (pleurocystidia).
Edges dark violet-brown.
trzon: Height 25–80 mm, thickness 2–8 mm, hollow in the middle, brittle, tough, cylindrical or widening towards the base, straight or bent, sometimes laterally flattened.
Surface coarsely fibrous or flocculose, whitish with a slightly yellowish, brownish or lilac tinge, longitudinally striate with dark violet-brown fibres.
Base densely white-woolly.
miazsz: It has a strong radish smell and taste.
podobne: Mycena pelianthina is easily recognised by its large size, violet colour or violet tinge and radish smell.
A similar Mycena lammiensis occurs in North America, but it is absent in Poland.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–12 mm, hemispherical, parabolic, broadly conical to convex, sometimes with a small papilla, often slightly flattened in the middle, furrowed, translucent-striate.
Surface dusted, shimmering, dark blue, bluish-grey or grey, turning brown with age.
spod: 8–14 in number reaching the stem, fairly broad, convex, broadly attached and decurrent with a short tooth, grey to pale bluish-grey or grey-white, with age becoming pale sepia-brown,.
Edges lighter.
trzon: Height 5–25 mm, thickness 0.2–1 mm, straight or bent.
Surface flocculose-dusted, from grey to bluish grey, more brownish with age.
The base is densely covered with long, white fibrils.
miazsz: Without smell.
podobne: The blue-grey Mycena often grows on the same stump together with the purple-brown Mycena (Mycena meliigena).
The blue-grey Mycena is more common.
Young fruit bodies of these species are easy to distinguish, but with age they become brown and difficult to tell apart.
They are also similar microscopically.
The feature by which they can be distinguished is the size and shape of the terminal cells of the hyphae of the stem skin.
In the bluish-grey bonnet they are squat, no longer than 37 µm.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–6 cm, shape at first convex to bell-shaped, then spread out.
Surface bare, at first lilac-violet, later whitish, yellowish, pink-brown or reddish.
spod: Moderately crowded, sinuately attached to the stem, in colour from whitish to grey-white, often tinged pink or violet.
Near the stem often joined by anastomoses.
trzon: Height 4–10 cm, thickness 0.4–0.6 cm, cylindrical, hollow, brittle.
Surface glossy, smooth or with fine hairs, whitish or of the colour of the cap.
miazsz: Watery, whitish or greyish in colour.
Smell and taste distinctly resembling radish.
podobne: Mycena pura can easily be confused with the poisonous Mycena rosea, as it often has the same pink colouring and the two species are morphologically similar.
Mycena pelianthina is also similar.

The lilac bonnet is most easily distinguished from them by the radish-like smell and taste; other features are also helpful in distinguishing these species: the pink bonnet does not occur in coniferous forests, the dove-coloured bonnet has darker gills and darker coloured gill edges.
Growing in broadleaved forests, the violet-ish Mycena is morphologically difficult to tell apart from the pink Mycena.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–3 cm, bell-shaped in young fruit bodies, later broadly bell-shaped, finally arched.
Edges usually toothed.
Surface smooth.
It is hygrophanous.
In dry weather it is matt, radially fibrous, and pinkish in colour with a darker top.
In wet weather it becomes furrowed with the gills showing through, and has a colour from yellow-brown to red-brown.
It usually has a smaller or larger umbo.
spod: Broad, decurrent with a small tooth, white or slightly pinkish, with smooth edges.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness 2–4 mm.
It is cylindrical and hollow.
Surface smooth, bare, shiny, golden yellow or orange-yellow in colour.
A felty mycelium is present at the base.
miazsz: Thin, watery, brittle, yellow in the stem, whitish in the cap.
Taste mild, similar to radish; the smell of young fruit bodies is like chlorine, that of older ones like radish.
podobne: Mycena inclinata.
It also grows on rotting wood, but has greyish gills and the stem in the lower part is reddish-brown,
Mycena alcalina.
It is distinguished by a smell of ammonia.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm, spherical when young, then flat, finally fully spread out.
In the centre it has an umbo.
It is markedly hygrophanous; when wet the cap is striate because the gills show through.
Colour from pale pink to pink, whereas the umbo in dry weather has a cream-yellow or yellow colour as a result of drying out.
spod: Distant, bellied, and notched and narrow at the stem.
Gill edges smooth.
At first they are white, with time they become pale pink.
trzon: Height 4–7 cm, thickness up to 0.7 cm, cylindrical, straight, with a slightly thickened base.
In young specimens it is solid, in older ones tubular.
Colour whitish or whitish-pink, surface delicately fibrous.
miazsz: Thin, white, with a weak taste and smell of radish.
wysyp: Spores broadly elliptical, amyloid, with a smooth surface.
On one side they have a bent-back beak.
podobne: It can be confused with Mycena pura, also called the pure bonnet.
This bonnet has a more violet tinge and occurs in coniferous forests.

kapelusz: Diameter 0.5–2 cm, bluntly bell-shaped in young ones, later conical, finally spread out.
The centre of the cap is usually flat.
The gills show through, so that the cap is radially striate.
It is hygrophanous; when wet it is sticky.
Surface bare, smooth, silky shiny, coloured brown, sepia, grey-brown, or dark reddish-brown, sometimes dark chocolate-brown.
spod: Gilled, gills attached and slightly decurrent with a small tooth, with wavy edges. Lamellulae are present.
At first the gills are pale grey with a pinkish tinge, later flesh-pinkish.
trzon: Height 1–7 cm, thickness 1–3 mm, tubular, bent, hard and cartilaginous.
Surface smooth, slightly sticky when moist, shiny when dry.
Colour pale grey, beige, often reddish at the base and passing into a pseudorhiza covered with spreading white hyphae.
miazsz: Very thin, beige-grey, with an indistinct, bitter taste.
It has a smell similar to potato peelings or chlorine.
The smell quickly fades.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid or stone-shaped with an indistinct beak, with a smooth surface, amyloid and hyaline.
podobne: Several similar species of small bonnet mushrooms grow on dead wood, however the late time of appearance of this bonnet and its formation of compact clumps make it easy to distinguish from other bonnets.
In winter, on dead wood, the velvet shank also grows in clusters, but it differs in appearance.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–5 cm, shape at first parabolic or conical, with a rounded umbo, gradually flattening.
It is grooved up to 2/3 of the diameter.
Margin uneven.
Surface smooth, matt in dry weather, coloured from dirty whitish, through light cream and light pink to flesh-brown.
The apex of the cap is distinctly darker.
On the cap there are rusty-brown, radiating spots.
spod: Broad and fairly distant, attached or weakly sinuate.
They are white-grey, in older specimens red-brown spots appear on them.
Transverse anastomoses often occur.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness up to 4 mm.
It is cylindrical, hollow inside (tube-like).
Surface fibrillose, grey-brown, covered with short white fibres only at the top.
White hairs also occur at the base of the stem.
miazsz: Thin, watery and brittle.
Colour grey, taste mild, smell similar to radish.
podobne: There are many Mycena species, but this one is morphologically fairly easy to recognise by the rusty-red spots on the cap.
Young fruit bodies may not yet have these spots, but they can be recognised by their relatively large caps, numerous gills and colour.
Mycena maculata also has rusty-brown spots on the cap, but the lower part of the stem is pink-violet-brown, and it grows on rotting wood.

owocnik: Partly underground, usually up to 8 cm in diameter, but sometimes even up to 20 cm.
It has a fairly variable shape.
It may be hemispherical, ovoid, pear-shaped or irregularly flattened.
The base ends in a thick mycelial cord, sometimes resembling a stem.
Peridium up to 0.5 cm thick.
Its outer, parchment-like, matt, thin and smooth layer (exoperidium) stays pale for a long time; at first whitish, then white-yellow, finally grey-brown.
Fairly early it falls off in flakes, exposing the thick inner layer (endoperidium).
In young fruit bodies it is soft, fleshy and pale, then gradually becomes leathery, corky, brittle, grey-brown.
As the spores mature, the endoperidium gradually splits at the top and opens out, forming several irregular lobes.
At this point it resembles in appearance the fruit bodies of Geastrum (earthstars).
Soon, however, these lobes break off in pieces.
In young fruit bodies the gleba is white, becoming increasingly darker as it matures: olive, brown-olive, finally chocolate.
No subgleba and columella.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–4 cm, shape at first bell-shaped, later convex, finally spread out.
Colour quite variable; from pale ochre to dark brown.
Surface matt, dry, sometimes wrinkled, margin smooth or grooved.
spod: Dirty whitish or greyish, with a regular trama.
trzon: Thin and long.
It is up to 10 cm tall and 1–2 mm thick.
Surface matt, black-brown or black and frosted white (felty).
Base rooting.
It is tough, fibrous, of cartilaginous consistency and so elastic that it cannot be broken.
miazsz: Thin, whitish.
It has a mild taste and a strong smell of garlic.
wysyp: Spores from broadly ellipsoid to almost spherical in shape, smooth, measuring 7–11 × 6–8 µm.
podobne: Mycetinis scorodonius.
It also has a garlic smell, but it is smaller and grows in coniferous forests.
Its stem is not black, but purple-brown.

kapelusz: Diameter up to 20 cm, semicircular in young specimens, spread out in older ones.
The cap surface is at first dry, suede-like, later smooth and bare.
Colour dark brown, sometimes with ochre spots.
spod: Long and notched at the stem.
In young fruit bodies yellow to olive, in older specimens – rusty.
When damaged they turn strongly blue.
trzon: Height 5–15 cm, thickness 2–5 cm.
In young specimens the stem is usually swollen, then club-shaped, barrel-shaped.
Solid.
Colour yellow, covered very densely with brick-red irregular hyphae (not a net).
In the upper part of the stem there are fewer hyphae, which makes the stem more yellow here.
miazsz: Yellow; when cut or damaged it quickly changes colour to dark blue.
Taste mild, smell faint.
podobne: Young fruit bodies may be confused with Caloboletus calopus, because both mushrooms often occur together in the same area.

The most important features distinguishing the brick-pored red bolete (Neoboletus) are: hyphae on the stem instead of a reticulum, red tubes instead of yellow (only in older fruit bodies) and a darker cap.
Suillellus queletii is also similar, but it has an olive-brown, orange-red or brick-red cap, orange pores and a stem that is carmine-red at the base.

kapelusz: Diameter up to 20 cm, semicircular in young specimens, spread out in older ones.
The cap surface is at first dry, suede-like, later smooth and bare.
Colour dark brown, sometimes with ochre spots.
spod: Long and notched at the stem.
In young fruit bodies yellow to olive, in older specimens – rusty.
When damaged they turn strongly blue.
trzon: Height 5–15 cm, thickness 2–5 cm.
In young specimens the stem is usually swollen, then club-shaped, barrel-shaped.
Solid.
Colour yellow, covered very densely with brick-red irregular hyphae (not a net).
In the upper part of the stem there are fewer hyphae, which makes the stem more yellow here.
miazsz: Yellow; when cut or damaged it quickly changes colour to dark blue.
Taste mild, smell faint.
podobne: Young fruit bodies may be confused with Caloboletus calopus, because both mushrooms often occur together in the same area.

The most important features distinguishing the brick-pored red bolete (Neoboletus) are: hyphae on the stem instead of a reticulum, red tubes instead of yellow (only in older fruit bodies) and a darker cap.
Suillellus queletii is also similar, but it has an olive-brown, orange-red or brick-red cap, orange pores and a stem that is carmine-red at the base.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–11 cm, conical when young, later flat with a blunt umbo or shallowly depressed in the centre.
Surface matt, dry, coloured from cream to light brown, covered with adhering, darker (brown) scales.
These scales are larger in the centre, finer towards the cap margin.
spod: Broad and broadly attached, on the stem decurrent as far as the annular zone.
They have wavy and toothed edges.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness up to 2 cm, cylindrical or conical, solid and springy.
Surface whitish; above the ring zone young specimens have a felty sheath, below it the stem is covered with scales, and the base itself is brown to black-brown in colour.
miazsz: Soft in young specimens, springy, hard and woody in older ones.
Colour whitish, smell sweetish-aniseed, taste indistinct.

owocnik: They have a very variable shape, they may be cushion-shaped, hoof-shaped, shelf-shaped, irregular.
They are attached to the substrate by the side, and neighbouring fruit bodies often grow together.
A single fruit body is 3–12 (exceptionally up to 20) cm wide.
Margin rounded, blunt, broad, wavy.
Upper surface uneven, usually warty, folded or furrowed, velvety or felty in young fruit bodies, smooth in older ones.
Its colour ranges from yellow-orange through ochre to cinnamon.
With age the colour becomes increasingly darker, to rusty brown or even black.
The margin is usually lighter.
spod: Tubular, at first lemon-yellow in colour, later grey-ochre.
The tubes formed in successive years form clearly visible layers.
They are 5-10 (15) mm long, shorter at the margin of the fruit body.
Pores angular, elongated or maze-like, 1-2 per 1 mm of length.
miazsz: Corky, colour from fawn to cinnamon.
A characteristic feature is the strong aniseed smell.
Taste mild, slightly bitter in older fruit bodies.
wysyp: Spores cylindrical, ellipsoid with sharply ending bases.
They are flattened on one side, smooth, colourless, usually with one droplet in the middle.
podobne: The aniseed smell in combination with the colour of the fruit bodies makes it easy to distinguish from other species.
This fungus is, however, very variable morphologically.
In specific conditions (e.g. in the absence of light in mines) it forms monstrous, strongly deformed fruit bodies without a hymenophore.
Sometimes it forms a hymenophore with strongly elongated pores, similar to gills.
Gloeophyllum trabeum is similar.
It can also be confused with Ischnoderma benzoinum or Ischnoderma resinosum.
Seen from above, Gloeophyllum sepiarium is similar, but it has a hymenophore that is usually gilled, a sharp cap margin and is more yellow.

owocnik: One-sidedly ear-shaped, usually with a slit down to the base, bent, slightly rooting and white-felty; spore-bearing layer strongly orange to yellow; on the outside delicately mealy.
Up to 4 cm wide.
Flesh white, without smell, with a mild taste.
podobne: A whole series of species is known that are difficult to distinguish.
Otidea leporina differs only in its rusty yellow colour when young, and later cinnamon-brown.
In beech forests the relatively rare Otidea conccinna occurs; it has fruit bodies growing densely, strongly lemon-yellow, rolled and split on one side.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–10 cm, hemispherical in young specimens, then increasingly flat, finally spread out with a blunt umbo.
Margin sharp, wrinkled-striate.
Surface pure white or whitish, ivory-coloured, sometimes ochre at the top, sometimes translucent.
In wet weather very sticky, slimy and gluey, in dry weather silkily dull, smooth.
spod: White, broad, bulging, distant, straight adnate, sinuately notched to slightly decurrent.
trzon: Height 4–10 cm, thickness 0.5–1 cm, cylindrical, solid, hard, often bent.
Surface smooth, sticky and whitish, brownish only at the bottom.
It has a large drooping or flaring ring.
miazsz: White, very thin and soft in the cap, fibrous and hard in the stem.
Taste mild, no smell.
It does not change colour after damage.
wysyp: Spores almost spherical, smooth, measuring 14–18 × 12–16 µm.
podobne: It is hard to confuse with other species of fungi, because none of the species growing on wood has such a pure white, porcelain-shiny and slippery cap.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–12 cm, in young fruit bodies bell-shaped, later flat-arched, finally flat.
In the centre it usually has a blunt umbo.
Surface smooth, shiny and sticky in wet weather, drying out in dry weather.
Often characteristically wrinkled.
Shiny, ochre, yellow-brown, yellow-grey in colour.
The skin can be easily peeled off.
spod: Distant, of various lengths, rounded or notched with a tooth at the stem, white.
trzon: Height 10–20 cm, thickness 5–12 mm.
Cylindrical, usually thickened in the lower part, solid in young fruit bodies, tubular in older ones.
An elongated, thinner rooting underground part, up to 30 cm long, with twisted fibres.
Surface smooth, delicately longitudinally crenate, whitish, brownish at the bottom.
miazsz: Brittle, white, not changing colour when damaged.
Taste mild, smell indistinct.
podobne: Xerula pudens has a dry cap, without wrinkles, and does not have a rooting stem,
Hydropus subalpinus has a cap without wrinkles and with a sharper tip.
A rare species.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–3 cm, flesh-brown to red-brown, very hygrophanous, often two-coloured at the place of growth, changing colour from the top while drying to pale beige to whitish-flesh.
Skin dry.
Margin when moist distinctly, translucently grooved far inward.
spod: At first grey-beige, later dark brown, characteristically variegated on the surfaces, attached at the top.
Gill edges paler.
trzon: Paler than the cap, slightly translucent, whitish when drying, delicately downy all over.
wysyp: Spores lemon-shaped, distinctly rough, measuring (11.5)14–17(22) × (7.5)8.5–11 µm.
podobne: It is often confused with Psilocybe semilanceata.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–2 cm, shape shell-shaped, hemispherical or kidney-shaped.
Colour whitish, in older specimens turning clay-brown or red-brown.
Surface delicate, felty on young fruit bodies, smooth on older ones.
It is rubbery, sticky and can be easily peeled.
spod: Crowded and decurrent on the stem.
They are white, with coloured, streak-like discolourations on the edges.
trzon: Length 2–5 mm, thickness 3–5 mm.
It grows from the side, is short, triangular in cross-section and solid.
Surface white, covered with small scales.
Sometimes there is no stem.
miazsz: Thin, tough-fibrous, white.
Taste mild, no smell.
podobne: It may be confused with Crepidotus mollis, which differs, among other things, in having no stem, or with Pleurocybella porrigens, which also has no stem and is larger.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–4 cm, round or kidney-shaped, with a wavy and inrolled margin.
Ochre colour.
Skin of the cap matt, at first smooth, in older specimens scaly with a mosaic pattern.
spod: Crowded and distinctly delimited from the stem.
Colour from pale beige to ochre-brown.
trzon: Height 1–2 cm, thickness 0.5 cm.
It grows from the side, is short and very broad at the point of connection with the cap.
Surface felty, colour ochre-brown.
miazsz: Thin, tough-fibrous, ochre in colour.
Smell faint, taste bitter, strongly astringent.
wysyp: Spores smooth, broadly ellipsoid, very small, measuring 2–3 × 1–1.5 μm.

kapelusz: Width 4–12 cm, shape shell-shaped or tongue-shaped, funnel-like depressed in the centre.
Surface smooth or velvety, lilac in young specimens, in older ones in colour from ochre to red-brown.
spod: Deeply decurrent on the stem, crowded, in colour from pale lilac to ochre.
trzon: Height 1–3 cm, thickness 1–2 cm, off-centre, surface felty, colour from ochre-brown to lilac.
miazsz: Whitish, bast-like and leathery.
podobne: Lentinus suavissimus is similar, but differs in its aniseed smell, is smaller and grows only on willows.

owocnik: Irregularly folded with two, more rarely three or four, upward-directed, inverted cornet-shaped folds, giving it the appearance of a mitre; dark chestnut or red-brown.
In particularly favourable conditions the fruit body (head together with stem) can reach a height of even up to 20 cm, but as a rule it is much smaller.
trzon: White; usually of equal thickness at the top and the bottom, sometimes flattened, swollen at the top and somewhat folded and narrowed at the base; solid when young, later chambered and hollow.
miazsz: White, brittle, with an indistinct taste and smell.
podobne: Gyromitra esculenta is similar, but it has a more brain-like folded head and occurs only in early spring.
Gyromitra ambigua is almost indistinguishable macroscopically.
It is usually smaller, darker and has a violet-brown colouring, but certainty is given only by microscopic analysis.
It is very rare and under partial species protection.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–10 cm, arched when young with an inrolled margin, later concave, finally funnel-shaped with a thin and inrolled margin.
No umbo, skin bare, smooth, slightly hygrophanous, coloured from yellowish through yellow-ochre and reddish-ochre to orange-brown.
Sometimes the cap is concentrically spotted and bent in waves.
spod: Thin, crowded and decurrent on the stem.
Colour at first whitish and white-cream, later yellow-rusty to ochre-red.
trzon: Height 3–5 cm, thickness 0.7–1.2 cm, cylindrical, solid when young, later hollow, sometimes club-like thickened at the bottom, fibrous.
Colour similar to the cap.
Sometimes it is eccentric (that is, it does not grow exactly from the centre of the cap).
miazsz: Springy, whitish in young mushrooms, later light buff to cream-ochre.
Smell aromatic, taste astringent.
podobne: Infundobulicybe gibba.
It has a paler colour and sparse flesh.
the poisonous Clitocybe rivulosa.
It has a velvety cap and a sweetish smell.

kapelusz: At maturity it reaches a diameter of 1–6 cm.
At first it is ovoid, then slightly conical or convex, finally almost flat.
Deeply grooved radially over almost the whole surface.
Surface smooth to the naked eye, finely hairy under a lens, orange-brown in young fruit bodies, greyish in older ones.
No remains of a partial veil.
spod: Free or almost free, moderately crowded, at first whitish, then dark grey, finally black.
trzon: Height 3–12 cm, diameter up to 3 mm, cylindrical, brittle, hollow inside.
Surface smooth or delicately silky, coloured from whitish to slightly yellowish.
Ring absent.
miazsz: Thin, without smell and taste.
podobne: Among small fungi with blackening gills growing in grass or wood chips, Parasola auricoma stands out by both macroscopic and microscopic features.

Its characteristic features are the lack of remains of a cortina, in young fruit bodies the cap rusty-brown to orange-brown, and in older ones grey-striate and resembling a parasol, with only the central part remaining orange-brown.
Under the microscope Parasola auricoma has fairly large, ellipsoid spores and a cap surface decorated with very long, red-brown hairs.
Parasola plicatilis is the most similar, but its young fruit bodies are not orange-brown, and under the microscope the differences are considerable.

kapelusz: Height 2–5 cm.
Shape conical or bell-shaped, in older specimens the margin is slightly inrolled.
It is never flat.
It is hygrophanous; when wet it is red-brown in colour and grooved (translucent gills), when dry pale ochre.
It has no veil, but characteristic of this species are long hairs (up to 0.5 mm long), visible however only through a lens.
spod: In young specimens light grey-brown, in older ones dark brown.
Edges of the gills covered with white cilia (visible only through a hand lens).
trzon: Height up to 2 cm, thickness 2–5 mm, cylindrical, thin, brittle.
Surface smooth, whitish.
miazsz: Whitish, taste and smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid, smooth, measuring 14–19 × 7–8.5 μm, staining dark brown with KOH.
podobne: Morphologically it is difficult to distinguish Parasola conopilus with the naked eye from some similar species of the genus Parasola and some Psathyrella, but it is easy to do so with microscopic examination, because Parasola conopilus is characterised by many different details in the structure of the cystidia and spores.
Already with a lens its very long hairs can easily be noticed, which do not occur in any of the similar species.

kapelusz: Cap at first cylindrical, 5–10 mm in diameter, then successively ellipsoid or egg-shaped, hemispherically convex, horizontally flattened, flat-convex, with a slightly concave centre.
When mature it reaches a diameter of up to 3.5 cm.
At first smooth, then deeply grooved from the margin almost to the centre.
The gills show through, in mature specimens in the form of deep, radial and parallel furrows.
Surface at first yellowish honey to pale brown in colour, later grey, only the centre has a cinnamon tinge.
The margin quickly becomes crenate.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness 1–2 mm, cylindrical, delicate and hollow inside.
Base slightly thickened and somewhat downy.
Surface smooth, sometimes somewhat longitudinally silky.
Colour at first whitish, then pale ochre.
Ring absent.
spod: Fairly sparse, notched, thin, up to 2 mm wide, sometimes slightly bulging.
In young fruit bodies the edges are fringed.
At first white, then grey from the spores, finally deliquescing.
miazsz: Very thin and brittle, white.
Without a distinct smell or taste.
podobne: Most similar are: Parasola auricoma, Pseudocoprinus lacteus, Parasola leiocephala and Parasola lilatincta.
A reliable distinction between them is possible only by analysing microscopic structural features.
A characteristic feature of P. plicatilis is the large, angular spores with eccentric germ pores.
P. leiocephala is practically identical morphologically.
Microscopically it is distinguished by smaller and more angular spores.

kapelusz: Diameter reaches 13 cm.
In young specimens it is gently arched with a distinctly rolled-under margin, later flat or slightly concave, but still with a rolled-under margin.
Colour yellow-brown, olive, ochre-brown, red-brown.
Young specimens have a delicately felty cap, which later becomes bald.
When damaged the cap skin is spotted dark brown.
In dry weather the cap is dry and shiny, in wet weather it becomes very slimy.
spod: Thin, crowded and clearly decurrent on the stem.
In young fungi wavy.
They are yellowish or rusty in colour, turning brown when damaged.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness 1–2 cm.
It is cylindrical, thick, solid, bare and sometimes narrowed in the lower part.
Colour close to that of the cap, usually slightly paler.
It turns brown when damaged.
miazsz: Yellow, yellowish white or pale ochre, at first hard, later soft; when the mushroom is cut it changes colour to red-brown or rusty brown; taste slightly sour, smell not very intense
podobne: Similar is Paxillus filamentosus.
It has a scaly cap and grows only under alders.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–10 cm, in young specimens flat and almost spread out, in older ones funnel-shaped concave.
Margins even, at first inrolled and felty, later straightening.
Skin light brown, radially torn and covered with darker, grey-brown or olive-brown or black scales strongly fused with the skin.
spod: Narrow and crowded, decurrent on the stem.
At first they are yellowish, then darken and have a rusty colour.
When pressed they stain red-brown.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness 0.8–1.5 cm, cylindrical at the bottom, widening towards the top.
Colour at first yellowish, later red-brown.
podobne: Paxillus rubicundulus resembles in colour and habit the poisonous Paxillus involutus, but it is smaller and set somewhat asymmetrically, more funnel-shaped, bent, and has a distinctly thinner cap and stem.

owocnik: Annual, spread out, or spread out with a turned-back margin.
Single ones are circular in shape, but often neighbouring fruit bodies merge with one another, forming a uniform coating.
They are strongly attached to the substrate.
During drought they shrink and crack.
The thickness of the fruit bodies is 0.2–2 mm and varies with the weather; they are thicker in wet weather and thinner in dry weather.

In young specimens the whole surface of the fruit body adheres to the substrate, and its margin is delicately fringed, whitish and fibrous; in older fruit bodies the margin stands away from the substrate and curls under.
The outer side of the fruit body, standing away from the substrate, is rough, uneven and dark brown or black in colour, violet-blue on oaks growing on wet ground.
spod: It is found over the whole surface of the fruit body.
It is smooth, wrinkled, nodular, dull, radially folded, and cracked on older fruit bodies.
It is grey-pink, light brown, grey-violet in colour, turning brown in older specimens.
miazsz: Very thin.
Soft and waxy in young specimens, brittle and leathery in older ones.
wysyp: Spores cylindrical in shape, with a pointed base and curved like a sausage.
Surface smooth, dark pink in colour, size 10–12 × 3–4 μm.

owocnik: An annual bracket fungus consisting of a cap and a stem.
It produces fruit bodies singly or in groups, in which the fruit bodies often grow together at the bases.
kapelusz: It has a circular, semicircular, kidney-shaped or irregular shape, width 8–30 cm, thickness 1–4 cm.
Margin wavy or rolled under, incised in some places and usually without hymenophore.
Surface uneven, folded and knobbly, at first felty, hairy or villose, becoming bare with age.
Margin sulphur-yellow or yellow-ochre, centre from orange to dark red, base almost black.
trzon: Short, lateral or central, funnel-shaped or flattened.
It is covered with a hymenophore.
Dimensions: 3–8 × 2–5 cm.
miazsz: It is 1–1.5 cm thick.
In young fruit bodies spongy and juicy, with time it hardens.
After drying it becomes fibrous and corky, brittle and light.
Colour from orange to brown, darkening when pressed or under the influence of KOH.
It has a weak smell and a sourish taste.
spod: Tubular, labyrinthine, coloured yellow, rusty-yellow, ochre, olive-green; the tubes are up to 1 cm long and form only one layer, also running down the stem.
In young fruit bodies the edges of the tubes are thick, then thin, toothed in older ones.
Pores round, angular or irregular in shape and 0.3–2.5 mm in diameter.
In the hymenium there are cylindrical skeletocystidia with thin walls, exuding a tarry substance visible as drops on their tips.
podobne: Onnia tomentosa, but it has smaller fruit bodies and smaller pores with bristles.
It causes white rot of wood.

owocnik: Young fruit bodies: in the form of a spherical or ovoid egg.
The mature fruit body (receptacle) consists of a volva and a stem up to 20 cm long, usually 6–10 cm.
The colouring of the covering is violet-ish or pinkish.
It has a weaker smell than Phallus impudicus.
miazsz: The flesh of the stem is whitish, spongy, with numerous chambers, very brittle.
podobne: Very similar is a stinkhorn.
It differs in its less violet colouring, smaller disc at the top of the cap, stronger smell and place of occurrence.

inne: It is a fungus with an atypical structure.
The fruit body of young specimens is spherical or egg-shaped, white or cream in colour, sometimes with a yellow tinge.
It measures 4–6 × 3–5 cm and is attached to the substrate by mycelium resembling fairly thick cords.
It is partly hidden underground.
This is the so-called egg, also commonly called the devil's egg.
On a cross-section it can be seen that inside the egg envelope there is already the beginning of the fruit body.
During development the egg bursts and a more typical mature fruit body appears (the so-called receptacle).
Young fruit bodies have a faint smell similar to that of radish.
They resemble puffballs in appearance, but differ from them in the covering; it consists of two layers, between which there is a gelatinous mass.
As the fungus matures, the mass becomes more liquid and, after the veil has torn, covers the head of the receptacle.
It is 10–30 cm tall, cylindrical, narrow at the top, porous, brittle and hollow inside.
It is white, with a volva at the base and a weakly differentiated head at the top.
The head resembles morels in appearance.
It is several centimetres long, cone- or thimble-shaped, and covered with a green, gelatinous mass containing the spores.
The fungus gives off an unpleasant smell reminiscent of carrion.
For humans this smell can be perceived from quite a distance.
It attracts flies, which feed on the gelatinous mass and spores, spreading them in the process.
After the flies have eaten the gelatinous spore mass, the receptacle is white and has empty chambers on its surface.

Scientific studies have shown that the slimy spore-bearing mass of stinkhorns is eaten by the flies Calliphora vicina, Lucilia caesar, Lucilia ampullacea and Dryomyza anilis, and their liquid droppings contain a large number of spores.
podobne: Phallus hadriani.
It has a distinctly slightly violet or pinkish colour of the veil and a weaker smell.

owocnik: Attached to the substrate by the side, stem absent.
Width 15–25 cm, thickness 8–15 cm, shape at first bulbous, later flat or hoof-shaped.
Surface grey, darkening with time, sometimes cracked.
It is smooth or delicately suede-like, sometimes green from algae growing on it, and irregularly, concentrically zoned.
The skin is tough, the cap margin broad, rounded.
spod: Tubular.
The tubes form many layers, each up to 5 mm thick.
They are of the same colour as the fruit body, or paler.
Pores of the tubes very small, round.
miazsz: Thickness up to 2 cm.
It is woody, zoned and has a colour from dark rusty brown to chestnut brown.
podobne: Fomes fomentarius.
It has softer and paler flesh and is not so strongly attached to the trunk.
Phellinus hartigii, but it grows mainly on firs
Phellinus tremulae, but it grows only on aspen.

owocnik: Perennial, of very varied shape.
It may be spread out (resupinate), spread out and reflexed, cushion-shaped, knobbly, hoof-shaped, hemispherical, and also of irregular shape.
Size usually up to several cm, often individual fruit bodies fuse together or occur overlapping like roof tiles one above the other, forming large clusters.
Surface of young fruit bodies sand-ochre, later through cinnamon-yellow and yellow-brown it becomes chestnut, finally grey and almost black.
At first it is slightly mossy, but quickly becomes smooth, later cracked.
The margin of the fruit body (growth zone) is blunt, paler and has no hymenophore on it.
spod: Tubular, multi-layered.
Tubes 2–3 mm long, rusty-brown, in older fruit bodies sometimes overgrown with mycelium.
Pores yellow-ochre, later rusty, finally brown.
They are round or angular, sometimes elongated, 1–2 mm in diameter.
miazsz: Yellow-brown or rusty-brown, corky or woody.
wysyp: Spores almost spherical, with slightly pointed ends, a smooth surface and measuring 5–7 × 4–5.5 µm.
Setae very few, hard to notice.

kapelusz: A single one is circular with a concave centre and has a diameter of 2–6 cm, but often neighbouring caps fuse together into an irregular cap reaching a diameter of up to 20 cm.
Surface matt, felty, with radially fused fibres on it.
It is concentrically zoned, darker in the centre. It is grey or reddish-brown in colour, the margin is whitish.
spod: Spiny.
The spines are up to 3 mm long and slightly decurrent on the stem.
White in young fruit bodies, greyish in older ones.
trzon: Height 1–3 cm, thickness up to 0.8 cm.
It is cylindrical, straight or twisted.
Surface colour from light brown to dark brown.
Neighbouring stems are often joined by a compact mycelium that also permeates the substrate.
miazsz: In the cap it is light brown, in the stem reddish or dark brown.
It is zoned.
Taste and smell bitterish; when drying, the smell resembles Maggi seasoning.
podobne: Phellodon niger.
It has darker fruit bodies, in colour from blue-black to grey-black,
Phellodon confluens.
It is cream-coloured, coffee-with-milk-coloured, grey-brown.
Occurring mainly in broadleaved forests,
Phellodon melaleucus.
It has grey-black fruit bodies and occurs on sandy soils in pine and spruce forests,
Phellodon violascens.
It has a matt felty surface of whitish or pale grey-brown colour with a violet tinge.
It grows in spruce forests.

owocnik: A jelly (tremelloid) fungus.
Fruit bodies up to 8 mm thick, at first circular or oval, later spreading widely.
They are spread out flat and completely attached to the substrate, less often with a turned-back margin.
Margin ragged.
Individual fruit bodies, as they grow, fuse with neighbouring ones, covering a considerable area.
Colour pale flesh-pinkish or orange-reddish, with distinct veins or folds of the hymenophore running radially.
spod: In the form of folds and veins spreading radially.
Colour pale pink, orange to red, darkening with age to brown or turning grey.
miazsz: Gelatinous or fleshy-waxy.
wysyp: Spores cylindrical, granular and smooth, measuring 4.5–6 × 1.5–2.5 μm.
podobne: Phlebia tremellosa has a similar underside of the fruit body, but unlike the radiating crust fungus, which adheres tightly to the substrate, it usually forms small caps or projecting lobes.
Another similar species is the one called zylica olbrzymia in Polish.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–12 cm.
In young individuals it is conical, later hemispherical, and finally flat.
It is golden-yellow or rusty-yellow in colour with darker, adhering patches.
On young mushrooms there are remnants of the partial veil of the fruit body at the cap margin, but they are fairly quickly washed away by rain.
In wet weather and in young specimens the cap surface is sticky, even slimy.
spod: White when young, then olive and rusty brown with a serrated edge, adnate to the stem or slightly notched with a tooth.
trzon: Height 10–12 cm, thickness up to 1 cm.
It is fibrous and has the same colour as the cap, or is slightly paler.
Its ring consists of brown threads forming a woolly band, which later partly disappears.
Below the ring it is covered with brown fibrils, above it is yellowish mossy.
miazsz: Yellowish in the cap, slightly darker in the stem, without smell and not changing colour when damaged.
It has a mild taste.
podobne: Hemipholiota populnea grows on poplars and has a more massive fruit body with large whitish scales
Pholiota lucifera is smaller and paler, and its scales on the cap dissolve
Pholiota astragalina grows in the mountains on conifers, has a smaller cap but a longer stem, and its flesh darkens when damaged.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–6 cm.
In young individuals it is hemispherical, then hemispherical-arched, finally flat-arched.
It keeps a rolled-under margin for a long time.
Surface dry, slightly slippery in wet weather, in colour from lemon yellow to orange.
It is entirely covered with large, uniformly coloured scales, which also hang from the margin of the cap.
spod: Crowded, lemon yellow in young fruit bodies, then darkening to olive, finally rusty brown.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness up to 0.8 cm.
Cylindrical, solid in young fruit bodies, hollow in older ones.
It is smooth only in a narrow zone under the cap; otherwise it is entirely covered with standing fibres of a sulphur colour.
miazsz: Sulphur-yellow in colour, rusting slightly only at the margins.
Taste bitterish, smell somewhat radish-like.
podobne: The species most similar to it is Pholiota squarosa.
Its fruit bodies, however, are larger and of a slightly different colour (not so intensely yellow, more ochre).
It occurs on both coniferous and deciduous trees (more often on the latter).
Microscopic differences have also been found between these species: in the shaggy scalycap the gelatinous cuticle also occurs on the stem.
Pholiota tuberculosa is of similar colour, but has no protruding scales.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–15 cm.
In young individuals it is egg-shaped and closed, later hemispherical, and finally flat.
Its colour is ochre, ochre-brown to brown, darker in the centre.
Surface densely covered with protruding small scales.
Margin rolled under for a long time.
spod: Yellowish when young, then rusty-brown.
They are crowded, somewhat decurrent and adnate to the stem.
trzon: Height 4–8 cm, thickness up to 12 mm.
It is fibrous and has the same colour as the cap.
It has a ring.
Below the ring it is covered with scales, like the cap.
miazsz: Yellowish, not changing colour after damage.
It has a mild taste slightly resembling the taste of radish.
podobne: Pholiota squarrosoides is the most similar.
It has a pale cap margin and grows only on dead beech wood.
Somewhat similar is Gymnopilus junionus.
It has very bitter flesh, and its cap and stem have no scales.
Less experienced mushroom pickers may confuse it with Armillaria mellea.
It has only small scales, which are easily rubbed off with a finger, and moreover its fruit bodies are less massive.

kapelusz: Length 3–7 cm, width 2–5 cm, shape kidney-shaped, shell-shaped, usually attached sideways, sometimes spread out.
