spod: Decurrent, crowded, at first pale yellowish, then gradually changing colour to orange, yellow-cream and ochre.
miazsz: Yellowish, with a faint smell and a slightly bitter taste.
podobne: Often confused with Pleurotus ostreatus, which also grows on trees in late autumn, but the oyster mushroom is larger and has a steel-blue cap, without green tinges.
Also the yellow stem of Sarcomyxa serotina should rule out such a mistake.

owocnik: From 1 to 5 cm in diameter, at first spherical, then goblet-shaped, later more widely spread out, cup-shaped to bowl-shaped.
A mature one has less regular shapes – oval or kidney-shaped.
Old fruit bodies may be spread out like a saucer.
The cups are set on a distinct stalk, up to 3–5 cm long and 0.3 cm thick, whitish.
Sessile fruit bodies are rare.
The inner covering of the fruit bodies (hymenium) is brightly coloured, vivid red, scarlet, brick-red, smooth and shiny.
Outer surface pale pink, pale reddish, hairy, felty, covered with whitish tufts.
The margin of the fruit bodies stays rolled under for a long time.
miazsz: White, thin, bast-like, without taste and smell.
podobne: Sarcoscypha coccinea, which can be distinguished only microscopically.
It has straight hairs on the outer surface of the cups, and its spores are rounded at the ends.
It occurs more often in lowland areas.
Aleuria aurantia.
It has no stem, its colour is less bright, more orange, and it forms fruit bodies at the end of summer.

owocnik: At first almost spherical, then cup-shaped, in old age almost spread out.
Diameter 0.5–1.5(2) cm.
Stem absent or of trace size.
Margin usually distinctly inrolled inwards.
Upper side woolly, ochre in colour, whitish in dried fruit bodies.
The lower side with the hymenium is light brown, clay-coloured, reddish-brown or chocolate-coloured, smooth, slightly dusted and folded.
Flesh very thin, leathery, without a distinct smell or taste.
Diameter 1–4 cm, shape circular, semicircular, fan-shaped or shell-shaped.
It is attached to the substrate sideways.
Stem absent.
Surface felty, in colour from whitish to grey.
It is covered with bristles and is radially wavy or furrowed.
Sometimes it has a beige or pink tint.
It also happens that algae settle between the bristles, giving the cap a green colour.
spod: Grey to pale red-brown and in a group of fruit bodies it resembles longitudinally split gills, which is a characteristic feature of the genus Schizophyllum.
In dry weather they curl up, thus protecting the spores from drying out.
miazsz: Fleshy in young specimens, but quickly becomes bast-like and leathery.
In damp weather, however, it becomes pliable and elastic.
wysyp: Spores colourless, elliptical, with a smooth surface.
podobne: Crepidotis variabilis is similar.
However, it can easily be distinguished by its unforked gills.
It has brown spores and grows in damper habitats.

owocnik: Irregularly spherical (flattened), wider than high, 2–5 cm in diameter.
On the surface of the fruit body there are a few depressions and pits.
A short stem up to 1.5 cm long, usually located in the soil, connects it to the substrate and mycelium.
Covering thin, dry and brittle, with small, dark scales surrounded by a lighter halo.
When ripe it splits at the top.
White rhizomorphs extend from the stem.
inne: In young specimens hard and white, then it darkens and becomes dark purple-olive or brown, finally turning into a powder containing an enormous quantity of spores.
podobne: Scleroderma verrucosum.
It is larger and has a longer stem and slightly different small scales.
Scleroderma bovista with somewhat different warts on the covering.
Reliable distinction between several similar species of earthballs (Scleroderma) is possible only by microscopic examination.

owocnik: Spherical or somewhat flattened, without a stem, 2–5 cm in diameter, exceptionally up to 8 cm.
It is hard, heavy, with a fairly thin and smooth peridium, cracked at the top in old age.
Colour sandy-brown-yellow, sometimes with an orange tinge.
The mature fruit body opens by splitting and does not tear into fragments.
The hymenial layer (gleba) is located inside the peridium.
It is white, dark brown with age.
The hyphae have clamp connections.
At the base the hyphae form a swollen mycelium.
podobne: Among the earthballs (Scleroderma) occurring in Poland, Scleroderma bovista is distinguished by the smooth surface of the fruit body.
The most reliable feature that makes it possible to distinguish it from other earthballs is, however, the sculpturing of the spores and the presence of clamp connections on the hyphae.

owocnik: Irregularly spherical or bulbous, without a stem, up to 10 cm in diameter and with a strong spicy smell.
It is hard, heavy and has a thick peridium.
Surface of the peridium straw-yellow, ochre-yellow or yellow-brown-ochre, covered with flat warts 1.5–4 mm high and furrowed with grooves that converge at the base of the fruit body.
Only the base of the fruit body is smooth.
A cord of mycelium grows from it.
The hymenial layer (gleba) is located inside the peridium.
Only in young fruit bodies is it white, soon becoming yellowish-greenish, finally black with a violet tinge, interspersed with thin, white fibres of the capillitium.
After ripening the fruit body splits, releasing the spores.
podobne: Scleroderma bovista has at the base of the fruit body a distinct, well-developed mycelial strand resembling a short root.

owocnik: Irregularly spherical, up to 5 cm in diameter.
It is connected to the substrate and mycelium by mycelial cords resembling roots.
Young specimens are whitish, then gradually darken, taking on a dirty yellowish, yellow-brown, finally chestnut-brown colour.
The covering of the fruit body (peridium) is fairly thin, covered with fine warts or small scales.
After ripening the outer covering splits irregularly.
Sometimes the fruit bodies are sunken into the ground even to half.
A characteristic feature is the presence of a short stem-like part in the lower part of the fruit body.
inne: In young specimens hard and white, then darkens, becomes umber-brown, and still later violet-black with whitish or pale greenish veins.
In the mature fruit body the gleba is violet-brown or violet-grey-brown.
podobne: Scleroderma citrinum.
It has a thicker covering, is larger and has no short stem-like part at the base of the fruit body;
Scleroderma areolatum.
It has a yellowish skin with a pinkish-violet tint.

owocnik: Annual, spread out or spread out and reflexed.
It adheres strongly to the substrate, covering large areas.
A single fruit body is at first circular in shape and reaches a diameter of 2–5 cm, but neighbouring fruit bodies often merge with one another.
The sterile margin is at first fluffy, cottony, up to 1.5 cm wide.
During drying it becomes leathery and stands away from the substrate.
Flesh of young fruit bodies spongy and flexible, of older ones fibrous and leathery.
It is 1–2 mm thick, yellow-rusty in colour, darkening when damaged.
Hymenophore at first smooth, then successively warty, radially folded, finally coarsely maze-like.
Colour at first cream, then yellow-rusty, finally dark brown.
Pores very fine, lilac in young fruit bodies, yellow-rusty after drying.
In the hymenium there are smooth-walled, spindle-shaped cystidia measuring 50–80 × 5.5–8 μm.
Young fruit bodies have a pleasant, mushroomy smell, older ones an unpleasant one.
No distinct taste.
podobne: Serpula lacrymans.
It occurs on structural timber in conditions of high humidity.
It forms larger and thicker fruit bodies.
Coniophora cerebella

owocnik: Diameter 10–50 cm, white when young, later straw-yellow, with fairly raised outer parts, thickly leaf-like and wavy to fan-shaped, often with coloured zones on the surfaces.
miazsz: White; without smell, with a mild taste.
podobne: Sparassis brevipes resembles Sparassis crispa in colour and size, but is paler and has more widely bent, more spread-out leaf-like branch ends.

owocnik: Height usually 5–20 cm, width 6–30 cm, but it can be larger, sometimes even reaching 6 kg (in 1711 in Turoszow two specimens were found by a forester, the larger of which weighed 20 kg and measured 2.55 metres).
Shape irregularly spherical, from a thick fleshy base it divides into lobed, variously fused branches with the hymenium on both sides.
The lobes are strongly folded, with teeth on the edges, so that in appearance it resembles a cauliflower.
In young specimens the fruit body is whitish, later yellowish, cream, ochre or yellow-brown.
The branches of the fruit body grow from a thick, blackish base of the stem, which often grows deep into the substrate.
miazsz: Waxy, elastic, white.
Smell pleasant, taste reminiscent of nuts.
wysyp: Spores 6–7 × 4–7 µm in diameter, short-ellipsoid, smooth, light yellow.
podobne: In Poland there also occurs a very similar Sparassis brevipes.
It has more faded, broader and more leaf-like ends of the branches.

owocnik: 1 to 3 mm in diameter, spherical and flexible, whitish to straw yellow in colour.
The gleba is contained in a smooth and sticky peridiole.
During the ejection of spores the outer membrane (exoperidium) suddenly opens into a star composed of 4 to 9 arms, which reveals the peridiole.

This is thrown out (hence the Polish name 'squirter') over a distance by the violent rupture and turning inside out of the inner layers, and thanks to its sticky layer it sticks to surrounding structures.
podobne: Nidularia deformis is distinguished by larger basidia, an epiphragm and numerous peridioles on the basidia.

owocnik: Annual, forming numerous clusters.
A single fruit body is 0.5–3 cm wide and 1–2 mm thick, in shape spread out, spread out and bent back, shelf-like, bracket-shaped and is wavy.
Fruit bodies growing in large numbers next to each other are arranged overlapping like roof tiles or fuse with one another.
They attach to the substrate by their upper surface, and its sides bend outwards.
Growing on vertical trunks it forms small caps bent back at the top.
The upper surface is hairy, velvety, rough or bristly.
It is whitish, ochre-yellow, grey-rusty-brown in colour and is concentrically zoned and striped.
The margin of the fruit body is sharp and wavy.
spod: Smooth, bright on young fruit bodies, later orange-yellow or ochre, on older fruit bodies fading and becoming pale orange-brown.
inne: Whitish (not changing colour when cut), hard, of leathery or corky consistency.
It is covered with a thin cortex, discernible even through a hand lens.
podobne: Stereum gausapatum growing on oak.
It has a distinctly spread-out or spread-out and bent-back fruit body, and a darker hymenophore – chocolate brown.
Stereum subtomentosum, with a fruit body attached sideways to the substrate and flesh turning yellow when cut.
Its hymenophore is never bright yellow or orange, but darker; ochre, coffee-coloured.
Stereum ochraceoflavum.
It occurs mainly on thinner branches, most often of oak, has smaller and thinner fruit bodies and a pale orange-yellow or brown-grey-ochre hymenophore.
Byssomerulius corium.
It also has a smooth hymenophore (but sometimes irregularly net-like or pore-pitted), and cream, pale yellowish or greyish fruit bodies.

owocnik: Perennial.
Young specimens are more or less round, spread out.
They adhere to the substrate entirely by their dorsal side, at most only their margins stand away slightly.
A single fruit body is 5–20 mm in diameter, but neighbouring fruit bodies merge with one another and form sheets reaching even several metres in length.
Older specimens, especially those growing on a vertical substrate, form protruding, elongated caps 1–2 cm wide.
They are narrowly, deeply grooved and zoned and hairless, only the margin is felted brownish.
The upper surface of these caps is at first whitish-hairy, later greyish-brown, and in old specimens dark brown-blackish.
Flesh leathery or corky-bast-like, woody in older fruit bodies.
The hymenial surface is uneven and wrinkled.
Its colour is yellowish, cream-yellowish to red-yellowish or grey-yellow, and in wet weather dark grey with spots.
Turns red when rubbed.
Older fruit bodies, which have 10–20 layers of hymenium, are 2–4 mm thick.
They are attached to the substrate at only a few points and can be easily detached.
podobne: On the wood of conifers grows the very similar and also common Stereum sanguinolentum.
Somewhat similar are: Amylostereum areolatum, Amylostereum chailletii, Xylobolus frustulatus, Aleurodiscus disciformis.

owocnik: At first thin, round or funnel-shaped and adhering to the substrate, then attached to the substrate only by the side or by a stem-like base, while the fan-shaped or spatula-shaped part of the fruit body is free and forms a thin, small cap.
It usually occurs in groups, and then the caps of neighbouring fruit bodies overlap like roof tiles or grow in rows.
A single cap reaches a width of 1–5 (exceptionally up to 10 cm) and a thickness of 0.5–1.2 mm.
Surface velvety or felty and concentrically zoned, with the zones often of different colours.
The zones are hairless, wood-brown in colour.
The upper surface is yellowish-grey, nut-brown or ochre, rarely chestnut-brown.
Older specimens change colour to grey.
In young fruit bodies the cap margin is silky-fibrous, but not felty.
On a cross-section under the cap skin a yellow-brown line about 0.1 mm thick is visible.
inne: Smooth, sometimes only slightly knobbly, often radially veined at the margins (especially on young fruit bodies).
Colour from pale beige through ochre to pale coffee.
Margin at first white, later dirty yellow, pale ochre, orange, dirty brown, and even grey.
Damaged spots turn yellow immediately and later turn brown.
podobne: Stereum hirsutum is similar.
A good way to distinguish these species is to observe their fruit bodies after damage – Stereum subtomentosum turns yellow, S. hirsutum does not change colour.

kapelusz: Diameter up to 15 cm, semicircular in young specimens, then convex to flattened in older ones.
Covered with characteristic woolly tufts arranged overlapping like roof tiles.
The fibrils are thick, protruding and grey-brown with a darker tip.
The cap surface is dry.
spod: Up to 14 mm long, attached or decurrent.
Colour from whitish in young to grey-brown (sometimes with a reddish tint) in older specimens.
Pores angular, relatively large, covered in young specimens with a white-grey covering.
Its remains sometimes stay on the margin of the cap.
Damaged tubes first turn red, then take on a black-violet colour.
trzon: Thickness 1–3 cm, height up to 15 cm.
Cylindrical, narrowing slightly towards the cap, very tough.
Colour similar to the cap, covered with numerous cottony, grey-brown hairs.
Under the cap there is a disappearing ring.
A damaged stem takes on a reddish colour.
miazsz: Fleshy, sometimes dry and springy, and woody in the stem.
White in young specimens, through reddish to dark brown in older ones.
When damaged it takes on a reddish colour.
Taste and smell faint.
wysyp: Spores spherical or ellipsoid, measuring 10–13 × 8–10 μm, with a surface sculpted in a net-like pattern.

kapelusz: Diameter 1.5–2.5 (exceptionally up to 3.5 cm), shape hemispherical to spread out, sometimes with a low umbo.
The cap margin is not inrolled.
Surface in colour from grey-ochre through red-brown to dark brown, smooth and matt.
Sometimes it may be wrinkled in places.
When wet the gills show through slightly at the cap margins.
If the fruit bodies develop under snow, they are white.
spod: Crowded, sinuately notched, coloured whitish to light ash-grey.
inne: Height 3–6 cm, thickness 1–2 mm, stiff, hard, tube-like, with remnants of mycelium at the base.
Surface shiny, brown-ochre, paler at the top.
miazsz: Thin, whitish, without smell.
Taste mild.
podobne: Several other species grow on cones:
Strobilurus stephanocystis.
Morphologically it is impossible to distinguish; in practice it is most easily distinguished by its place of occurrence (on pine cones).
In the hymenium it has broad cystidia with a crown of crystals at the top,
Strobilurus tenacellus.
The cap has a slightly banded surface because of the gills showing through.
This species develops on pine cones.
It is bitter,
Mycena strobilicola.
It also occurs in spring and also on spruce cones.
It differs in a distinct smell of chlorine and a white, brittle stem.
Baeospora myosura.
It has a light, flesh-beige cap and a white-dusted stem, the fruit bodies appear on pine cones, less often on spruce.

kapelusz: Diameter 3-8(10) cm, covered with a layer of blue-green or bluish-green slime, in which white small scales can be seen.
In drought the cap loses its slime, becomes glossy, smooth and of a faded colour.
The cap shape in the initial phase of growth is convex, and with time it changes to bell-shaped, flat.
Flesh fairly compact, the skin can be easily pulled off the cap.
spod: Crowded and attached to the stem.
In young fruit bodies covered by a veil.
Colour at first whitish, later violet-blue, finally chocolate-brown.
Gill edges white and dusted.
trzon: Reaches 8 cm in height and 1 cm in thickness.
Colour pale beige or pale green, changing with time to brown, hollow in the middle.
The ring is in the middle of the stem and disappears early.
Below this ring the stem is covered with white small hairs, or scales.
miazsz: At first greenish-white, later cream.
Taste and smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spores violet-brown, elliptical-egg-shaped, 7-9 × 4-5.5 µm in diameter.
Edge of the gills with hair-like cystidia.
podobne: Stropharia aeruginosa can be confused with Stropharia caerulea, which has a bluer cap and pinkish gills and is also less slimy.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–7 cm.
Conical-arched when young, later spread out with a distinct umbo.
The umbo is usually blunt, less often sharp.
Cap skin slippery, sky-blue or blue-green, and in older specimens in colour from sulphur yellow to cream.
The cap of Stropharia caerulea quickly loses its bluish colour.
spod: Attached and decurrent with a small tooth.
At first they are flesh-olive in colour, later purple-brown, and their edges are white, fibrous or toothed.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness 2–5 mm.
It is cylindrical and springy.
At first it is blue-greenish in colour, later it becomes lighter; straw-yellow at the base, sky-blue at the top.
Finally it becomes whitish and covered with small flakes or fibrous-scaly.
miazsz: Thin, fleshy.
At first it is blue-green, then green-grey and dirty white, and cream at the base of the stem.
Smell sour.
wysyp: Spores ellipsoid, smooth, thick-walled and without a germ pore.
podobne: Stropharia aeruginosa is the most similar.
It is, however, more greenish and there are no blue tints on the cap.
Its gills are violet with white edges, and it is also more slimy.

kapelusz: Diameter 2–4 cm, whitish, pale ochre or yellowish, sticky when wet.
Cap shape mostly semicircular.
spod: At first pale lilac, later purple-violet, with a paler edge.
trzon: Whitish, with a tightly adhering, narrow ring (or without).
podobne: Stropharia coronilla can be confused with dwarf Agaricus species, which, however, have free gills.

kapelusz: Diameter 6–15, even 20 cm, at first conically convex, then convex, finally spread out.
Margin sharp, inrolled for a long time.
Surface smooth, bare, matt, dark wine-brown, then paler and becoming ochre-brown, finally cream, but sometimes from the very beginning it is cream-yellow with wine-red fibrils.
It is dry and slippery, when wet only slightly sticky.
spod: Crowded, at first light grey, then grey-lilac to violet-black, with a paler edge.
trzon: Height 7–15 cm, thickness 1.5–3 cm, cylindrical, sometimes with a widened base, white, turning yellow with age.
Ring white, thick, sometimes its remnants remain on the cap margin and on the stem.
Surface covered with long fibrils, but without scales.
With rhizomorphs at the base.
podobne: Stropharia hornemannii, which has scales on the stem, and the ring (if it remains) does not split, and the whole fruit body is paler.
Probably poisonous.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–20 cm, at first hemispherical, then flat-arched or cushion-shaped.
Surface smooth, sometimes suede-like, dry, in colour from cream to brown-olive.
Skin strongly fused with the flesh.
It darkens when pressed.
spod: Long, notched with a sinus at the stem, olive.
Pores small, at first yellow, dark orange in older specimens, olive in very old ones.
They turn blue when cut.
trzon: Height 5–15 cm, barrel-shaped in young specimens, club-shaped or cylindrical in older ones.
Colour from yellow to orange-reddish, wine-red at the base.
A characteristic feature is the presence on the stem of a distinct, darker (rusty-reddish) reticulum with elongated meshes.
miazsz: Firm, yellow in the cap, reddish in the lower part of the stem.
When cut it turns strongly blue.
Mild in taste, smell weak.
podobne: Sutorius luridiformis also turns blue, but the stem has no reticulum (net), only small carmine-red scales.
Some colour varieties may be similar to Suillus variegatus, but its flesh does not turn blue, the stem does not have a reticulum, and the pores are brown in colour.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–12 cm, at first hemispherical with a slightly wavy margin, later flat, becoming bent in older fruit bodies.
The cap skin is covered when young with a delicate, light, felty bloom, later slimy (especially when wet) and shiny, smooth, very difficult to peel.
Cap colour cream, cream-ochre, orange-ochre, orange-brown, mostly with a paler border at the margin.
spod: Mature ones 4–10 mm long.
Adnate to the stem, and even decurrent on it; grey-yellowish in young fruit bodies, later yellow, grey-ochre, finally brownish.
They separate from the cap flesh with difficulty.
Pores of the tubes very large and resembling the holes of a sieve in appearance.
Hence the species name.
When pressed they turn brown.
trzon: Height 2–10 cm and width 0.8–2 cm.
Cylindrical, solid, fibrous, without a ring.
The colour of the cap or slightly paler, sometimes red-brown at the base.
Mycelium at the base of the stem in colour from whitish to violet-pink.
miazsz: Flexible, rubbery, cream, ochre-orange to brownish in colour, sometimes pink or reddish in the stem; when cut it does not change colour, but usually becomes pink-reddish after drying.
Smell delicate, pleasant, slightly fruity.
Taste slightly sourish.
wysyp: Spores measuring 6.5–11 × 3–4 µm, spindle-shaped to ellipsoid, with a smooth surface.
podobne: Suillus variegatus.
However, it has smaller pores, and the upper part of its stem is dotted with spots
Suillus flavidus.
It is very rare.
It has a ring on the stem, and thick, embedded fibrils on the cap
Gyrodon lividus.
Its thin tubes run far down the stem and are strongly fused with the cap flesh

kapelusz: 4–12 cm in diameter, at first semicircular or conical, with age flat with a small umbo in the centre.
At first it has an inrolled margin, later sharp.
It is entirely covered with fine, darker fibrils and is felty-scaly.
Colour from yellow-brown through red-brown to brown.
spod: Short, slightly decurrent on the stem.
Pores very large, radially elongated, yellow to yellow-olive in colour.
They do not change colour.
When young they are covered with a whitish veil.
trzon: Height 4–10 cm, thickness 1–2 cm, cylindrical, thickened at the bottom, hollow.
Colour the same as the cap or paler.
With a whitish ring in the upper part.
miazsz: In the cap yellowish, spongy, in the stem white, drier and more compact.
It does not change colour after damage.
Smell pleasant, taste somewhat sour, in older specimens astringent, slightly bitter.

kapelusz: At first brown or rusty-red, bare and slimy, in mature specimens yellow-ochre and dry.
Skin smooth, bare and easily separating from the flesh.
Arched with a sharp margin when young, cushion-shaped when mature, 4–10 cm in diameter.
spod: At first pale yellow, later ochre, finally brown-yellow, adnate to the stem.
Pores pale yellow, small when young, larger when mature.
They exude white droplets of milky liquid, which, when dried, leave brown grains on the pores and the top of the stem.
trzon: Height 4–8 cm, diameter 1–2 cm, cylindrical, solid, without a ring.
Surface pale yellow, brownish at the base in mature fruit bodies, with brown granules at the top.
These are dried droplets of milky fluid.
miazsz: White-yellowish, brownish only at the stem base.
Taste mild, smell pleasant.
podobne: Suillus luteus.
It has larger fruit bodies, a ring on the stem and a yellow-orange cap.
Grows under pines.
Suillus collinitus also grows under two-needle pines, but only on limestone and has a pinkish mycelium at the base of the stem.
It is rare.

kapelusz: Conical in young fruit bodies, flattened and cushion-shaped in mature ones, 40–150 mm in diameter.
Cap skin smooth, bare, covered with slime, which dries in drought, and in wet weather is very slippery and shiny.
Colour golden yellow, golden orange, paler at the margin.
The skin is very hard to separate from the flesh; it can only be partly peeled from the margin of the cap in older fruit bodies, but in young specimens this is almost impossible.
spod: In young specimens they are covered by a yellow-white veil.
Length 5–10 mm.
They are yellow, later olive-yellow, adnate.
Pores at first round, later angular, yellow when young, brown-yellow with age, turning pink-brown when pressed and then darkening.
trzon: Height 5–14 cm and diameter up to 2.5 cm, cylindrical or club-shaped, solid, with a ring at the top.
Above the ring a lemon-yellow slimy ring zone, often with a reticulum, and below the ring the stem is orange-brown.
In older specimens the ring disappears, but a trace of it is clearly visible.
miazsz: Yellow, sometimes turning pink in places, soft and juicy in the cap, hard and fibrous in the stem.
Taste slight, smell indistinct.
In older specimens the flesh becomes watery.
When cut or crushed it turns dirty pink.
wysyp: Spores measuring 7-11× 3-4 µm, spindle-shaped to ellipsoid, smooth, pale yellow.
podobne: The most similar is Suillus bresadolae var. flavogriseus Cazzoli & Consiglio, growing only in the higher parts of the mountains, also under larches.
Also similar are Suillus flavidus and Suillus granulatus (the latter, however, has no ring on the stem).

kapelusz: Diameter 4–12 cm, dark brown, chocolate brown, sometimes yellow-brown.
In young fungi hemispherical, then flattened, broad.
Skin radially veined, sticky and shiny, dried out during drought.
It can be easily separated from the flesh.
spod: Length 6–12 mm, lemon-yellow tubes, in young fruit bodies covered with a white, membranous partial veil.
In adult individuals the remains of this veil stay on the stem in the form of a white-violet, adhering ring.
Pores of the tubes at first roundish, on older specimens angular.
trzon: Height 3–11 cm, thickness 1–2.5 cm, cylindrical, hard and solid.
It is pale yellow, with brown granules on the upper part.
A very characteristic feature is the presence of a skin-like ring on the stem.
By this it can be distinguished from the very similar Suillus granulatus, which does not have this ring.
miazsz: At first hard, then soft.
It is white-yellowish in colour and only at the bottom of the stem is it slightly brown.
Taste and smell pleasant.
podobne: Suillus collinitus; it also grows under pines, but has a paler cap and has no ring.
Suillus granulatus; it has no ring.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–14 cm, in young specimens semicircular with inrolled margins, then cushion-shaped with a sharp margin.
The skin when young is in colour from yellow or yellow-grey through olive to dirty orange and is felty, then becomes ochre-brown to pale orange.
Its surface is covered with fine fibrils, which sometimes disappear in older specimens.
It separates from the flesh rather with difficulty.
spod: Fairly short, yellow or pale orange when young, then dark olive.
When pressed they first turn blue, then brown.
Pores roundish and of similar colour to the tubes.
trzon: Height 4–10 cm, thickness 2–4 cm.
It is cylindrical, smooth and thickened at the bottom.
It has a yellow or yellow-brownish colour with a slight reddish tinge.
miazsz: Hard, pale yellow or pale orange, lemon-yellow beneath the surface of the stem.
When cut, in places it turns slightly blue (slightly bluish).
Taste insignificant, smell distinctive, somewhat reminiscent of conifer needles.
podobne: Suillus bovinus, but it has larger pores and does not have the characteristic smell
Chalciporus piperatus, but it is much smaller and has a peppery taste.
The so-called Boletinus cavipes.
It occurs more often in the mountains and is easier to distinguish by its hollow stem and disappearing ring; moreover it is densely covered with small tufts.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–12 cm, at first convex with an inrolled margin, later cushion-shaped, finally spread flat.
Skin easily peeling, slimy, surface colour from grey-white through yellow-grey, olive-grey to red-grey.
In dry weather the surface cracks into fibrous small scales.
In young fruit bodies the margin is joined to the stem by a white-grey partial veil.
spod: Long, attached, often decurrent, grey-white in young fruit bodies, dark grey in older ones.
Pores large, angular, radially elongated, whitish in young fruit bodies, dark blue in older ones, finally cinnamon-brownish.
trzon: Height 4–10 cm, thickness up to 2.5 cm, cylindrical, fleshy, solid, club-like thickened at the base.
Surface yellow-grey in colour, paler than the cap, reticulate above the ring, pitted below.
Ring thin, quickly disappearing.
miazsz: Compact, later soft, whitish, greyish, yellowish in the stem.
Faint smell, taste mild, fruity.
podobne: Under larch there also grow Suillus grevillei and Suillus tridenticus, but they differ in appearance.
The characteristic colour of the pores distinguishes the grey Suillus from all other Suillus species.

kapelusz: It grows to a large size – diameter up to 30 cm.
In young specimens the margin is rolled under, the skin matt and suede-like, in older ones it becomes smooth.
Colour from olive to dark brown, sometimes also rusty brown.
It often has an irregular shape.
spod: Crowded and distinctly decurrent on the stem (especially in young specimens).
Their colour is at first white, with age ochre-yellow.
They are often connected by transverse anastomoses.
In damaged places they turn brown.
trzon: Thickness about 2–4 cm, height about 3–7 cm.
It is solid, hard, springy and covered with a dark brown or black, velvety down.
It is usually eccentric.
miazsz: Colour white or white-yellow, juicy, brittle.
Taste slightly bitterish, no smell.
wysyp: Spores broadly ellipsoid, with a smooth surface and almost colourless.

kapelusz: Diameter from 1–12 cm, but usually not exceeding 8 cm, shell-shaped or spatula-shaped, sometimes cup-shaped.
Fruit bodies attached sideways to the substrate or, less often, lateral on a short stalk.
The skin of the cap is dry, velvety to suede-like, with age becoming almost smooth, with only the margin felty.
Margin inrolled, increasingly wavy with age.
spod: Gills crowded, with numerous connections resembling anastomoses, forked, usually wavy, decurrent.
Ochre-yellow to yellow in colour, fading with age, easily detached from the cap.
trzon: Most often stem absent.
Less often rudimentary lateral and short, the colour of the cap, with gills running down onto it.
miazsz: White or cream in colour and sometimes dirty yellow, soft and thin.
It does not change colour after damage.
Mild in taste, smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spore print colour yellowish, light brown or ochre-brown.
Spores with a smooth surface, broadly elliptical, measuring 4–6×3–4 µm, dextrinoid.
Mature spores usually with a single droplet.
podobne: Similar fruit bodies are produced by Phyllotopsis nidulans – with a more saturated, orange, bristly cap surface and a cream spore print.

owocnik: Funnel-shaped, up to 5 cm in diameter and up to 4 cm high.
The upper part of the cap is often irregularly ragged and resembles a flower.
Cap surface brown or chocolate in colour, only the margin whitish.
It is more or less zoned, sometimes covered with small scales or delicately hairy.
It fades after drying.
It has a short, fairly thick and centrally attached stem.
Hymenium smooth, decurrent on the stem, brown or violet-brown, paler at the margins.
Flesh thin, brown, without smell.
podobne: Thelephora terrestris forms a fruit body of similar colour and also funnel-shaped, but it does not have such ragged margins and is often a tiered fruit body made up of several funnels.
Sometimes Thelephora palmata is similar, but it is easy to distinguish by smell.
A similar, brownish, but flat, spread-out fruit body is formed by Tomentella ferruginea, growing on wood.

owocnik: Bushy-branched, up to 10 cm tall, without a distinct main stem.
Branches dense, with flattened tips with small teeth.
Surface smooth, dark brownish, chocolate-brown or rusty-brown, often with a violet tinge.
In youth the ends of the segments have whitish tips.
miazsz: Black-brown, very firm and tough-fibrous, with an unpleasant smell of garlic or rotten cabbage.
Sometimes, however, there is no smell.
After drying it becomes brittle.
podobne: Thelephora anthocephala is the most similar.
It has similar bushy fruit bodies, but smaller, sometimes resembling a flower crown.
They give off no smell.
It occurs in deciduous forests.

owocnik: Short-lived, fan-shaped, resembling a rosette, formed low on the forest floor.
It is 4 to 15 cm wide, and the individual spines reach a length of 2 to 7 cm.
Colour violet-brown at the base and white or cream towards the branched and pointed tips.
Older fruit bodies turn brown from the centre.
Smell earthy, but faint, taste mild, not characteristic.
Perennial, of very varied shapes.
They may be goblet-shaped, funnel-shaped, circular, semicircular, fan-shaped, kidney-shaped, or shelf-like.
They are attached to the substrate sideways or by means of a short stem.
Sometimes they occur singly, but more often in groups.
They may grow in overlapping tiers or in rows, and then sometimes fuse together.
A single fruit body is 3-5, exceptionally up to 10 cm wide and 2–3 mm thick.
The margin is usually sharp, fringed, and ragged in older specimens.
The upper surface is rough, uneven, wavy-rough or hairy, and zoned both concentrically and radially.
Its colour ranges from cinnamon to chocolate-brown, the margin is paler; at first white, with age becoming white-beige.
spod: Smooth, slightly warty or radially wavy and wrinkled.
miazsz: Chocolate-brown, elastic and soft in young fruit bodies, fibrous and leathery in older ones.
Earthy in taste, smell faint, sourish.
podobne: Thelephora caryophyllea is the most similar, and to a lesser extent other, rarer species of Thelephora: Thelephora penicillata, Thelephora palmata and Thelephora anthocephala.

owocnik: Annual.
A single fruit body is bracket-shaped or hemispherical, 2–8 cm wide, 0.3–1.5 cm thick, attached to the substrate sideways or centrally.
Fruit bodies usually occur in groups, overlapping like roof tiles, or are fused sideways or at the base.
The surface is uneven, felty-hairy, concentrically zoned and striped, as a result of which it resembles some species of bracket fungi.
The upper surface of the fruit body is dirty white, straw yellow, grey, fawn.
Sometimes algae grow on it and then it is green.
Margin of the fruit body in the same colour or ochre-brown, thin and even.
spod: Gilled.
The gills radiate from the base, are mostly smooth, sometimes ragged.
In one fruit body there are 12–15 of them per 1 cm, exceptionally up to 17 (counting at the margin of the fruit body).
At the base they are connected by anastomoses.
Gill colour from white through light grey to light nut-brown.
miazsz: It is up to 1 cm thick, leathery, white or light brown.
Taste and smell indistinct.
wysyp: Spores colourless, cylindrical with a pointed base and curved in the shape of a comma.
In the hymenium there are a few thick-walled cystidia of straw-yellow colour and fusiform shape.
podobne: It can be confused with other tree-dwelling fungus species, because it is very variable morphologically and very variously coloured.

Its upper surface resembles bracket fungi (especially Trametes versicolor and Trametes hirsuta), but it can easily be told apart from them, because bracket fungi have no gills in the hymenophore, but tubes with small pores.

owocnik: Up to 10 cm wide, semicircular or fan-shaped and attached sideways to the substrate.
Margin thin and sharp.
The upper surface is usually uneven, wrinkled.
Colour cinnabar, reddish or brick-red, fading in older individuals.
spod: In the form of tubes with pores cinnabar-coloured or reddish.
Pores round or angular.
miazsz: Up to 2 cm thick, cinnabar-coloured, flexible, fibrous and without smell.
podobne: Because of its distinctive vermilion colour and lack of zoning it is easy to distinguish from other species.
It may possibly be confused with Pycnoporellus fulgens, which has fruit bodies of similar colour (orange or brick-red), but occurs mainly on conifers.

owocnik: Annual, but fairly durable, so that they can be found throughout the year.
Sometimes they overwinter.
Young specimens have the shape of a shapeless bulb, after maturing they become bracket-shaped, semicircular or shell-shaped.
They are attached sideways to the tree and reach a width of 8-10, exceptionally up to 20 cm, and a thickness of 1-4, exceptionally up to 8 cm.
They differ from other bracket fungi in the humped thickening at the point of attachment.
The upper surface of the fruit body has very varied colours: white, white-ochre, yellowish, white-hazel, grey, rusty-cinnamon, olive-celadon, bluish, and it has concentric ridges of the same colour.

The margin of the fruit body is even, blunt, becoming wavy with time, sometimes brown-red. The fruit body is often overgrown with algae, taking on a green colour, and usually only the margins are white.
Only in young fruit bodies is the upper surface velvety; later it becomes smooth and bare.
spod: Tubular.
The tubes are 1–5 mm long and the pores are white.
A characteristic feature of this species is that these pores never have a round shape, but are always elongated, pit-like.
Sometimes near the umbo they take the form of gills.
miazsz: White, corky-fibrous in young fruit bodies, woody and hard in older ones.
Smell weak, taste indistinct.
wysyp: Spores colourless, smooth, cylindrical, non-amyloid, measuring 4–5.5 × 2–2.5 μm.
podobne: Young fruit bodies with a velvety surface can be confused with the hairy fruit bodies of Trametes pubescens or Trametes hirsuta.
Older fruit bodies are easy to tell apart, because in Trametes gibbosa they have a smooth upper surface.
Trametes versicolor has a more zoned, multicoloured and bare fruit body.
The most characteristic feature, however, allowing Trametes gibbosa to be distinguished infallibly from other bracket fungi, is the pit-like pores.
Daedaleopsis confragosa has similar, radiating, pitted pores, but its fruit body is distinctly brown.
Lenzites betulina also has a very similar upper side of the fruit body, but it has gills on the underside.

owocnik: It reaches a width of up to 10 cm and a thickness of up to 1 cm.
It is flat, attached to the tree sideways and has a semicircular, fan-shaped or shell-shaped form.
The upper surface is in colour from whitish through grey-yellowish and rusty to nut-brown and has a characteristic concentric grooving.
It is covered with tufts giving it a shaggy or felty appearance.
The margin is usually darker (brownish) and wavy or crenate.
The fruit body is often overgrown with algae, as a result of which it becomes green.
Bluish or grey-black tinges never occur.
Fruit bodies often occur in groups in rows.
They are very variable morphologically and in different environmental conditions this fungus forms many forms differing considerably in the morphology of the fruit bodies.
spod: Tubular, white on young specimens, then cream, finally greyish or rusty.
The tubes form only a single layer.
They are 1–3 (exceptionally up to 5) mm long, pores round or polygonal, white, cream on older fruit bodies, 0.2–0.4 mm in diameter.
miazsz: Whitish, elastic, 2–6 mm thick.
It has a slight smell of aniseed.
wysyp: Spores smooth, cylindrical, with a pointed base and straight or bent ends, non-amyloid.
podobne: Lenzites betulina, often completely identical, indistinguishable from the upper side of the fruit body, but differs fundamentally on the underside, since it has gills rather than tubes,
Trametes pubescens, which also has fibrils on the cap.
However, it is almost uniformly white and has no concentric grooving.
It is also much rarer,
Trametes ochracea has more clearly zoned, more colourful fruit bodies with a triangular cross-section.

owocnik: Width 3–10 cm, thickness 0.5–1 cm.
It is attached to the tree sideways or centrally.
With lateral attachment it is bracket-shaped, with central attachment plate-shaped or rosette-shaped.
Cap margin sharp, thin and wavy.
At the point of attachment the cap is distinctly thicker and usually has a knob here.
Surface delicately velvety, felty, dull, without gloss, in colour from ochre-brown through light red-brown to chestnut or grey-coffee.
The cap is distinctly concentrically zoned, but less contrastingly than in Trametes versicolor.
spod: Tubular.
Tubes 1–4 mm long, pores roundish and angular, flattened in older fruit bodies.
They are 2.5–3.3 mm in diameter, in colour from white to cream.
The tubes form only a single layer, and their edge is toothed or serrated.
miazsz: White, elastic with a slightly sourish smell.
wysyp: Spores colourless, non-amyloid, cylindrical and bent into a comma shape.
podobne: The most similar and sometimes difficult to distinguish is Trametes versicolor.
It is more colourful and often has zones with a blue-black colouring, which do not occur in Trametes ochracea.
In addition, Trametes ochracea is thicker where it is attached to the tree (here it has a triangular cross-section) and usually has a small knob at that spot.

inne: Width 3–8 cm, thickness 2–5 mm.
It is attached to the tree sideways or centrally.
With lateral attachment it is bracket-shaped, with central attachment plate-shaped or rosette-shaped.
Young individuals are almost uniformly light brown and felty, and at this stage of development are difficult to distinguish from other species of Trametes-like polypores.
Older ones become bare, silky shiny and, which is a characteristic feature of this species, they have distinct concentric zones of various shades from brown through dark blue to black.
Margin of the fruit body sharp and thin, surface uneven, radially folded and furrowed, shortly hairy or rough, silkily shiny.
Algae often develop on older fruit bodies, so that they turn more or less greenish.
White and very thin (2–5 mm), flexible and aromatic.
spod: Polyporoid.
Tubes 0.5–2 mm long.
They form only one layer, their edges are toothed or serrated.
They are cream in colour, light brown in older specimens.
Pores round, with time angular, and in older fruit bodies irregular, 0.15–0.4 mm in diameter.
podobne: Trametes ochracea can sometimes be difficult to distinguish.
Its fruit body is thicker, less variegated, matt (usually chestnut or grey-cocoa) and has a small umbo at the base.
In the upper surface of the fruit body it is also similar to Stereum hirsutum, but that one has a smooth hymenophore.

owocnik: Annual.
Width from a few to over ten cm.
Thin, of variable shape.
It is usually spread out and bent back, but sometimes shelf-like, hemispherical or fully spread out.
Margin thin and sharp.
It is attached to the substrate by the upper surface, which is uneven, felty and in colour from whitish through white-grey, greyish to grey-yellowish.
spod: Tubular.
Pores beautifully violet when young, especially near the margin, sometimes extending far down onto the wood.
miazsz: Thin, two-layered, elastic, leathery-waxy.
podobne: Trichaptum fuscoviolaceum, also occurring on the wood of conifers, but differs in its gill-like toothed hymenophore.
Trichaptum biforme, lilac or greyish in colour, also grows attached sideways, but grows only on broadleaved trees.
Veluticeps abietina.
It has a similar colour and also grows on conifers, but is distinguished by its hymenophore.

owocnik: Sessile (without a stem), up to 6 cm in diameter and up to 3 mm thick, more or less semicircular, irregularly hoof-shaped or kidney-shaped, sometimes spread out and bent back.
Surface hairy, finely hairy or fairly smooth, with zones whitish to greyish-white in colour.
Margin pale lilac in places.
Fruit bodies usually in large and dense, overlapping clusters.
Hymenophore tubular.
Pores 3–5 per mm, coloured from violet to lilac, most strongly coloured at the margin, fading with age to fawn or brownish, becoming teeth or spines as they mature.
They do not turn blue when touched.
Flesh whitish, hard and leathery, negative to pale yellow in reaction with KOH.
podobne: Trichaptum fuscoviolaceum, occurring on the wood of conifers, also differs in its gill-like toothed hymenophore.
Trichaptum biforme, forming very small, light yellow, yellow-brown, rarely purplish fruit bodies with a tubular hymenophore, also attached sideways, but growing only on conifers.
Veluticeps abietina.
It has a similar colour, but grows on conifers; it also differs in its hymenophore.

owocnik: Annual and usually occurring in groups.
A single fruit body is 1.5–6 cm wide, 1–4 mm thick, semicircular, fan-shaped, spread out or spread out and reflexed.
Margin sharp and thin, inrolled in older specimens.
It has no stem, attaching to the substrate by its side or base.
Fruit bodies growing in large numbers next to one another fuse at their bases, sometimes covering a large area.
In young specimens the surface is strongly felty-hairy, woolly, or at least velvety, in older ones bare.
Colour white, white-grey, green-grey, concentrically zoned and furrowed.
Cap margin at first purple, later yellow-brown.
spod: Tubular-reticulate-gilled.
It has the form of a reticulate structure at the margin passing into radiating gills.
The openings of the hymenophore are spatula-shaped and toothed.
At first cream-violet or violet, later grey-yellow-brown.
It is covered with a grey-violet bloom.
miazsz: It forms two layers, the upper one felty, white, the lower one skin-like, yellow-brown.
In young fruit bodies it is elastic, in older ones gradually hardening, finally stiff.
podobne: Trichaptum abietinum, forming light yellow, yellow-brown, rarely violet-ish and very small fruit bodies with a tubular hymenophore.
It is encountered much more rarely than the toothed Trichaptum species,
Trichaptum biforme, growing only on deciduous trees.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–10 cm, at first bell-shaped convex and inrolled at the margin, later spread, with embedded radial fibrils, chestnut brown to rusty brown, granular at the top.
Skin moist, sticky and greasy.
spod: Crowded, sinuately notched at the stem, white when young, generally rusty-spotted in old age.
Turning red-brown when pressed.
trzon: Length 5–7 cm and thickness 1–2 cm, cylindrical.
Stem light brown, under the cap a paler annular zone, but weakly marked.
miazsz: White, slowly turning red when crushed, smells of flour and has a mild taste at first and a bitter taste after maturing.
wysyp: Spores spherical-egg-shaped, smooth, colourless, 4–5(6) × 3–4 µm in diameter, without a germ pore.
podobne: There are several similar species of brown knight fungi with white gills.
When identifying them, pay attention to the stem: whether it has a ring and whether a distinctly contrasting white zone is visible at its top (under the cap).
Similar, for example, are Tricholoma pessundatum and Tricholoma populinum.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–9 cm, at first bell-shaped or broadly conical with a narrowly inrolled margin, later arched or spread out, often wavy.
In the centre it usually has a broad umbo.
The skin has this colour and is densely covered with fibrous scales, which on young fruit bodies are grey-black, on older ones brown-black.
The centre of the cap is darkest, the margins are often whitish.
spod: Fairly crowded, in colour from white to greyish.
Sometimes there are black tufts on their edges.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness up to 2 cm, cylindrical, solid.
Surface in colour from whitish to blackish-scaly, smooth or fibrous.
miazsz: Brittle, fleshy, whitish.
Taste slightly mealy, smell spicy.
podobne: There are several species of grey colouring:
Tricholoma virgatum, which, however, always has a sharp umbo on the cap and its surface is not so scaly but radially fibrous, and it has an acrid taste,
Tricholoma terreum, but this one in turn has a cap that is more hairy than scaly and is paler and greyer,
Tricholoma orirubens, in which the gills of adult fruit bodies are coloured pinkish,
Tricholoma portentosum has a yellowish stem and gills, mild, nutty taste.

kapelusz: It is thick-fleshed and 5–14 cm in diameter.
Shape at first hemispherical, later low-arched or flat, without an umbo, with an inrolled margin.
Surface with radially fused fibrils coloured from red to chestnut-brown, even blackish-brown in the centre.
When wet it is sticky.
spod: Crowded and broad, notched at the stem, at first creamy white, later with an ochre tint, and often with rusty spots on the edges.
trzon: Height from 5 to 10 cm, diameter 1–3 cm, shape cylindrical, widened at the bottom, and wedge-shaped narrowed at the base.
It is solid and does not change colour.
Surface brown-orange or red-brown and fibrous, white and smooth only right under the cap.
In young fruit bodies, at the boundary of the white zone under the cap and the rest of the stem, there is a slimy small ring, later disappearing.
miazsz: Thick, fleshy and hard.
In the cap it is whitish, in the stem base ochre.
It has a mealy smell and taste, but after some time bitter.
podobne: There are many similar brown knight fungi, including:
Tricholoma fulvum with yellowish gills,
Tricholoma ustale, with a smooth and shiny cap and rusty gills,
Tricholoma imbricatum, which has a delicately scaly cap, white flesh and cream gills,
Tricholoma psammopus, which has no smell and grows only under larch.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–5 cm, at first convex, then flat-convex, with a low umbo.
Surface dry, dull, white to greyish, covered with delicate fibrils in colour from grey-brown to olive.
Margin inrolled when young, often irregularly wavy.
spod: 2–4 mm wide, with short gills (l = 1–3), free, distinctly whitish to cream.
trzon: Height 3–5 cm, width 1–1.5 cm, cylindrical, with a fibrillose to scaly surface.
Its characteristic feature is the annular zone; above it it is white, below brown.
miazsz: Fleshy, white to cream.

kapelusz: Diameter from 5 to 10 cm, conical when young, later flat, with a broad blunt umbo, margin at first rolled under, later sharp, wavy and finally bent back.
Skin silky-shiny, radially fibrous, sticky in damp conditions, whitish, often with ochre, greenish or reddish spots.
spod: At first narrow and crowded, later up to 10 mm wide, with irregularly toothed edges, whitish to whitish-cream.
trzon: Height from 5 to 10 cm, diameter up to 3 cm, cylindrical, narrowed at the base, whitish, often with blue-green spots at the bottom.
miazsz: Juicy, compact, whitish.
Smell indistinctly earthy-mealy.
Taste slightly mealy.
podobne: There are several white Tricholoma species, but this one is easy to tell apart if certain characteristic features of structure and habitat are taken into account.
The inedible Tricholoma album has no distinct coloured spots on the cap, the flesh is slightly burning and when drying it gives off a repulsive smell of natural gas.
The poisonous Tricholoma inamoenum has a repulsive smell of coal gas and grows in coniferous forests.
The deadly poisonous white species of Amanita, such as Amanita verna and Amanita virosa, have a volva and a ring on the stem.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–10 cm, yellow-green or yellow-brown, darker in the middle, smooth, conically convex in the young fruit body, later flat, often variously bent.
Skin bare or finely scaly, greasy and therefore often with grains of sand, slippery in wet conditions.
spod: From pale yellowish to sulphur yellow, moderately crowded, thin, notched with a tooth, but broadly adnate at the base.
trzon: It reaches a length of 3 to 9 cm and a thickness of up to 3 cm.
It is cylindrical, solid.
Surface at first with longitudinal fibres, later smooth, yellow or yellowish-green.
miazsz: Hard, brittle, white, does not change colour when cut.
Taste sweetish-nutty, it smells like freshly ground flour.
podobne: Tricholoma frondosae,
the poisonous Tricholoma sulphureum, which has yellow flesh, distant gills and an unpleasant smell,
Tricholoma sejunctum, which has a more olive-grey cap and occurs mainly in broadleaved forests,
The deadly poisonous Amanita phalloides; young specimens in particular are similar.
The Amanita differs in having a volva at the base of the stem, a tall stem and free gills.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–8.5 cm, at first broadly conical to convex, later flattened, often with a broad umbo.
On the surface concentrically arranged, clearly visible scales, especially in the centre.
Scales yellow-brown, brownish-olive on a greenish-yellow, pale yellow or light yellow background.
spod: Reaching the cap margin, greenish-yellow to sulphur yellow.
trzon: Height 6–8.5 cm, thickness 1–1.5 cm, cylindrical.
Surface smooth, slightly shiny, straw yellow to sulphur yellow.
miazsz: White with a mild taste and a mealy smell.
podobne: Tricholoma frondosae is closely related to Tricholoma equestre and is morphologically similar to it.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–8 cm, at first hemispherical to conically convex, later flat, with a blunt broad umbo, sometimes shallowly concave in the centre, sticky in wet conditions, shiny in dry spells, with fine, embedded, radial fibres, smooth, red-brown, brown, yellow-brown, with a darker centre
spod: Width from 6 to 10 mm, moderately crowded, pale yellow to brownish yellow, with red-brown spots on the smooth edge.
trzon: Height from 5 to 11 cm, diameter from 1 to 1.8 cm, cylindrical, young – solid, later tubular, with longitudinal brown fibrils on a yellowish background, paler in the upper part, turning yellow when scraped.
miazsz: Compact, fairly thick in the centre of the cap, white to yellowish.
Smell slightly mealy, taste mealy and slightly bitter.
wysyp: Spores smooth, elliptical, non-amyloid, measuring 5-7.5 × 6-4 µm.
podobne: There are many similar brown knight fungi, including:
Tricholoma batschii with cream-white gills and a stem wedge-shaped and narrowed at the base,
Tricholoma ustale, with a smooth and shiny cap and rusty gills
Tricholoma imbricatum, which has a delicately scaly cap, white flesh, cream gills and grows in coniferous forests,
Tricholoma psammopus, which has no smell and grows only under larch.
A yellow tinge of the gills is characteristic of Tricholoma fulvum, but on older fruit bodies it is often visible only on a longitudinal section.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–8(10) cm, young almost bell-shaped, with an inrolled margin, later slightly flattened to completely flat, at first smooth-fibrous, then scaly over the whole surface except the top, red-brown to brown, rarely also with an olive-yellow background.
Skin dry, cracking into tiny small scales.
spod: Crowded, rounded at the stem or notched with a small tooth, at first dirty white, later spotted reddish-brownish.
When damaged they turn brown.
trzon: Length 6–15 cm and thickness 1–1.5 cm, cylindrical, at first solid, later hollow.
White at the top, otherwise pale brown with fine tufts.
Base of the stem narrowed or rooting.
Annular zone invisible.
miazsz: White, rusty-brownish at the base of the stem.
It is without smell, or has a weak mushroomy-herbal smell.
Taste mild or slightly bitter.
podobne: Many similar species of knights (Tricholoma) grow in Poland.
Morphological features important in identifying them include: the texture of the cap surface, its stickiness, the taste and smell of the flesh, and the trees under which they grow.
Tricholoma imbricatum can be confused with the poisonous Tricholoma albobrunneum.
Also similar are the inedible Tricholoma fulvum, Tricholoma vaccinum and Tricholoma psammopus.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–10 cm, at first arched or hemispherical with a small umbo, later spread out.
Young fruit bodies have an inrolled margin, older ones straightened and wavy.
The skin is whitish or cream in colour, but is densely covered with grey-black scales arranged radially.
In dry weather it becomes more silvery-grey with lighter margins.
spod: They are whitish-grey in colour, and after being detached from the fruit body they turn red after some time.
trzon: Height 4–10 cm, thickness up to 2 cm, cylindrical, solid and hard, with a pointed base, sometimes bulbous.
Colour white, surface longitudinally covered with darker fibrils.
Turns red after damage.
miazsz: Thin, whitish-grey, turning red after some time.
Taste mealy, smell aromatic.
podobne: Similar is the very rarely found Tricholoma atrosquamosum, which however has a more scaly cap, and Tricholoma terreum, but that one in turn has a cap that is more hairy than scaly.
The reddening knight differs from all other knights in that its damaged flesh, gills and stem turn red after a longer time.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–10 cm, fairly fleshy at the top, bell-shaped convex in a young fruit body, later flattened.
Skin whitish, dry, with regularly, concentrically arranged scales, small to large.
These scales are grey-brown or blackish-grey.
spod: At first white, often with a greenish tinge, then pale yellowish, never grey, moderately crowded, notched with a tooth.
When young, exuding water-clear droplets on the edge.
trzon: Height 6–12 cm, thickness 2–4 cm, cylindrical or swollen, often with a thickened base.
Surface white, ochre only in the lower half, at the top it often exudes clear drops of liquid.
miazsz: White, not changing colour when cut.
Taste slight, smell pleasant, but not very distinct.
wysyp: Spores relatively large, 8–10 × 6–7 µm, egg-shaped, smooth, colourless.
podobne: Most similar, indeed deceptively so, is Tricholoma scalpturatum.
It is distinguished by the yellowing of various parts of the fruit body with age, and after damage (but this takes several hours).
Also similar are:
Tricholoma atrosquamosum.
It has a similarly scaly cap, but a peppery, fruity or geranium smell.
Tricholoma orirubens.
Its cap and flesh slowly turn reddish after damage,
Tricholoma terreum, with thinner flesh and without a smell of meal,
Tricholoma cingulatum.
It occurs only under willows.

kapelusz: Diameter 6–12 cm, shape at first hemispherical, later convex, even flat.
Mature specimens sometimes have an indistinct umbo, sometimes they are concave.
In young specimens the margin is inrolled, in older ones straightened, sometimes bent and ribbed.
Surface smooth, moist, slightly sticky and slippery.
It is brown, red-brown or yellowish brown in colour.
Margin slightly paler.
Sometimes darker, orange-brown spots occur on the surface.
spod: Crowded, broad, notched with a small tooth at the stem.
In addition to full-length gills there are also short gills.
At first they are white, in older fruit bodies they darken and have a colour from cream to light brown.
They darken when pressed.
Gill edges of the same colour as the gills.
In older specimens rusty spots appear on the gills.
trzon: Height 3–7 cm, thickness 1–2 cm.
Cylindrical, often bent.
Hard and solid in young specimens, chambered in older ones.
Surface smooth or slightly fibrillose, white, darker towards the base – rusty brown.
At the top of the stem there is no paler zone.
Base overgrown with white mycelium.
miazsz: White, only at the base of the stem and under the cap skin sometimes light brown.
It is compact and fleshy, and does not change colour when damaged.
It has a mealy smell and a bitterish taste.
podobne: Among brown-coloured knights (Tricholoma), there are many similar species, including:
Tricholoma fulvum with yellowish gills,
Tricholoma ustale, with a smooth and shiny cap and rusty gills,
Tricholoma stans, which has a distinct ring zone on the stem under the cap.

kapelusz: Diameter 6–12 cm, reddish-brownish in colour, slippery when wet.
spod: Whitish in colour, then turning slightly brown.
trzon: In young fruit bodies whitish, then brownish (especially at the base).
miazsz: With a mealy smell, mild taste (slightly bitter in old age).
podobne: Tricholoma albobrunneum, growing in coniferous forests.
Poisonous.
Tricholoma pessundatum, growing in coniferous forests.
Poisonous.
Tricholoma ustale, with a distinctly bitter taste.
Inedible.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–10 cm, surface grey, pale grey, dark grey, often with an olive, yellowish or violet tinge and with characteristic blackish, radially embedded fibres.
At first the fruit body is conically convex, later flattened, with rolled-under margins, often with a blunt umbo in the centre, usually with wavy margins.
In humid conditions slightly slippery.
spod: At first white, then greyish, moderately crowded, thin, notched with a tooth.
trzon: Height 5–10 cm, thickness 2 cm.
It is cylindrical, solid, smooth, shiny.
Surface whitish with a yellowish or greyish tint, in old age greenish-yellow in places.
miazsz: White, bluish-grey only under the cap skin.
Does not change colour when pressed.
Taste mild – sweetish and nutty, smell mealy.
podobne: There are several species of Tricholoma with a similar grey-black colouring:
Tricholoma virgatum.
It has a sharply conical cap, without fibrils, and is peppery in taste,
Tricholoma atrosquamosum has blackish scales on the cap,
Tricholoma terreum has a fibrous-scaly cap,
Tricholoma sciodes has a silky shiny cap and an acrid taste.
Because it often has a yellowish tint, it can also be confused with the yellow Tricholoma species: Tricholoma equestre and Tricholoma sejunctum.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–8 cm.
At first bell-shaped or spherically convex, later spread out and often slightly umbonate, colour cream or brown-yellow to ochre.
Surface dry, at first finely granular, later finely fibrillose; the margin remains bent for a long time.
spod: Sparsely spaced.
Whitish in young fruit bodies, later straw yellow, and with age they have rusty brown spots.
trzon: Cylindrical, 4 to 8 (10) cm long and from 0.7 to 1.5 cm thick.
It is pale ochre or a colour similar to the cap, peeling.
The tip of the stem is whitish.
miazsz: The whitish to pale yellow-brownish flesh tastes bitter and has an inconspicuous smell.
podobne: Typical of this Tricholoma is a uniform ochre-brown, finely granular to finely fibrous-scaly cap and almost odourless, slightly bitter flesh.
The usually larger Tricholoma imbricatum occurs under pines.
Its cap, which is also brown, has a dry, embedded, radially fibrous or finely scaling surface.
The stem has a pale tip, without a ring.
Tricholoma vaccinum, which grows under spruces, also shows some similarities.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–10 cm, bell-shaped or hemispherical when young, later flat-arched, but for a long time with an inrolled margin, finally becoming flat and bent with concave hollows.
It is fleshy, smooth and shiny, in dry weather it has a cracked skin, in wet weather it is sticky.
It is characterised by enormous variability of colours between individual specimens.
Most often the cap skin is grey-green, but it can be from white to black-brown.
In dark-coloured specimens the margin is distinctly lighter.
Several varieties that differ markedly in colouring are distinguished.
spod: Widely spaced, slightly thickened, notched with a tooth.
At first they are white, later yellow-grey, when damaged they turn black.
trzon: Height 6–10 cm, thickness 1–2.5 cm.
It is cylindrical or spindle-shaped, pointed at the bottom, usually smooth, bare or scaly, sometimes with ochre spots.
Coloured similarly to the cap, but in a paler shade.
miazsz: Whitish, fleshy, at the base of the stem tinged red.
Turning red some time after picking, with a soapy smell and (sometimes) a bitterish-mealy taste.
podobne: Tricholoma saponaceum is a fungus with a very variable appearance of the fruit bodies and occurs in many varieties, but it always has a soapy smell and turns red (these features often appear only after several hours).
Tricholoma portentosum is similar, for example, but is distinguished by a cap with a grey-brown tinge rather than a greenish one.
It differs from Russula species in its fibrous and non-brittle stem.

kapelusz: Diameter 2.5–8 cm, at first arched, but quickly becomes flatly spread out.
In the centre it has a blunt umbo.
The margin remains inrolled for a long time.
Surface covered radially with fibrils and scales.
Colour at first grey-brown with a faint violet tinge, later becoming paler, cream.
Scales in colour from dark grey-brown to black-brown with a reddish tinge.
Older specimens turn yellow.
spod: Decurrent with a tooth on the stem, broad.
Colour at first white, turning yellow with age.
trzon: Height 3–6 cm, thickness 0.6–1.2 cm, cylindrical with a thickened base, solid.
Surface longitudinally fibrous and silky-shiny, whitish or slightly grey, turning yellow in older specimens.
miazsz: White, turning yellow with age.
Taste and smell faint, mealy.
podobne: A characteristic feature of this species is turning yellow with age, and when various parts of the fruit body are damaged, especially the gills.
This feature makes it possible to distinguish the yellowing Tricholoma from the very similar Tricholoma pardinum, which does not turn yellow.
Tricholoma cingulatum is also similar, but it occurs exclusively under willows and has a ring on the stem.
It can also be confused with Tricholoma terreum.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–8 cm, conical-bell-shaped on young fruit bodies, later arched, finally flat with a blunt bulge.
The margin is sharp, smooth and remains inrolled for a long time.
Surface of young fruit bodies smooth, silky shiny, of older ones fibrous and sometimes delicately scaly.
In moist conditions it is dark grey with a violet tinge and becomes sticky, while in older fruit bodies brown-grey.
spod: Broad.
They are white-grey with a slight pink tint; their edges in young fruit bodies are whitish, later become black and crenate.
trzon: Height 3–8 cm, thickness 0.7–1.8 cm, cylindrical and slightly widening downwards.
Surface smooth, matt, in colour from white to grey with a faint pink tinge.
miazsz: Grey-white with a pinkish tinge.
It has an earthy smell, in taste it is acrid.
podobne: There are several species of Tricholoma with a similar grey-black colouring:
Tricholoma virgatum.
It has a sharply conical cap, without fibrils, and is peppery in taste,
Tricholoma atrosquamosum has blackish scales on the cap.
It is rare,
Tricholoma portentosum has a cap without small scales, a yellowish stem and a mild, nutty taste,
Tricholoma terreum has a fibrous cap and a mild taste.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–8 cm, shape at first semicircular and arched with an inrolled margin, later flat-arched with a straightened margin.
It often has a bulge in the centre.
Surface covered with adhering fibrils.
It is yellowish, green, olive in colour, sometimes with a brown or grey tint.
In wet conditions it is sticky.
The top of the cap is usually darker.
spod: Fairly crowded, broad, notched with a tooth, white with yellowish edges.
trzon: Height 4–9 cm, thickness 1–3 cm.
It is cylindrical, often curved, widened at the base.
Surface covered with adhering fibrils, whitish, sometimes with a yellow or yellow-green tint.
miazsz: Whitish, yellowish only under the skin of the cap.
Does not change colour when pressed.
Taste and smell cucumber-mealy or bitterish.
podobne: Tricholoma equestre.
It has intensely yellow gills and grows mainly on sandy ground under pines,
Tricholoma saponaceum.
Some of its forms are similar to a greenish-yellow Tricholoma, but it is distinguished by reddish flesh and a soapy smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 5–10 cm, at first convex, then becoming almost flat.
Surface smooth, red-brown to grey-brown, sometimes with a pale margin, usually without striation, but sometimes it may be very faintly striate.
spod: Notched at the stem, of medium density, white or cream.
trzon: Height 4–6 cm, thickness 1–3 cm, cylindrical or slightly bulbous at the base.
Surface smooth and whitish at the top, finely fibrous and pale brown lower down.
No ring.
miazsz: White, turning brown when touched.
Taste and smell indistinct, mealy.
podobne: Tricholoma pessundatum is the most similar.
It is distinguished by a stronger aromatic smell and taste, its spores are much narrower and it usually has round, sunken spots near the cap margin.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–8 cm, conically convex in the young fruit body, later flat.
Margin sharp, surface bare, sometimes delicately scaly, slippery in wet weather.
Colour sulphur yellow, olive yellow, and in places red-brown.
Darker in the centre and very delicately covered with purple flakes.
spod: Bright yellow, fairly thick, notched with a small tooth.
They are distant, which is an important feature allowing Tricholoma sulphureum to be distinguished from the similar Tricholoma equestre, which has more crowded gills.
trzon: Height 4–10 cm, thickness up to 2 cm, cylindrical or club-shaped.
It is at first solid, later hollow, sulphur yellow, covered with rusty fibrils.
At the base it is whitish and hairy.
miazsz: Yellow.
Smell unpleasant, like carbide or coal gas.
wysyp: Spores fairly large, egg-shaped, smooth, colourless, measuring 9–12 × 5–7 µm.
podobne: The edible Tricholoma equestre is similar, which has white flesh, more crowded gills and does not give off an unpleasant smell.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–8 cm, conical when young, later spread out, mostly with a small umbo.
In older specimens it is cracked.
Colour pale grey or dark grey, often with a paler margin, with thin flesh.
Skin dry, felty-fibrillose, with a scaly surface.
spod: Brittle, notched, widely spaced, thin, notched with a tooth.
At first white, later ash-grey.
trzon: Height 4–8 cm, thickness up to 1.6 cm, cylindrical, solid, sometimes slightly curved.
White, grey-whitish, bare or with delicate, cobweb-like remains of the veil.
miazsz: White or greyish, not changing colour.
Smell and taste not mealy, mild.
wysyp: Spores egg-shaped, smooth, colourless, 5-8 × 4-5 µm in diameter.
podobne: There are several species of Tricholoma with a similar grey-black colouring:
Tricholoma virgatum.
It has a sharply conical cap, without fibrils, and is peppery in taste,
Tricholoma atrosquamosum has blackish scales on the cap,
Tricholoma portentosum has a cap without small scales, a yellowish stem and a mild, nutty taste,
Tricholoma sciodes has a silky shiny cap and an acrid taste.

kapelusz: Diameter 4–10 cm, at first convex with a small umbo, later spread out and often bent.
The margin remains inrolled for a long time.
Skin smooth, bare, without zoning, colour from orange to red-brown, often with an olive tinge.
When young it is strongly slimy, later it becomes drier.
In old age, or after drying, the fruit bodies turn black.
spod: Crowded and tightly packed, notched, or sinuately adnate.
Whitish in young individuals, then rusty, turning black in older ones.
trzon: Height 5–10 cm, thickness 0.8–1.5 cm, cylindrical, without a ring.
Solid when young, then hollow, lighter than the cap and covered with brown fibres.
miazsz: Whitish, mild or bitter, sometimes turning red when broken and giving off a mealy smell.
podobne: Similar ones with brown colouring are: Tricholoma fulvum, Tricholoma batschii, Tricholoma stans.

The beech knight differs from other brown knights in that it occurs exclusively under beeches, the cap has an orange or olive tinge, and the stem is uniformly coloured (without a pale zone under the cap).

kapelusz: Diameter 3–7 cm, silvery grey to ash-grey, with darker, embedded, radial streaks, with thin flesh, with a characteristically pointed top.
Skin dry, smooth and bare, but also cracking into radially fibrous scales.
spod: Light grey, later darkening, crowded.
Notched with a tooth at the stem and slightly decurrent on the stem.
trzon: Height 6–12 cm, thickness 1–2 cm, cylindrical and slightly widening downwards, sometimes misshapen.
Surface colour from white to grey, sometimes dark spots occur.
Under the cap it is covered with delicate flakes.
miazsz: Whitish, not changing colour.
Smell from neutral to earthy.
Taste bitter and almost immediately burning-acrid.
podobne: There are several Tricholoma species of similar grey colouring, but none of them has such a sharp point on the cap.
This is the feature by which the peppery Tricholoma is most easily distinguished from them.
In addition, other similar knight fungi also differ in somewhat different features:
Tricholoma terreum has a fibrous cap and a mild taste,
Tricholoma atrosquamosa has grey-black scales on the cap.
It is rare,
Tricholoma sciodes has a silkily shiny cap and is also acrid in taste, but only after a longer time.
It is rare,
Tricholoma portentosum has a yellowish stem and gills, mild, nutty taste.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–6 cm, at first arched, later flat with a concave centre.
Surface golden yellow, covered with scales in colour from olive-brown to olive-black.
Most scales are in the centre of the cap.
spod: Moderately crowded, 3–8 mm wide, notched with a tooth at the stem.
They are intensely yellow, with evenly frosted edges.
trzon: Height 5–8 cm, thickness 0.7–1.2 cm.
It is cylindrical, usually curved, at first solid, with time hollow inside.
Surface scaly or fibrous, yellow, whitish only in the uppermost part under the gills in young fruit bodies.
miazsz: Thin, springy, yellow.
It does not change colour after damage.
Taste slightly bitter, smell mild and weak.
In reaction with KOH it changes colour to pink or red.
wysyp: Spores elliptical, smooth, non-amyloid, measuring 6–7.5 × 4.5–5 μm.
Pleurocystidia rare and barely projecting above the basidia, cheilocystidia numerous.
podobne: Tricholomopsis ornata, which has red-brown or reddish scales.
Tricholomopsis rutilans is larger, has reddish tones on the cap and red-violet scales.

kapelusz: Diameter 3–15 cm, semicircular in young specimens, arched with a rolled-under margin, spread out in older ones, sometimes with a blunt umbo.
Skin delicately felty, the yellow background is covered with lilac-red scales.
This species has a very variable cap colour; in young specimens the cap may be entirely purple-violet, and in older ones uniformly yellow.
A record specimen was found in Italy on a cork oak trunk – its cap had a diameter of 56 cm.
spod: Fairly crowded, notched with a tooth at the stem or broadly attached, and slightly flaky.
They are always yellowish in colour, but in younger specimens paler, darkening with age.
trzon: Height 5–12 cm, thickness 1–3 cm.
It is cylindrical, the colour of the cap, sometimes only yellow, set off whitish or yellowish right at the cap, soon becoming hollow.
miazsz: Yellow.
Smell and taste somewhat bland.
wysyp: Spores smooth, elliptical, measuring 6.5–8 × 4.5–5.5 μm, without a germ pore.

kapelusz: Diameter 8–25 mm, at first hemispherical, then weakly convex, sometimes with a slight depression in the centre.
Margin at first curved under, then straight, finally slightly raised, indistinctly striate, sometimes with hanging flocks.
It is hygrophanous.
When moist bright cinnamon-brown, when dry ochre or grey-ochre.
Surface at first delicately felty, then scaly.
spod: Adnate and slightly decurrent, broad, distant, light cinnamon-brown.
trzon: Height 2–3.5 cm, thickness 1.5–3 mm, cylindrical, sometimes thickened at the base.
Surface bare with a few small scales, with white hyphae of mycelium at the base.
miazsz: Very thin, elastic, whitish-ochre-brown, fleshy in the cap, fibrous in the stem.
It does not change colour after damage.
Taste mild, smell mushroomy, faint.

kapelusz: Diameter 1–4 cm, at first convex, but quickly becoming spread out, sometimes with a blunt umbo.
In young fruit bodies there are fibres at the margins that are remains of the veil.

It is hygrophanous; when wet the surface is in colour from yellow-brown to red-brown and the cap from the margins to half its diameter is translucently striate, when dry it is in colour from brown-ochre to pale ochre and is not striate.
In older specimens the margin of the cap is bent outwards.
spod: Broad and broadly decurrent, in colour from light ochre to red-brown.
trzon: Height 2–4 cm, thickness approx. 0.4 cm, cylindrical.
Surface pale ochre-brown with remnants of the veil in the form of whitish scales.
In young fruit bodies there is a fibrillose annular zone, which however quickly disappears.
miazsz: Thin and the same colour as the cap.
It has an indistinct taste and a faint mushroomy or radish smell.
wysyp: Spores oval or ellipsoid, smooth, measuring 7–8 × 4.5–5 μm.

owocnik: The young fruit body is spherical or egg-shaped, and develops underground (hypogeically).
During ripening a stem develops that pushes up above the ground, and at its top a spherical head up to 1.3 cm in diameter forms.
The outer covering (exoperidium) is membranous, whitish and falls off quickly.
Only on the lower part of the head are its remains often preserved in the form of hanging fringes.
Inner covering (endoperidium) stiff, parchment-like, smooth, whitish, with age ochre-white with rusty spots.
It opens at the top with a short tubular, slightly protruding mouth.
The zone around the mouth is darker in colour.
Stem 1.5 to 7 cm long and up to 0.4 cm thick, fawn-reddish, at first fibrous, then bare.
Covered with delicate small scales more or less adpressed to the stem, smooth with age.
Gleba light brown.
podobne: The winter stalked puffball (Tulostoma brumale) can be confused with the inedible Tulostoma fimbriatum, in which the mouth is ragged.

kapelusz: Diameter generally up to 12 cm, in young specimens semicircular, then convex, to spread out in older ones.
Surface at first mossy, suede-like, then smooth.
Colour from light brown to flesh brown.
spod: Long, with pores extending beyond the margin of the cap.
In young specimens they are white, later pale pink, when damaged they take on a dirty wine colour.
They can easily be separated from the flesh.
trzon: Thickness 2–4 cm, height up to 14 cm.
Solid, barrel-shaped in young specimens, club-shaped in older ones, paler than the cap, covered with a distinct, brownish reticulum (net) with wide meshes.
miazsz: White, elastic, does not change colour after damage.
Hard when young, spongy in older specimens.
It has a pleasant smell, but is very bitter.
wysyp: Spores spindle-shaped or ellipsoid, measuring 10–15 × 4–6 μm.
podobne: Quite often young specimens are confused with Boletus edulis or Leccinum scabrum.
A simple way to tell these species apart is to touch a broken piece of the cap with the tongue.
The taste of bile leaves no doubt that this is the bitter bolete (Tylopilus felleus).
Older specimens of the bitter bolete can be distinguished even more easily by the pinkish pores.

owocnik: A single fruit body is several cm in diameter, often neighbouring fruit bodies fuse together.
It is leaf-like lobed in shape, the surface is folded, resembling the convolutions of the brain.
Flesh gelatinous, surface the colour of burnt sugar (caramel), brown or red-brown.
podobne: Tremella foliacea.
It occurs only on deciduous trees and has more flattened, leaf-like fruit bodies.

owocnik: Made up of a head and a small stalk.
It reaches a height of up to 10–20 cm.
2–5 cm high, 2–4 cm in diameter and conical to bell-shaped, attached only at the top, the whole rest is free.
Surface ribbed; between low, thin, vertical, wavy ribs, sometimes connected crosswise, there are alveoli.
Colour from yellow-brown to dark brown.
trzon: Height 7–20 cm, thickness 1–2.5 cm, cylindrical, sometimes flattened and bent over, at first cottony, then hollow, brittle.
Surface at first whitish with whitish tufts, then bare, cream-yellowish with ochre-orange spots.
miazsz: Thin, waxy, white.
Taste mild, smell mushroomy.
